G1: alpha; the first letter of the Greek alphabet.
Of Hebrew origin; the first letter of the alphabet; figuratively, only (from its use as a numeral) the first.
Alpha. Often used (usually an, before a vowel) also in composition (as a contraction from aneu) in the sense of privation; so, in many words, beginning with this letter; occasionally in the sense of…
G10: Abiud, son of Zerubbabel and father of Eliakim.
Of Hebrew origin ('Abiyhuwd); Abihud, an Israelite.
G1000: a casting, throw; in acc: as measure of distance.
From ballo; a throw (as a measure of distance).
G1001: to cast the line (for sounding), to sound.
From bolis; to heave the lead.
G1002: From ballo; a missile, i.e. Javelin.
G1003: Boaz, son of Salmon and Rahab, husband of Ruth, father of Obed.
Of Hebrew origin (Bo'az); Booz, (i.e. Boaz), an Israelite.
G1005: the north wind, hence: the North.
Of uncertain derivation; the north (properly, wind).
G1006: A prolonged form of a primary verb (compare bibrosko, bous); to pasture; by extension to, fodder; reflexively, to graze.
G1007: Of Hebrew origin (b'owr); Bosor (i.e. Beor), a Moabite.
G1008: From bosko; herbage (as if for grazing).
G1009: Of uncertain derivation; a bunch (of grapes).
G101: to be impossible; to be unable.
From adunatos; to be unable, i.e. (passively) impossible.
G1010: a member of a city council, in NT of the Sanhedrin at Jerusalem.
From bouleuo; an adviser, i.e. (specially) a councillor or member of the Jewish Sanhedrin.
G1011: From boule; to advise, i.e. (reflexively) deliberate, or (by implication) resolve.
consult, take counsel, determine, be minded, purpose.
G1012: From boulomai; volition, i.e. (objectively) advice, or (by implication) purpose.
G1014: Middle voice of a primary verb; to "will," i.e. (reflexively) be willing.
be disposed, minded, intend, list, (be, of own) will (-ing). Compare ethelo.
G1015: Probably of foreign origin; a hillock.
G1016: Probably from the base of bosko; an ox (as grazing), i.e. An animal of that species ("beef").
G1017: From brabeus (an umpire of uncertain derivation); an award (of arbitration), i.e. (specially) a prize in the public games.
G1018: (lit: to act as arbiter in the games), to rule, arbitrate.
From the same as brabeion; to arbitrate, i.e. (genitive case) to govern (figuratively, prevail).
G1019: to be slow, to delay, tarry.
G102: of persons: incapable; of things: impossible; either the inability, or that which is impossible.
From a (as a negative particle) and dunatos; unable, i.e. Weak (literally or figuratively); passively, impossible.
could not do, impossible, impotent, not possible, weak.
G1020: From bradus and a prolonged form of pleo; to sail slowly.
G1021: Of uncertain affinity; slow; figuratively, dull.
G1023: Properly, comparative of brachus, but apparently in the sense of brasso (to wield); the arm, i.e. (figuratively) strength.
G1024: Of uncertain affinity; short (of time, place, quantity, or number).
G1025: an unborn or a newborn child.
Of uncertain affinity; an infant (properly, unborn) literally or figuratively.
G1026: A primary verb; to moisten (especially by a shower).
G1029: a noose or snare; a cord.
G1030: a biting, a gnashing of teeth.
From brucho; a grating (of the teeth).
G1031: to grind or gnash, as with the teeth for rage or pain.
A primary verb; to grate the teeth (in pain or rage).
G1032: to be full to bursting, to gush with.
A primary verb; to swell out, i.e. (by implication) to gush.
G1033: From the base of bibrosko; food (literally or figuratively), especially (ceremonially) articles allowed or forbidden by the Jewish law.
G1035: (a) abstr: eating, (b) food, a meal, (c) rust.
From the base of bibrosko; (abstractly) eating (literally or figuratively); by extension (concretely) food (literally or figuratively).
G1036: to cause to sink; mid: to sink, submerge, drown.
From buthos; to sink; by implication, to drown.
G1037: A variation of bathos; depth, i.e. (by implication) the sea.
G1039: From bussos; made of linen (neuter a linen cloth).
G104: always, unceasingly, perpetually; on every occasion.
From an obsolete primary noun (apparently meaning continued duration); "ever,"by qualification regularly; by implication, earnestly.
G1040: byssus (a species of flax), also (the) linen (made from it).
G1041: an altar, platform; a slightly-elevated spot.
From the base of basis; properly, a stand, i.e. (specially) an altar.
G1042: Gabbatha, a sort of paved square, on which the procurator had his judgment seat.
Of Chaldee origin (compare gab); the knoll; gabbatha, a vernacular term for the Roman tribunal in Jerusalem.
G1043: the angel Gabriel, a messenger of God.
Of Hebrew origin (Gabriy'el); Gabriel, an archangel.
G1045: Gad, one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
Of Hebrew origin (Gad); Gad, a tribe of Israelites.
G1046: Gadarene, belonging to Gadara (an important Hellenized town, one of the Decapolis, and south-east of the Sea of Galilee).
From Gadara (a town east of the Jordan); a Gadarene or inhabitant of Gadara.
G1048: Gaza, an old town in the south of Palestine, on the sea-coast.
Of Hebrew origin (Azzah); Gazah (i.e. Azzah), a place in Palestine.
G1049: From gaza and phulake; a treasure-house, i.e. A court in the temple for the collection-boxes.
G105: From the same as aer; an eagle (from its wind-like flight).
G1050: Gaius, (a) a Corinthian, (b) a Macedonian, (c) a citizen of Derbe, (d) an Ephesian.
Of Latin origin; Gaius (i.e. Caius), a Christian.
G1052: a Galatian (meaning any inhabitant of the Roman province Galatia).
From Galatia; a Galatian or inhabitant of Galatia.
G1053: Galatia, a large Roman province in central Asia Minor, comprising the districts of Paphlagonia, Pontus Galaticus, Galatia (in the narrower sense, which some still think is intended in the NT), Phrygia Galatica, Lycaonia…
Of foreign origin; Galatia, a region of Asia.
G1054: Galatic, belonging to the province Galatia.
From Galatia; Galatic or relating to Galatia.
G1056: Galilee, a district towards the southern end of the Roman province Syria; the northern division of Palestine.
Of Hebrew origin (Galiyl); Galiloea (i.e. The heathen circle), a region of Palestine.
G1057: a Galilean, an inhabitant of Galilee.
From Galilaia; Galilean or belonging to Galilea.
G1058: Gallio, Lucius Iunius Gallio, who received this name by adoption into another family, but was born brother of the philosopher Seneca and originally named L. Annaeus Nouatus; proconsul of the Roman province Achaia from…
Of Latin origin; Gallion (i.e. Gallio), a Roman officer.
G1059: Gamaliel, a noted Pharisee, teacher of Saul.
Of Hebrew origin (Gamliy'el); Gamaliel (i.e. Gamliel), an Israelite.
G106: unleavened, the paschal feast (a feast of the Hebrews); fig: uncorrupted, sincere.
From a (as a negative particle) and zume; unleavened, i.e. (figuratively) uncorrupted; (in the neutral plural) specially (by implication) the Passover week.
G1060: to marry, used of either sex.
From gamos; to wed (of either sex).
G1061: From gamos; to espouse (a daughter to a husband).
G1062: a marriage, wedding, wedding-ceremony; plur: a wedding-feast.
G1063: for, indeed (a conjunction used to express cause, explanation, inference or continuation).
A primary particle; properly, assigning a reason (used in argument, explanation or intensification; often with other particles).
and, as, because (that), but, even, for, indeed, no doubt, seeing, then, therefore, verily, what, why, yet.
G1064: the womb, stomach; of a woman: to be with child (lit: to have [a child] in the belly).
Of uncertain derivation; the stomach; by analogy, the matrix; figuratively, a gourmand.
G1065: an enclitic, emphasizing particle: at least, indeed, really, but generally too subtle to be represented in English.
A primary particle of emphasis or qualification (often used with other particles prefixed).
and besides, doubtless, at least, yet.
G1066: Gideon, one of the Judges of Israel.
Of Hebrew origin (Gid'own); Gedeon (i.e. Gid(e)on), an Israelite.
G1067: Gehenna, and originally the name of a valley or cavity near Jerusalem, a place underneath the earth, a place of punishment for evil.
Of Hebrew origin (gay' and Hinnom); valley of (the son of) Hinnom; ge-henna (or Ge-Hinnom), a valley of Jerusalem, used (figuratively) as a name for the place (or state) of everlasting punishment.
G1068: Gethsemane, a small place between the brook Kidron and the Mount of Olives near Jerusalem.
Of Chaldee origin (compare gath and shemen); oil-press; Gethsemane, a garden near Jerusalem.
G1069: From ge; a neighbour (as adjoining one's ground); by implication, a friend.
G107: Azor, son of Eliakim and father of Zadok, an ancestor of Jesus.
Of Hebrew origin (compare Azzuwr); Azor, an Israelite.
G1070: Of uncertain affinity; to laugh (as a sign of joy or satisfaction).
G1071: From gelao; laughter (as a mark of gratification).
G1072: Transitive from gemo; to fill entirely.
G1073: A primary verb; to swell out, i.e. Be full.
G1074: a generation; if repeated twice or with another time word, practically indicates infinity of time.
From (a presumed derivative of) genos; a generation; by implication, an age (the period or the persons).
G1075: to put into a genealogy, reckon descent.
From genea and logos; to reckon by generations, i.e. Trace in genealogy.
G1076: the making of a pedigree, a genealogy.
From the same as genealogeo; tracing by generations, i.e. "genealogy".
G1077: Neuter plural of a derivative of genesis; birthday ceremonies.
G1078: From the same as genea; nativity; figuratively, nature.
G1079: Feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of genea; birth.
G108: Azotus, Ashdod, a coast town of Palestine belonging to the ancient Philistia, and part of Herod's kingdom.
Of Hebrew origin ('Ashdowd); Azotus (i.e. Ashdod), a place in Palestine.
G1080: to beget (of the male), (of the female) to bring forth, give birth to.
From a variation of genos; to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother); figuratively, to regenerate.
bear, beget, be born, bring forth, conceive, be delivered of, gender, make, spring.
G1081: From gennao; offspring; by analogy, produce (literally or figuratively).
G1082: Gennesaret, a fertile district by the lake of Tiberias, which was in consequence sometimes called the Lake of Gennesaret.
Of Hebrew origin (compare Kinnrowth); Gennesaret (i.e. Kinnereth), a lake and plain in Palestine.
G1085: From ginomai; "kin" (abstract or concrete, literal or figurative, individual or collective).
born, country(-man), diversity, generation, kind(-red), nation, offspring, stock.
G1086: Gerasene, of Gerasa, a city East of the Jordan.
Of Hebrew origin (Girgashiy); a Gergesene (i.e. Girgashite) or one of the aborigines of Palestine.
G1087: the assembly or body of elders.
From geron; the eldership, i.e. (collectively) the Jewish Sanhedrin.
G1089: A primary verb; to taste; by implication, to eat; figuratively, to experience (good or ill).
G109: air, the lower air we breathe.
From aemi (to breathe unconsciously, i.e. Respire; by analogy, to blow); "air" (as naturally circumambient).
G1090: to work the soil, cultivate the earth.
G1091: Neuter of a (presumed) derivative of georgos; cultivable, i.e. A farm.
G1092: a worker of the soil, husbandman, farmer, farm-laborer, vine-dresser.
From ge and the base of ergon; a land-worker, i.e. Farmer.
G1093: the earth, soil, land, region, country, inhabitants of a region.
Contracted from a primary word; soil; by extension a region, or the solid part or the whole of the terrene globe (including the occupants in each application).
G1096: to come into being, be born, become, come about, happen.
A prolongation and middle voice form of a primary verb; to cause to be ("gen"-erate), i.e. (reflexively) to become (come into being), used with great latitude (literal, figurative, intensive, etc.).
arise, be assembled, be(-come, -fall, -have self), be brought (to pass), (be) come (to pass), continue, be divided, draw, be ended, fall, be finished, follow, be found, be fulfilled, + God forbid,…
G1097: to be taking in knowledge, come to know, learn; aor: to ascertained, realized.
A prolonged form of a primary verb; to "know" (absolutely) in a great variety of applications and with many implications (as follow, with others not thus clearly expressed).
allow, be aware (of), feel, (have) know(-ledge), perceived, be resolved, can speak, be sure, understand.
G1098: the unfermented juice of grapes; hence: sweet new wine.
Akin to glukus; sweet wine, i.e. (properly) must (fresh juice), but used of the more saccharine (and therefore highly inebriating) fermented wine.
G1099: Of uncertain affinity; sweet (i.e. Not bitter nor salt).
G11: Abraham, progenitor of the Hebrew race.
Of Hebrew origin ('Abraham); Abraham, the Hebrew patriarch.
Abraham. (In Acts 7:16 the text should probably read Jacob.)
G110: From a compound of a (as a negative particle) and thanatos; deathlessness.
G1100: the tongue, a language, a nation (usually distinguished by their speech).
Of uncertain affinity; the tongue; by implication, a language (specially, one naturally unacquired).
G1101: (a vernacular word), bag, purse; some prefer to take as: box, chest.
From glossa and the base of kosmos; properly, a case (to keep mouthpieces of wind-instruments in) i.e. (by extension) a casket or (specially) purse.
G1102: By variation for a derivative from knapto (to tease cloth); a cloth-dresser.
G1103: (lit: born in wedlock), hence: real, true, genuine; with definite article: the true, genuine element.
From the same as genesia; legitimate (of birth), i.e. Genuine.
G1104: Adverb from gnesios; genuinely, i.e. Really.
G1105: Akin to nephos; gloom (as of a storm).
G1106: From ginosko; cognition, i.e. (subjectively) opinion, or (objectively) resolve (counsel, consent, etc.).
advice, + agree, judgment, mind, purpose, will.
G1107: to make known, declare, know, discover.
From a derivative of ginosko; to make known; subjectively, to know.
certify, declare, make known, give to understand, do to wit, wot.
G1108: From ginosko; knowing (the act), i.e. (by implication) knowledge.
G111: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of themis (statute; from the base of tithemi); illegal; by implication, flagitious.
G1111: to whisper, murmur, grumble (generally of smoldering discontent).
G1114: a conjuror, juggler, sorcerer; a tricky (crafty) deceiver, imposter.
From goao (to wail); properly, a wizard (as muttering spells), i.e. (by implication) an imposter.
G1115: Golgotha, a knoll outside the wall of Jerusalem.
Of Chaldee origin (compare gulgoleth); the skull; Golgotha, a knoll near Jerusalem.
G1116: Gomorrah, one of the destroyed cities on the Dead Sea.
Of Hebrew origin (Amorah); Gomorrha (i.e. Amorah), a place near the Dead Sea.
G1117: From gemo; a load (as filling), i.e. (specially) a cargo, or (by extension) wares.
G1118: From the base of ginomai; a parent.
G112: without god, without (the only true) God, godless.
From a (as a negative particle) and theos; godless.
G1120: to fall on knees before (in supplication), supplicate, entreat.
From a compound of gonu and the alternate of pipto; to fall on the knee.
G1121: a letter of the alphabet; collectively: written (revelation); (a) a written document, a letter, an epistle, (b) writings, literature, learning.
From grapho; a writing, i.e. A letter, note, epistle, book, etc.; plural learning.
bill, learning, letter, scripture, writing, written.
G1122: (a) in Jerusalem, a scribe, one learned in the Jewish Law, a religious teacher, (b) at Ephesus, the town-clerk, the secretary of the city, (c) a man of learning generally.
From gramma. A writer, i.e. (professionally) scribe or secretary.
G1124: (a) a writing, (b) a passage of scripture; plur: the scriptures.
A document, i.e. Holy Writ (or its contents or a statement in it).
G1125: to write; pass: it is written, it stands written (in the scriptures).
A primary verb; to "grave", especially to write; figuratively, to describe.
G1126: belonging to old women, such as old women tell.
From graus (an old woman) and eidos; crone-like, i.e. Silly.
G1127: (a) to be awake (in the night), watch, (b) to be watchful, on the alert, vigilant.
From egeiro; to keep awake, i.e. Watch (literally or figuratively).
G1128: to train by physical exercise; hence: train, in the widest sense.
From gumnos; to practise naked (in the games), i.e. Train (figuratively).
G113: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of tithemi (in the sense of enacting); lawless, i.e. (by implication) criminal.
G1130: to be poorly clad; to be habitually wearing an under-garment only.
From a derivative of gumnos; to strip, i.e. (reflexively) go poorly clad.
G1131: rarely: stark-naked; generally: wearing only the under-garment; bare, open, manifest; mere.
Of uncertain affinity; nude (absolute or relative, literal or figurative).
G1133: a woman, with all a woman's weakness, a poor weak woman, a silly woman.
A diminutive from gune; a little (i.e. Foolish) woman.
G1134: belonging to woman, of woman, female.
G1135: Probably from the base of ginomai; a woman; specially, a wife.
G1136: Gog, in Ezekiel a king of Magog, a land of the remote north; hence, in Revelation, of a people far remote from Palestine.
Of Hebrew origin (Gowg); Gog, a symbolic name for some future Antichrist.
G1137: a corner; met: a secret place.
Probably akin to gonu; an angle.
G1138: Of Hebrew origin (David); Dabid (i.e. David), the Israelite king.
G1139: to be possessed, be under the power of an evil-spirit or demon.
Middle voice from daimon; to be exercised by a dæmon.
have a (be vexed with, be possessed with) devil(-s).
G114: to annul, make of no effect, set aside, ignore, slight; to break faith with.
From a compound of a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of tithemi; to set aside, i.e. (by implication) to disesteem, neutralize or violate.
cast off, despise, disannul, frustrate, bring to nought, reject.
G1140: an evil-spirit, demon; a heathen deity.
Neuter of a derivative of daimon; a dæmonic being; by extension a deity.
G1142: From daio (to distribute fortunes); a dæmon or supernatural spirit (of a bad nature).
G1143: to bite; hence: to backbite, harm seriously.
A prolonged form of a primary root; to bite, i.e. (figuratively) thwart.
G1144: Or dakruon dak'-roo-on; of uncertain affinity; a tear.
G1148: Dalmanutha, an unidentified place near the Sea of Galilee.
Probably of Chaldee origin; Dalmanutha, a place in Palestine.
G1149: Dalmatia, a province of the Roman Empire, east of the Adriatic, a later name for part of what was earlier called Illyricum.
Probably of foreign derivation; Dalmatia, a region of Europe.
G1150: to tame, subdue, involving obedience and restraint.
A variation of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; to tame.
G1151: Probably from the base of damazo; a heifer (as tame).
G1152: Probably from the base of damazo; perhaps gentle; Damaris, an Athenian woman.
G1153: a Damascene, an inhabitant of Damascus.
From Damaskos; a Damascene or inhabitant of Damascus.
G1154: Of Hebrew origin (Dammeseq); Damascus, a city of Syria.
G1155: From daneion; to loan on interest; reflexively, to borrow.
G1156: From danos (a gift); probably akin to the base of didomi; a loan.
G1158: Of Hebrew origin (Daniye'l); Daniel, an Israelite.
G1159: to spend, bear expense, waste, squander.
From dapane; to expend, i.e. (in a good sense) to incur cost, or (in a bad one) to waste.
G116: Athens, the intellectual capital of Greece.
Plural of Athene (the goddess of wisdom, who was reputed to have founded the city); Athenoe, the capitol of Greece.
G1161: a weak adversative particle, generally placed second in its clause; but, on the other hand, and.
A primary particle (adversative or continuative); but, and, etc..
also, and, but, moreover, now (often unexpressed in English).
G1163: it is necessary, inevitable; less frequently: it is a duty, what is proper.
3d person singular active present of deo; also deon deh-on'; neuter active participle of the same; both used impersonally; it is (was, etc.) Necessary (as binding).
behoved, be meet, must (needs), (be) need(-ful), ought, should.
G1164: an example, type; a thing shown.
From the base of deiknuo; a specimen (as shown).
G1165: to hold up as an example, make a show of, expose.
G1166: to point out, show, exhibit; met: to teach, demonstrate, make known.
A prolonged form of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; to show (literally or figuratively).
G1168: to shrink, be fearful, timid, cowardly.
G1169: From deos (dread); timid, i.e. (by implication) faithless.
G117: From Athenai; an Athenoean or inhabitant of Athenae.
G1170: so and so, such a one, where the name of the person is known but not used.
Probably from the same as deinos (through the idea of forgetting the name as fearful, i.e. Strange); so and so (when the person is not specified).
G1171: Adverb from a derivative of the same as deilos; terribly, i.e. Excessively.
G1172: From deipnon; to dine, i.e. Take the principle (or evening) meal.
G1173: a dinner, an afternoon or evening meal.
From the same as dapane; dinner, i.e. The chief meal (usually in the evening).
G1174: respectful of what is divine; religious, perhaps, rather than superstitious (the usual meaning).
The compound of a derivative of the base of deilos and daimon; more religious than others.
G1175: religion in general; in a bad sense: superstition.
From the same as deisidaimonesteros; religion.
G1177: From deka and duo; two and ten, i.e. Twelve.
G1178: From deka and pente; ten and five, i.e. Fifteen.
G1179: Decapolis, meaning a group or district of ten cities (of the Greek type) in Palestine, mostly south-east of the Lake of Tiberias; the names and number vary in ancient authorities.
From deka and polis; the ten-city region; the Decapolis, a district in Syria.
G118: to engage, compete, in an (athletic) contest.
From athlos (a contest in the public lists); to contend in the competitive games.
G1180: From deka and tessares; ten and four, i.e. Fourteen.
G1181: Feminine of dekatos; a tenth, i.e. As a percentage or (technically) tithe.
G1183: From dekate; to tithe, i.e. To give or take a tenth.
G1185: From the base of dolos; to entrap, i.e. (figuratively) delude.
G1186: Probably from drus (an oak); a tree.
G1187: one posted on the right hand, a spear-man.
From dexios and lambano; a guardsman (as if taking the right) or light-armed soldier.
G1188: on the right hand, right hand, right.
From dechomai; the right side or (feminine) hand (as that which usually takes).
G1189: to want for myself; to want, need; to beg, request, beseech, pray.
Middle voice of deo; to beg (as binding oneself), i.e. Petition.
beseech, pray (to), make request. Compare punthanomai.
G119: a struggling (as in an athletic contest).
G1190: From Derbe; a Derbæan or inhabitant of Derbe.
G1191: Derbe, a town in Lycaonia and in the southern part of the Roman province Galatia.
Of foreign origin; Derbe, a place in Asia Minor.
G1192: the skin or hide of an animal.
G1194: A primary verb; properly, to flay, i.e. (by implication) to scourge, or (by analogy) to thrash.
G1195: to bind, put in chains, tie together.
From a (presumed) derivative of desmeo; to be a binder (captor), i.e. To enchain (a prisoner), to tie on (a load).
G1196: From desmon; to tie, i.e. Shackle.
G1199: a bond, chain, imprisonment; a string or ligament, an impediment, infirmity.
Or desmos des-mos' neuter and masculine respectively from deo; a band, i.e. Ligament (of the body) or shackle (of a prisoner); figuratively, an impediment or disability.
G12: the abyss, unfathomable depth, an especially Jewish conception, the home of the dead and of evil spirits.
From a (as a negative particle) and a variation of buthos; depthless, i.e. (specially) (infernal) "abyss".
G120: to lose heart, be despondent, be disheartened.
From a compound of a (as a negative particle) and thumos; to be spiritless, i.e. Disheartened.
G1200: a keeper of a prison, a jailer.
From desmon and phulax; a jailer (as guarding the prisoners).
G1201: From a derivative of desmon (equivalent to desmeo); a place of bondage, i.e. A dungeon.
G1202: From the same as desmoterion; (passively) a captive.
G1203: Perhaps from deo and posis (a husband); an absolute ruler ("despot").
G1204: (originally: hither, hence) (a) exclamatory: come, (b) temporal: now, the present.
Of uncertain affinity; here; used also imperative hither!; and of time, hitherto.
G1205: come hither, come, hither, an exclamatory word.
From deuro and an imperative form of eimi (to go); come hither!.
G1206: adj. where English requires an adv., on the second day, on the next day.
From deuteros; secondary, i.e. (specially) on the second day.
G1207: second-first, a word of uncertain meaning.

From deuteros and protos; second-first, i.e. (specially) a designation of the Sabbath immediately after the Paschal week (being the second after Passover day, and the first of the seven Sabbaths intervening before Pentecost).
G1208: second; with the article: in the second place, for the second time.
As the compare of duo; (ordinal) second (in time, place, or rank; also adverb).
G1209: Middle voice of a primary verb; to receive (in various applications, literally or figuratively).
G121: From a (as a negative particle) and probably a derivative of tithemi (meaning a penalty); not guilty.
G1210: to bind, tie, fasten; to impel, compel; to declare to be prohibited and unlawful.
A primary verb; to bind (in various applications, literally or figuratively).
bind, be in bonds, knit, tie, wind. See also dei, deomai.
G1211: (a) in a clause expressing demand: so, then, (b) indeed, (c) truly.
Probably akin to de; a particle of emphasis or explicitness; now, then, etc..
G1213: From delos; to make plain (by words).
G1214: Demas, a helper of Paul in Rome.
Probably for Demetrios; Demas, a Christian.

G1817: (a) in trans. tenses: to raise up, cause to grow, (b) in intrans. tenses: to rise up from.
From ek and anistemi; objectively, to produce, i.e. (figuratively) beget; subjectively, to arise, i.e. (figuratively) object.
G1818: From ek and apatao; to seduce wholly.
G1819: From ek and a derivative of the same as aiphnidios; of a sudden, i.e. Unexpectedly.
G182: unsettled, unstable (though these are hardly strong enough equivalents), almost anarchic.
From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of kathistemi; inconstant.
G1820: to be utterly without resource, be in despair.
Middle voice from ek and aporeo; to be utterly at a loss, i.e. Despond.
G1821: to send away, send forth (a person qualified for a task).
From ek and apostello; to send away forth, i.e. (on a mission) to despatch, or (peremptorily) to dismiss.
G1822: (a) to fit up, completely furnish, equip, furnish, supply, (b) to accomplish, finish.
From ek and a derivative of artios; to finish out (time); figuratively, to equip fully (a teacher).
G1823: to flash forth like lightning, gleam, be radiant.
From ek and astrapto; to lighten forth, i.e. (figuratively) to be radiant (of very white garments).
G1824: From ek and the genitive case singular feminine of autos (hora being understood); from that hour, i.e. Instantly.
by and by, immediately, presently, straightway.
G1825: From ek and egeiro; to rouse fully, i.e. (figuratively) to resuscitate (from death), release (from infliction).
G1826: (originally: to shall go out), to go out (away), depart.
From ek and eimi (to go); to issue, i.e. Leave (a place), escape (to the shore).
G1827: From ek and elegcho; to convict fully, i.e. (by implication) to punish.
G1828: (lit: to draw out of the right place, or to draw aside out of the right way), to entice.
From ek and helkuo; to drag forth, i.e. (figuratively) to entice (to sin).
G1829: From a comparative of ek and a presumed erao (to spue); vomit, i.e. Food disgorged.
G183: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of katecho; unrestrainable.
G1830: to search diligently, to examine carefully (minutely).
From ek and ereunao; to explore (figuratively).
G1831: to go or come out of.
From ek and erchomai; to issue (literally or figuratively).
come (forth, out), depart (out of), escape, get out, go (abroad, away, forth, out, thence), proceed (forth), spread abroad.
G1832: Third person singular present indicative of a compound of ek and eimi; so also exon ex-on' neuter present participle of the same (with or without some form of eimi expressed); impersonally, it is right (through the figurative idea of being out in public).
G1833: to examine, question, inquire at, search out.
From ek and etazo (to examine); to test thoroughly (by questions), i.e. Ascertain or interrogate.
G1834: to lead, show the way; met: to unfold, narrate, declare.
From ek and hegeomai; to consider out (aloud), i.e. Rehearse, unfold.
G1835: The tenth multiple of hex; sixty.
G1836: next in order, the next day, the following day, at the period immediately following.
From echo (in the sense of taking hold of, i.e. Adjoining); successive.
G1837: to sound out (forth) (referring either to the clearness or to the loudness of the sound).
Middle voice from ek and echeo; to "echo" forth, i.e. Resound (be generally reported).
G1838: condition, state, habit, use, especially: good condition of body or soul.
From echo; habit, i.e. (by implication) practice.
G1839: (lit: to remove from a standing position), (a) in trans. tenses: to astonish, amaze, (b) in intrans. tenses: to be astonished, amazed; to be out of mind, be mad.
From ek and histemi; to put (stand) out of wits, i.e. Astound, or (reflexively) become astounded, insane.
amaze, be (make) astonished, be beside self (selves), bewitch, wonder.
G184: Hakeldama, a field apparantly located south of the valley of Hinnom.
Of Chaldee origin (meaning field of blood; corresponding to kathairesis and exapatao); Akeldama, a place near Jerusalem.
G1840: to have strength for (a difficult task), be perfectly able.
From ek and ischuo; to have full strength, i.e. Be entirely competent.
G1841: (a) an exit, going out, departure from a place; the exodus, (b) death.
From ek and hodos; an exit, i.e. (figuratively) death.
G1842: to destroy utterly, annihilate, exterminate, root out.
From ek and olothreuo; to extirpate.
G1843: (a) to consent fully, agree out and out, (b) to confess, admit, acknowledge (cf. the early Hellenistic sense of the middle: to acknowledge a debt), (c) to give thanks, praise.
From ek and homologeo; to acknowledge or (by implication, of assent) agree fully.
G1844: to adjure, put to oath; to exorcise.
From ek and horkizo; to exact an oath, i.e. Conjure.
G1845: an exorcist, a caster out of evil spirits by the use of names or spells.
From exorkizo; one that binds by an oath (or spell), i.e. (by implication) an "exorcist" (conjurer).
G1846: (a) to dig out, hence: to open up, (b) to gouge.
From ek and orusso; to dig out, i.e. (by extension) to extract (an eye), remove (roofing).
G1847: to set at naught, ignore, despise.
From ek and a derivative of the neuter of oudeis; to make utterly nothing of, i.e. Despise.
set at nought. See also exoutheneo.
G1848: to set at naught, ignore, despise.
A variation of exoudenoo and meaning the same.
contemptible, despise, least esteemed, set at nought.
G1849: (a) power, authority, weight, especially: moral authority, influence, (b) in a quasi-personal sense, derived from later Judaism, of a spiritual power, and hence of an earthly power.

From exesti (in the sense of ability); privilege, i.e. (subjectively) force, capacity, competency, freedom, or (objectively) mastery (concretely, magistrate, superhuman, potentate, token of control), delegated influence.
authority, jurisdiction, liberty, power, right, strength.
G185: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of kerannumi; unmixed, i.e. (figuratively) innocent.
G1850: to exercise (wield) power (authority), pass: to be ruled, be held under authority.
exercise authority upon, bring under the (have) power of.
G1851: From a compound of ek and echo (meaning to stand out); prominence (figuratively).
G1854: Adverb from ek; out(-side, of doors), literally or figuratively.
G1855: (a) from outside, from without, (b) outside, both as adj. and prep; with article: the outside.
G1856: to drive out, expel, propel, thrust out; to drive out of the sea, drive on shore.
Or exotho ex-o'-tho from ek and otheo (to push); to expel; by implication, to propel.
G1858: to take part in a festival, keep a feast (allegorically).
From heorte; to observe a festival.
G186: From a (as a negative particle) and klino; not leaning, i.e. (figuratively) firm.
G1860: From epaggello; an announcement (for information, assent or pledge; especially a divine assurance of good).
G1861: From epi and the base of aggelos; to announce upon (reflexively), i.e. (by implication) to engage to do something, to assert something respecting oneself.
G1862: From epaggello; a self-committal (by assurance of conferring some good).
G1863: to bring upon; met: to cause to be imputed to.
From epi and ago; to superinduce, i.e. Inflict (an evil), charge (a crime).
G1864: From epi and agonizomai; to struggle for.
G1865: to gather together, pass: to crowd upon (some one), press around.
From epi and athroizo (to assemble); to accumulate.
G1866: From epaineo; praised; Epaenetus, a Christian.
G1867: From epi and aineo; to applaud.
G1868: From epi and the base of aineo; laudation; concretely, a commendable thing.
G1869: From epi and airo; to raise up (literally or figuratively).
G187: to reach maturity, become ripe, be in full vigor.
From the same as akmen; to make a point, i.e. (figuratively) mature.
G1870: to be ashamed, be ashamed of.
From epi and aischunomai; to feel shame for something.
G1871: to beg, be a beggar, ask alms.
From epi and aiteo; to ask for.
G1872: to follow close after, accompany, dog; to imitate, pursue, be studious of.
From epi and akoloutheo; to accompany.
G1873: From epi and akouo; to hearken (favorably) to.
G1874: to listen to, hear, hearken to.
From epi and the base of akroates; to listen (intently) to.
G1875: From epi and an; a particle of indefinite contemporaneousness; whenever, as soon as.
G1876: Neuter of a presumed compound of epi and anagke; (adverbially) on necessity, i.e. Necessarily.
G1877: (a) nautical: to put out (from the shore), (lit: to take up a ship on to the high seas), (b) to go up, possibly: to go up again, return.
From epi and anago; to lead up on, i.e. (technical) to put out (to sea); (intransitively) to return.
G1878: to remind, possibly: to remind again.
From epi and anamimnesko; to remind of.
G1879: to rest upon, rely on, trust in.
Middle voice from epi and anapano; to settle on; literally (remain) or figuratively (rely).
G188: at the present point of time.
Accusative case of a noun ("acme") akin to ake (a point) and meaning the same; adverbially, just now, i.e. Still.
G1880: From epi and anerchomai; to come up on, i.e. Return.
G1881: intrans. tenses: to rise up against.
Middle voice from epi and anistemi; to stand up on, i.e. (figuratively) to attack.
G1882: From a compound of epi and anorthoo; a straightening up again, i.e. (figuratively) rectification (reformation).
G1883: (a) adv: on the top, above, (b) prep: on the top of, above, over, on, above, more than, superior to.
From epi and ano; up above, i.e. Over or on (of place, amount, rank, etc.).
G1884: to aid, relieve, do service, render help, be strong enough for.
From epi and arkeo; to avail for, i.e. Help.
G1885: From a compound of epi and archo (meaning a governor of a district, "eparch"); a special region of government, i.e. A Roman præfecture.
G1886: From epi and an equivalent of aule; a hut over the head, i.e. A dwelling.
G1887: From epi and aurion; occurring on the succeeding day, i.e. (hemera being implied) to-morrow.
G1888: From epi and autos and (the dative case singular of) a derivative of phor (a thief); in theft itself, i.e. (by analogy) in actual crime.
G1889: Epaphras, Epaphroditus, a Colossian Christian, in captivity with Paul in Rome.
Contracted from Epaphroditos; Epaphras, a Christian.
G189: hearing, faculty of hearing, ear; report, rumor.
From akouo; hearing (the act, the sense or the thing heard).
audience, ear, fame, which ye heard, hearing, preached, report, rumor.
G1890: to foam out (a metaphor from the seaweed and refuse borne on the crest of waves), vomit forth.
From epi and aphrizo; to foam upon, i.e. (figuratively) to exhibit (a vile passion).
G1891: Epaphras, Epaphroditus, a Colossian Christian, in captivity with Paul in Rome.
From epi (in the sense of devoted to) and Aphrodite (Venus); Epaphroditus, a Christian.
G1892: From epi and egeiro; to rouse upon, i.e. (figuratively) to excite against.
G1893: of time: when, after; of cause: since, because; otherwise: else.
From epi and ei; thereupon, i.e. Since (of time or cause).
because, else, for that (then, -asmuch as), otherwise, seeing that, since, when.
G1894: of time: when, now, after that; of cause: seeing that, forasmuch as.
From epei and de; since now, i.e. (of time) when, or (of cause) whereas.
after that, because, for (that, -asmuch as), seeing, since.
G1895: From epeide and per; since indeed (of cause).
G1896: And other moods and persons of the same tense; from epi and eido; to regard (favorably or otherwise).
G1897: From epei and per; since indeed (of cause).
G1898: bringing in (besides or in addition), introduction, importation.
From a compound of epi and eisago; a superintroduction.
G19: intrinsic goodness, especially as a personal quality, with stress on the kindly (rather than the righteous) side of goodness.
From agathos; goodness, i.e. Virtue or beneficence.
G190: From a (as a particle of union) and keleuthos (a road); properly, to be in the same way with, i.e. To accompany (specially, as a disciple).
G1900: From epi and (the accusative case plural neuter of) ekeinos; upon those parts of, i.e. On the further side of.
G1901: to extend, mid. to stretch forward.
Middle voice from epi and ekteino; to stretch (oneself) forward upon.
G1902: to have on over (as a garment); mid: to put on myself in addition.
Middle voice from epi and enduo; to invest upon oneself.
G1903: a coat, outer wrap or tunic.
From ependuomai; a wrapper, i.e. Outer garment.
G1904: to come to, arrive, come on, come upon, attack.
From epi and erchomai; to supervene, i.e. Arrive, occur, impend, attack, (figuratively) influence.
G1905: From epi and erotao; to ask for, i.e. Inquire, seek.
G1906: inquiry, request, appeal, demand; a profession, pledge.
G1907: (a) trans: to hold forth, (b) intrans: to mark, pay attention (heed), note; to delay, stay, wait.
From epi and echo; to hold upon, i.e. (by implication) to retain; (by extension) to detain; (with implication, of nous) to pay attention to.
give (take) heed unto, hold forth, mark, stay.
G1908: to insult, treat wrongfully, molest, revile.
From a comparative of epi and (probably) areia (threats); to insult, slander.
G1909: on, to, against, on the basis of, at.

A primary preposition; properly, meaning superimposition (of time, place, order, etc.), as a relation of distribution (with the genitive case), i.e. Over, upon, etc.; of rest (with the dative case) at, on, etc.; of direction (with the accusative case)…
about (the times), above, after, against, among, as long as (touching), at, beside, X have charge of, (be-, (where-))fore, in (a place, as much as, the time of, -to), (because) of, (up-)on (behalf…
G191: to hear, listen, comprehend by hearing; pass: is heard, reported.
A primary verb; to hear (in various senses).
give (in the) audience (of), come (to the ears), (shall) hear(-er, -ken), be noised, be reported, understand.
G1910: (a) to set foot on, step on, (b) to mount (a horse), board (a vessel).
From epi and the base of basis; to walk upon, i.e. Mount, ascend, embark, arrive.
come (into), enter into, go abroad, sit upon, take ship.
G1911: (a) to throw upon, cast over, (b) to place upon, (c) to lay, (d) intrans: to strike upon, rush.
From epi and ballo; to throw upon (literal or figurative, transitive or reflexive; usually with more or less force); specially (with heautou implied) to reflect; impersonally, to belong to.
beat into, cast (up-)on, fall, lay (on), put (unto), stretch forth, think on.
G1912: to put a burden on, be burdensome.
From epi and bareo; to be heavy upon, i.e. (pecuniarily) to be expensive to; figuratively, to be severe towards.
G1913: From epi and a reduplicated derivative of the base of basis (compare anabibazo); to cause to mount (an animal).
G1914: to look with favor on, regard.
From epi and blepo; to gaze at (with favor, pity or partiality).
look upon, regard, have respect to.
G1915: that which is put on, a patch.
G1916: to cry out to or against.
From epi and boao; to exclaim against.
G1917: From a presumed compound of epi and boulomai; a plan against someone, i.e. A plot.
G1918: to take to wife after, marry a deceased brother's wife.
From epi and a derivative of gamos; to form affinity with, i.e. (specially) in a levirate way.
G1919: (a) on the earth, belonging to the earth (as opposed to the sky), (b) in a spiritual sense, belonging to the earthly sphere, earthly (as opposed to heavenly).
From epi and ge; worldly (physically or morally).
G192: incontinence, intemperance (in wide sense), lack of restraint.
G1920: to arise, spring up, arrive, come on.
From epi and ginomai; to arrive upon, i.e. Spring up (as a wind).
G1921: to come to know by directing attention to him or it, to perceive, discern, recognize; aor: to found out.
From epi and ginosko; to know upon some mark, i.e. Recognize; by implication, to become fully acquainted with, to acknowledge.
G1922: knowledge of a particular point (directed towards a particular object); perception, discernment, recognition, intuition.
From epiginosko; recognition, i.e. (by implication) full discernment, acknowledgement.
G1924: to write upon, inscribe, imprint a mark on.
From epi and grapho; to inscribe (physically or mentally).
G1925: to show, display, point out, indicate; to prove, demonstrate.
From epi and deiknuo; to exhibit (physically or mentally).
G1926: to accept as true, to receive besides.
From epi and dechomai; to admit (as a guest or (figuratively) teacher).
G1927: to sojourn, be resident (temporarily, in a foreign city).
From a compound of epi and demos; to make oneself at home, i.e. (by extension) to reside (in a foreign country).
G1928: to make an additional testamentary disposition, to furnish with additions.
Middle voice from epi and diatasso; to appoint besides, i.e. Supplement (as a codicil).
G1929: (a) trans: to hand in, give up, (b) intrans: to give way (to the wind).
From epi and didomi; to give over (by hand or surrender).
deliver unto, give, let (+ (her drive)), offer.
G193: lacking self-control, powerless, inclined to excess.
From a (as a negative particle) and kratos; powerless, i.e. Without self-control.
G1930: to set in order besides, put in order, correct.
From epi and a derivative of orthos; to straighten further, i.e. (figuratively) arrange additionally.
G1931: to sink, set, set during, go down.
From epi and duno; to set fully (as the sun).
G1932: From epieikes; suitableness, i.e. (by implication) equity, mildness.
G1933: gentle, mild, forbearing, fair, reasonable, moderate.
From epi and eiko; appropriate, i.e. (by implication) mild.
G1934: to seek after, desire, search for, make inquiries about.
From epi and zeteo; to search (inquire) for; intensively, to demand, to crave.
G1935: at the point of death, condemned to death.
From epi and thanatos; doomed to death.
G1936: a laying on; an attack, assault.
From epitithemi; an imposition (of hands officially).
G1937: to long for, covet, lust after, set the heart upon.
From epi and thumos; to set the heart upon, i.e. Long for (rightfully or otherwise).
G1939: desire, eagerness for, inordinate desire, lust.
From epithumeo; a longing (especially for what is forbidden).
G194: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of kerannumi; undiluted.
G1940: to sit upon, cause to sit upon.
From epi and kathizo; to seat upon.
G1941: (a) to call (name) by a supplementary (additional, alternative) name, (b) mid: to call upon, appeal to, address.
Middle voice from epi and kaleo; to entitle; by implication, to invoke (for aid, worship, testimony, decision, etc.).
G1942: From epikalupto; a covering, i.e. (figuratively) pretext.
G1943: to put a cover on, cover up.
From epi and kalupto; to conceal, i.e. (figuratively) forgive.
G1944: on whom a curse has been invoked, accursed, doomed to destruction.
From epi and a derivative of kataraomai; imprecated, i.e. Execrable.
G1945: (a) dat: to be placed upon, be laid upon, lie upon, be imposed; to press upon, (b) absol: to press hard, be insistent, insist.
From epi and keimai; to rest upon (literally or figuratively).
impose, be instant, (be) laid (there-, up-)on, (when) lay (on), lie (on), press upon.
G1946: an Epicurean, one who holds the tenets of Epicurus.
From Epikouros (compare epikouria) (a noted philosopher); an Epicurean or follower of Epicurus.
G1947: From a compound of epi and a (prolonged) form of the base of korasion (in the sense of servant); assistance.
G1948: From epi and krino; to adjudge.
G1949: to lay hold of, take hold of, seize (sometimes with beneficent, sometimes with hostile, intent).
Middle voice from epi and lambano; to seize (for help, injury, attainment, or any other purpose; literally or figuratively).
catch, lay hold (up-)on, take (by, hold of, on).
G195: strictness, accuracy, exactness, attention to detail, scrupulousness.
From the same as akribestatos; exactness.
G1950: Middle voice from epi and lanthano; to lose out of mind; by implication, to neglect.
G1951: to call; mid: to choose for myself; pass: to be named.
Middle voice from epi and lego; to surname, select.
G1952: From epi and leipo; to leave upon, i.e. (figuratively) to be insufficient for.
G1953: From a derivative of epilanthanomai; negligence.
G1954: remaining, that is left over, still left.
From epi and loipoy; left over, i.e. Remaining.
G1956: to loose, release; to solve, settle, explain, interpret, decide.
From epi and luo; to solve further, i.e. (figuratively) to explain, decide.
G1957: to testify earnestly, bear witness to.
From epi and martureo; to attest further, i.e. Corroborate.
G1958: From epimeleomai; carefulness, i.e. Kind attention (hospitality).
G1959: to take care of, attend to.
Middle voice from epi and the same as melo; to care for (physically or otherwise).
G196: Superlative of akribes (a derivative of the same as akron); most exact.
G1960: Adverb from a derivative of epimeleomai; carefully.
G1961: (a) to remain, tarry, (b) to remain in, persist in.
From epi and meno; to stay over, i.e. Remain (figuratively, persevere).
G1962: to nod to, assent to, consent.
From epi and neuo; to nod at, i.e. (by implication) to assent.
G1963: From epi and nous; attention of the mind, i.e. (by implication) purpose.
G1964: to take an oath, swear falsely.
G1965: From epi and horkos; on oath, i.e. (falsely) a forswearer.
G1966: Feminine singular participle of a comparative of epi and heimi (to go); supervening, i.e. (hemera or nux being expressed or implied) the ensuing day or night.
G1967: Perhaps from the same as epiousa; tomorrow's; but more probably from epi and a derivative of the present participle feminine of eimi; for subsistence, i.e. Needful.
G1968: to fall upon, press upon, light upon, come over.
From epi and pipto; to embrace (with affection) or seize (with more or less violence; literally or figuratively).
fall into (on, upon) lie on, press upon.
G1969: to strike at, to rebuke (with words).
From epi and plesso; to chastise, i.e. (with words) to upbraid.
G197: Neuter of the comparative of the same as akribestatos; (adverbially) more exactly.
G1970: From epi and pnigo; to throttle upon, i.e. (figuratively) overgrow.
G1971: to long for, strain after, desire greatly, have affection for.
From epi and potheo (to yearn); to dote upon, i.e. Intensely crave possession (lawfully or wrongfully).
G1973: From epi and a derivative of the latter part of epipotheo; yearned upon, i.e. Greatly loved.
G1975: From epi and poreuomai; to journey further, i.e. Travel on (reach).
G1976: From epi and the base of rhaphis; to stitch upon, i.e. Fasten with the needle.
G1977: From epi and rhipto; to throw upon (literally or figuratively).
G1978: From epi and some form of the base of semaino; remarkable, i.e. (figuratively) eminent.
G1979: From a compound of epi and a derivative of sitos; a provisioning, i.e. (concretely) food.
G198: to learn carefully, inquire with exactness.
From the same as akribestatos; to be exact, i.e. Ascertain.
G1980: to look upon, visit, look out, select.
Middle voice from epi and the base of skopos; to inspect, i.e. (by implication) to select; by extension, to go to see, relieve.
G1981: to raise a tent (over), dwell, spread a tabernacle over.
From epi and skenoo; to tent upon, i.e. (figuratively) abide with.
G1982: From epi and a derivative of skia; to cast a shade upon, i.e. (by analogy) to envelop in a haze of brilliancy; figuratively, to invest with preternatural influence.
G1983: to exercise oversight, care for, visit.
From epi and skopeo; to oversee; by implication, to beware.
G1984: From episkeptomai; inspection (for relief); by implication, superintendence; specially, the Christian "episcopate".
the office of a "bishop", bishoprick, visitation.
G1985: (used as an official title in civil life), overseer, supervisor, ruler, especially used with reference to the supervising function exercised by an elder or presbyter of a church or congregation.
From epi and skopos (in the sense of episkopeo); a superintendent, i.e. Christian officer in genitive case charge of a (or the) church (literally or figuratively).
G1986: (lit: to draw over), mid: to become as uncircumcised.
From epi and spao; to draw over, i.e. (with akrobustia implied) efface the mark of circumcision (by recovering with the foreskin).
G1987: Apparently a middle voice of ephistemi (with nous implied); to put the mind upon, i.e. Comprehend, or be acquainted with.
G1988: From epi and a presumed derivative of histemi; an appointee over, i.e. Commander (teacher).
G1989: From epi and stello; to enjoin (by writing), i.e. (genitive case) to communicate by letter (for any purpose).
G199: Adverb from the same as akribestatos; exactly.
G1991: to prop up, uphold, support, confirm, make stronger.
From epi and sterizo; to support further, i.e. Reestablish.
G1993: to muzzle, silence, stop the mouth.
From epi and stoma; to put something over the mouth, i.e. (figuratively) to silence.
G1994: (a) trans: to turn (back) to (towards), (b) intrans: to turn (back) (to [towards]); to come to myself.

Of uncertain derivation; Thyatira, a place in Asia Minor.

G2372: From thuo; passion (as if breathing hard).
G2373: to provoke to anger; pass: to be wroth or very angry.

G2374: Apparently a primary word (compare "door"); a portal or entrance (the opening or the closure, literally or figuratively).
G2375: From thura; a large shield (as door-shaped).

G2377: From thura and ouros (a watcher); a gate- warden.

G2379: From a derivative of thusia; a place of sacrifice, i.e. An altar (special or genitive case, literal or figurative).

G2381: "the twin", Thomas, one of the twelve apostles.

G2383: Jairus, the ruler of a synagogue in Palestine.

G2384: (Hebrew), Jacob, (a) the patriarch, son of Isaac, (b) father of Joseph, the husband of Mary.

Of Egyptian origin; Jambres, an Egyptian.
G2388: Jannai, an ancestor of Jesus; Jannai was the son of Joseph, and father of Melchi.

Of Egyptian origin; Jannes, an Egyptian.

Middle voice of apparently a primary verb; to cure (literally or figuratively).
G2391: (Hebrew), Jared, son of Mahalalel and father of Enoch.
Of Hebrew origin (Yered); Jared (i.e. Jered), an antediluvian.

G2420: the abstract notion of the priestly office.
From hieros; sacredness, i.e. (by implication) the priestly office.
G2421: (Hebrew), Jesse, son of Obed, and father of King David.

Of Hebrew origin (Ykonyah); Jechonias (i.e. Jekonjah), an Israelite.

G2425: (a) considerable, sufficient, of number, quantity, time, (b) of persons: sufficiently strong (good, etc.), worthy, suitable, with various constructions, (c) many, much.

G243: other, another (of more than two), different.
A primary word; "else," i.e. Different (in many applications).
G2430: Iconium, a Phrygian city of the Roman province Galatia (modern Konia).

G2431: From the same as hileos; propitious or merry ("hilarious"), i.e. Prompt or willing.
