From Kaisar; Caesaria, the name of two places in Palestine.
G2543: From kai and toi; and yet, i.e. Nevertheless.
G2544: From kaitoi and ge; and yet indeed, i.e. Although really.
G2545: to ignite, light, burn, lit. and met; to consume with fire.
Apparently a primary verb; to set on fire, i.e. Kindle or (by implication) consume.
G2546: and there, and yonder, there also.
From kai and ekei; likewise in that place.
G2547: and thence, and from there; and then afterwards.
From kai and ekeithen; likewise from that place (or time).
G2548: and he, she, it, and that.
From kai and ekeinos; likewise that (or those).
and him (other, them), even he, him also, them (also), (and) they.
G2549: (a) evil (i.e. trouble, labor, misfortune), (b) wickedness, (c) vicious disposition, malice, spite.
From kakos; badness, i.e. (subjectively) depravity, or (actively) malignity, or (passively) trouble.
G255: From a (as a negative particle) and the base of lusitelei; gainless, i.e. (by implication) pernicious.
G2550: From a compound of kakos and ethos; bad character, i.e. (specially) mischievousness.
G2551: to speak evil of, curse, revile, abuse.
From a compound of kakos and logos; to revile.
G2552: experience of evil, suffering, distress, affliction, perseverance.
From a compound of hemiorion and pathos; hardship.
G2553: From the same as kakopatheia; to undergo hardship.
be afflicted, endure afflictions (hardness), suffer trouble.
G2554: to do harm, do wrong, do evil, commit sin.
From kakopoios; to be a bad-doer, i.e. (objectively) to injure, or (genitive) to sin.
G2555: From kakos and poieo; a bad-doer; (specially), a criminal.
G2556: bad, evil, in the widest sense.
Apparently a primary word; worthless (intrinsically, such; whereas poneros properly refers to effects), i.e. (subjectively) depraved, or (objectively) injurious.
bad, evil, harm, ill, noisome, wicked.
G2557: From kakos and the base of ergon; a wrong-doer, i.e. Criminal.
G2558: From a presumed compound of kakos and echo; to maltreat.
G2559: to treat badly, afflict, embitter, make angry.
From kakos; to injure; figuratively, to exasperate.
make evil affected, entreat evil, harm, hurt, vex.
G256: Alphaeus; apparently two persons, (a) father of Levi, and (b) father of James.
Of Hebrew origin (compare Cheleph); Alphoeus, an Israelite.
G2560: amiss, diseased, evil, grievously, miserably, sick, sore.
G2562: Feminine of kalamos; a stalk of grain, i.e. (collectively) stubble.
G2563: a reed; a reed-pen, reed-staff, measuring rod.
Or uncertain affinity; a reed (the plant or its stem, or that of a similar plant); by implication, a pen.
G2564: (a) to call, summon, invite, (b) to call, name.
Akin to the base of keleuo; to "call" (properly, aloud, but used in a variety of applications, directly or otherwise).
G2565: From the base of kallion and elaia; a cultivated olive tree, i.e. A domesticated or improved one.
G2566: Neuter of the (irregular) comparative of kalos; (adverbially) better than many.
G2567: a teacher of that which is noble (honorable) and good.
From kalos and didaskalos; a teacher of the right.
G2568: Fair Havens, a harbor in Crete.
Plural of kalos and limen; Good Harbors, i.e. Fairhaven, a bay of Crete.
G2569: to do well, act honorably, do what is right.
From kalos and poieo; to do well, i.e. Live virtuously.
G257: Probably from the base of heilisso; a threshing-floor (as rolled hard), i.e. (figuratively) the grain (and chaff, as just threshed).
G2570: beautiful, as an outward sign of the inward good, noble, honorable character; good, worthy, honorable, noble, and seen to be so.

Of uncertain affinity; properly, beautiful, but chiefly (figuratively) good (literally or morally), i.e. Valuable or virtuous (for appearance or use, and thus distinguished from agathos, which is properly intrinsic).
X better, fair, good(-ly), honest, meet, well, worthy.
G2571: a covering, especially a covering of head and face, a veil.
From kalupto; a cover, i.e. Veil.
G2572: Akin to klepto and krupto; to cover up (literally or figuratively).
G2576: From a compound of kata and the base of musterion; to shut down, i.e. Close the eyes.
G2577: to work, be weary, be sick.
Apparently a primary verb; properly, to toil, i.e. (by implication) to tire (figuratively, faint, sicken).
G2578: Apparently a primary verb; to bend.
G2579: and if, even if, even, at least.
From kai and ean; and (or even) if.
and (also) if (so much as), if but, at the least, though, yet.
G258: a fox; a fox-like, crafty person.
Of uncertain derivation; a fox, i.e. (figuratively) a cunning person.
G2580: Of Hebrew origin (compare Qanah); Cana, a place in Palestine.
G2581: Cananaean, Aramaic for Zealot, surname of one of the twelve apostles.
Of Chaldee origin (compare qanna'); zealous; Cananites, an epithet.
Canaanite (by mistake for a derivative from Chanaan).
G2582: Candace, a proper name; the Candace, a dynastic name for queens of the Ethiopians in Abyssinia.
G2583: (lit: a level, ruler), a rule, regulation, rule of conduct or doctrine, (b) a measured (defined) area, province.
From kane (a straight reed, i.e. Rod); a rule ("canon"), i.e. (figuratively) a standard (of faith and practice); by implication, a boundary, i.e. (figuratively) a sphere (of activity).
G2584: Of Hebrew origin (probably kaphar and Nachuwm); Capernaum (i.e. Caphanachum), a place in Palestine.
G2585: to hawk, trade in, deal in for purposes of gain.
From kapelos (a huckster); to retail, i.e. (by implication) to adulterate (figuratively).
G2587: Cappadocia, a large Roman province in the central eastern part of Asia Minor.
Of foreign origin; Cappadocia, a region of Asia Minor.
G2588: lit: the heart; mind, character, inner self, will, intention, center.
Prolonged from a primary kar (Latin cor, "heart"); the heart, i.e. (figuratively) the thoughts or feelings (mind); also (by analogy) the middle.
G2589: a knower of the inner life (character, hearts).
From kardia and ginosko; a heart-knower.
G259: From a collateral form of haireomai.
G2590: (a) fruit, generally vegetable, sometimes animal, (b) met: fruit, deed, action, result, (c) profit, gain.
Probably from the base of harpazo; fruit (as plucked), literally or figuratively.
G2591: Perhaps for karpos; Carpus, probably a Christian.
G2592: From karpophoros; to be fertile (literally or figuratively).
G2594: to persevere, endure, be steadfast, patient.
From a derivative of kratos (transposed); to be strong, i.e. (figuratively) steadfast (patient).
G2595: a dry stalk, chip of wood, twig, splinter, chaff.
From karpho (to wither); a dry twig or straw.
G2596: gen: against, down from, throughout, by; acc: over against, among, daily, day-by-day, each day, according to, by way of.
A primary particle; (prepositionally) down (in place or time), in varied relations (according to the case (genitive, dative or accusative) with which it is joined).
about, according as (to), after, against, (when they were) X alone, among, and, X apart, (even, like) as (concerning, pertaining to touching), X aside, at, before, beyond, by, to the charge of,…
G2597: to go down, come down, either from the sky or from higher land, descend.
From kata and the base of basis; to descend (literally or figuratively).
G2598: (a) mid: to lay, of a foundation, (b) met: to cast down, prostrate.
From kata and ballo; to throw down.
G2599: From kata and bareo; to impose upon.
G26: love, benevolence, good will, esteem; plur: love-feasts.
From agapao; love, i.e. Affection or benevolence; specially (plural) a love-feast.
G260: at the same time, therewith, along with, together with.
A primary particle; properly, at the "same" time, but freely used as a preposition or adverb denoting close association.
G2601: to bring down, cast down, cause to go down.
From kata and a derivative of the base of basis; to cause to go down, i.e. Precipitate.
G2602: (a) foundation, (b) depositing, sowing, deposit, technically used of the act of conception.
From kataballo; a deposition, i.e. Founding; figuratively, conception.
G2603: of the umpire in a contest: to decide against, take part against, condemn (perhaps with the idea of assumption, officialism).
From kata and brabeuo (in its original sense); to award the price against, i.e. (figuratively) to defraud (of salvation).
G2605: to declare openly, proclaim, preach, laud, celebrate.
From kata and the base of aggelos; to proclaim, promulgate.
declare, preach, shew, speak of, teach.
G2607: From kata and ginosko; to note against, i.e. Find fault with.
G2608: to break down (in pieces), crush, break into.
From kata and the base of rhegnumi; to rend in pieces, i.e. Crack apart.
G2609: to lead down, bring down, either from a high place on land or to a lower (or actually to the sea-coast), or from the high seas to land.
From kata and ago; to lead down; specially, to moor a vessel.
G261: From a (as a negative particle) and manthano; ignorant.
G2610: to subdue (in warfare); to struggle against, conquer, overcome.
From kata and agonizomai; to struggle against, i.e. (by implication) to overcome.
G2611: From kata and deo; to tie down, i.e. Bandage (a wound).
G2612: From kata intensive and delos; manifest.
G2613: From kata and a derivative of dike; to adjudge against, i.e. Pronounce guilty.
G2614: From kata and dioko; to hunt down, i.e. Search for.
G2615: From kata and douloo; to enslave utterly.
G2616: From kata and a derivative of dunastes; to exercise dominion against, i.e. Oppress.
G2617: to shame, disgrace, bring to shame, put to utter confusion, frustrate.
From kata and aischunomai; to shame down, i.e. Disgrace or (by implication) put to the blush.
G2618: From kata and kaio; to burn down (to the ground), i.e. Consume wholly.
G2619: From kata and kalupto; to cover wholly, i.e. Veil.
G2620: From kata and kauchaomai; to exult against (i.e. Over).
G2621: to recline (at table); more often: to keep bed, be lying ill (in bed).
From kata and keimai; to lie down, i.e. (by implication) be sick; specially, to recline at a meal.
G2622: to break in pieces, break up.
From kata and klao; to break down, i.e. Divide.
G2623: From kata and kleio; to shut down (in a dungeon), i.e. Incarcerate.
G2624: to give as an inheritance, distribute by lot.
From kata and a derivative of a compound of kleros and didomi; to be a giver of lots to each, i.e. (by implication) to apportion an estate.
G2625: to cause to recline at table; mid. and pass: to recline at table.
From kata and klino; to recline down, i.e. (specially) to take a place at table.
G2626: From kata and the base of kludon; to dash (wash) down, i.e. (by implication) to deluge.
G2628: From kata and akoloutheo; to accompany closely.
G2629: to cut up, cut in pieces, mangle, wound.
From kata and kopto; to chop down, i.e. Mangle.
G263: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of maraino; unfading, i.e. (by implication) perpetual.
G2630: to cast down headlong, throw over a precipice.
From kata and a derivative of kremnos; to precipitate down.
G2631: punishment following condemnation, penal servitude, penalty.
From katakrino; an adverse sentence (the verdict).
G2632: to condemn, judge worthy of punishment.
From kata and krino; to judge against, i.e. Sentence.
G2634: to exercise authority over, overpower, master.
From kata and kurieuo; to lord against, i.e. Control, subjugate.
exercise dominion over (lordship), be lord over, overcome.
G2635: to speak evil of, rail at, slander.
From katalalos; to be a traducer, i.e. To slander.
G2637: slanderous, back-biting; subst: a railer, defamer.
From kata and the base of laleo; talkative against, i.e. A slanderer.
G2638: (a) to seize tight hold of, arrest, catch, capture, appropriate, (b) to overtake, (c) mid. aor: to perceived, comprehended.
From kata and lambano; to take eagerly, i.e. Seize, possess, etc. (literally or figuratively).
apprehend, attain, come upon, comprehend, find, obtain, perceive, (over-)take.
G2639: to enter in a list, register, enroll.
From kata and lego (in its original meaning); to lay down, i.e. (figuratively) to enrol.
G264: originally: to miss the mark, hence (a) to make a mistake, (b) to sin, commit a sin (against God); sometimes the idea of sinning against a fellow-creature is present.
Perhaps from a (as a negative particle) and the base of meros; properly, to miss the mark (and so not share in the prize), i.e. (figuratively) to err, especially (morally) to sin.
for your faults, offend, sin, trespass.
G2640: From kataleipo; a remainder, i.e. (by implication) a few.
G2641: to leave behind, desert, abandon, forsake; to leave remaining, reserve.
From kata and leipo; to leave down, i.e. Behind; by implication, to abandon, have remaining.
G2642: to stone down, stone to death, overwhelm with stones.
From kata and lithazo; to stone down, i.e. To death.
G2643: From katallasso; exchange (figuratively, adjustment), i.e. Restoration to (the divine) favor.
G2644: From kata and allasso; to change mutually, i.e. (figuratively) to compound a difference.
G2645: left behind; the rest, the remainder.
From kata and loipoy; left down (behind), i.e remaining (plural the rest).
G2646: From kataluo; properly, a dissolution (breaking up of a journey), i.e. (by implication) a lodging-place.
G2647: (lit: to loosen thoroughly), (a) trans: to break up, overthrow, destroy, both lit. and met., (b) to unyoke, unharness a carriage horse or pack animal; hence: to put up, lodge, find a lodging.
From kata and luo; to loosen down (disintegrate), i.e. (by implication) to demolish (literally or figuratively); specially (compare kataluma) to halt for the night.
destroy, dissolve, be guest, lodge, come to nought, overthrow, throw down.
G2648: to understand, take in a fact about, consider carefully.
From kata and manthano; to learn thoroughly, i.e. (by implication) to note carefully.
G2649: From kata and martureo; to testify against.
G2650: to wait, stay (with), remain, abide, dwell.
From kata and meno; to stay fully, i.e. Reside.
G2651: From kata and accusative case plural feminine of monos (with chora implied); according to sole places, i.e. (adverbially) separately.
G2652: From kata (intensive) and anathema; an imprecation.
G2653: From kata (intensive) and anathematizo; to imprecate.
G2654: to use up, spend, consume (as with fire).
From kata and analisko; to consume utterly.
G2655: (properly a medical term: to stupefy, hence) to burden, encumber.
From kata and narkao (to be numb); to grow utterly torpid, i.e. (by implication) slothful (figuratively, expensive).
G2656: to make a sign (by nodding the head).
From kata and neuo; to nod down (towards), i.e. (by analogy) to make signs to.
G2657: to take note of, perceive, consider carefully, discern, detect, make account of.
From kata and noieo; to observe fully.
G2658: (a) to come down, either from high land to lower (or actually to the sea-coast), or from the high seas to the coast; hence met: to arrive at, reach (destination), (b) of property: to come down (descend) by inheritance…
From kata and a derivative of anti; to meet against, i.e. Arrive at (literally or figuratively).
G2659: From katanusso; a prickling (sensation, as of the limbs asleep), i.e. (by implication, (perhaps by some confusion with neuo or even with nux)) stupor (lethargy).
G266: prop: missing the mark; hence: (a) guilt, sin, (b) a fault, failure (in an ethical sense), sinful deed.
G2660: met: to be pierced, stung, smitten.
From kata and nusso; to pierce thoroughly, i.e. (figuratively) to agitate violently ("sting to the quick").
G2661: From kata and axioo; to deem entirely deserving.
G2662: to trample down, trample under foot (lit. and met.), spurn.
From kata and pateo; to trample down; figuratively, to reject with disdain.
G2663: (in the Old Testament of the rest attained by the settlement in Canaan), resting, rest, dwelling, habitation.
From katapauo; reposing down, i.e. (by Hebraism) abode.
G2664: (a) trans: to cause to rest, bring to rest; to cause to refrain, (b) intrans: to rest.
From kata and pauo; to settle down, i.e. (literally) to colonize, or (figuratively) to (cause to) desist.
G2665: (lit: that which is spread out downwards, that which hangs down), a curtain, veil, of that which separated the Holy of Holies from the outer parts of the temple at Jerusalem, also of an outer curtain at the entrance to…
From a compound of kata and a congener of petomai; something spread thoroughly, i.e. (specially) the door screen (to the Most Holy Place) in the Jewish Temple.
G2666: to drink down, swallow, devour, destroy, consume.
From kata and pino; to drink down, i.e. Gulp entire (literally or figuratively).
G2667: From kata and pipto; to fall down.
G2668: to sail down (from the high seas to the shore).
From kata and pleo; to sail down upon a place, i.e. To land at.
G2669: to exhaust by labor or suffering, wear out, overpower, oppress.
From kata and a derivative of ponos; to labor down, i.e. Wear with toil (figuratively, harass).
G267: From a (as a negative particle) and a form of martus; unattested.
G2670: to sink in the sea, pass: to drown, be submerged.
From kata and a derivative of the same as Pontos; to plunge down, i.e. Submerge.
G2671: cursing; a curse; meton: a doomed one.
From kata (intensive) and ara; imprecation, execration.
G2672: Middle voice from katara; to execrate; by analogy, to doom.
G2673: (a) to make idle (inactive), make of no effect, annul, abolish, bring to naught, (b) to discharge, sever, separate from.
From kata and argeo; to be (render) entirely idle (useless), literally or figuratively.
abolish, cease, cumber, deliver, destroy, do away, become (make) of no (none, without) effect, fail, loose, bring (come) to nought, put away (down), vanish away, make void.
G2674: From kata and arithmeo; to reckon among.
G2675: (a) to fit (join) together; met: to compact together, (b) act. and mid: to prepare, perfect, for his (its) full destination or use, bring into its proper condition (whether for the first time, or after a lapse).
From kata and a derivative of artios; to complete thoroughly, i.e. Repair (literally or figuratively) or adjust.
fit, frame, mend, (make) perfect(-ly join together), prepare, restore.
G2677: a bringing to a condition of fitness, perfecting.
G2678: to shake (the hand) up and down, wave; intrans: to beckon for silence.
From kata and seio; to sway downward, i.e. Make a signal.
G2679: to dig down under, demolish, undermine.
From kata and skapto; to undermine, i.e. (by implication) destroy.
G268: From hamartano; sinful, i.e. A sinner.
G2680: to build, construct, prepare, make ready.
From kata and a derivative of skeuos; to prepare thoroughly (properly, by external equipment; whereas hetoimazo refers rather to internal fitness); by implication, to construct, create.
G2681: to encamp, take up quarters, tabernacle, pitch tent, dwell.
From kata and skenoo; to camp down, i.e. Haunt; figuratively, to remain.
G2682: From kataskenoo; an encamping, i.e. (figuratively) a perch.
G2683: From kata and a derivative of skia; to overshade, i.e. Cover.
G2684: to view closely, inspect, spy out.
From kataskopos; to be a sentinel, i.e. To inspect insidiously.
G2685: From kata (intensive) and skopos (in the sense of a watcher); a reconnoiterer.
G2686: Middle voice from kata and sophizo; to be crafty against, i.e. Circumvent.
G2687: to let down, lower; to keep down, restrain, pacify.
From kata and stello; to put down, i.e. Quell.
G2688: From kathistemi; properly, a position or condition, i.e. (subjectively) demeanor.
G2689: From katastello; a deposit, i.e. (specially) costume.
G269: peaceable, abstaining from fighting, not contentious.
From a (as a negative particle) and mache; peaceable.
G2690: From kata and strepho; to turn upside down, i.e. Upset.
G2691: From kata and streniao; to become voluptuous against.
G2692: From katastrepho; an overturn ("catastrophe"), i.e. Demolition; figuratively, apostasy.
G2693: to strew or spread over; to lay low, overthrow.
From kata and stronnumi; to strew down, i.e. (by implication) to prostrate (slay).
G2694: From kata and suro; to drag down, i.e. Arrest judicially.
G2695: From kata and sphazo; to kill down, i.e. Slaughter.
G2696: to seal up, secure with a seal.
From kata and sphragizo; to seal closely.
G2697: From katecho; a holding down, i.e. Occupancy.
G2698: (a) to lay down, deposit, (b) mid: to lay down or deposit a favor, with the view of receiving one in return, seek favor.
From kata and tithemi; to place down, i.e. Deposit (literally or figuratively).
G2699: From a compound of kata and temno (to cut); a cutting down (off), i.e. Mutilation (ironically).
G27: loved, beloved, with two special applications: the Beloved, a title of the Messiah (Christ), as beloved beyond all others by the God who sent Him; of Christians, as beloved by God, Christ, and one another.
G270: From hama; properly, to collect, i.e. (by implication) reap.
G2700: to strike down with an arrow.
From kata and a derivative of toxon; to shoot down with an arrow or other missile.
G2701: From kata and trecho; to run down, i.e. Hasten from a tower.
G2702: to bear down, overpower; to give a vote or verdict, bring charges.
From kata and phero (including its alternate); to bear down, i.e. (figuratively) overcome (with drowsiness); specially, to cast a vote.
G2703: to flee for refuge (implying that the refuge is reached); aor. indicates moment of arrival.
From kata and pheugo; to flee down (away).
G2704: From kata and phtheiro; to spoil entirely, i.e. (literally) to destroy; or (figuratively) to deprave.
G2705: From kata and phileo; to kiss earnestly.
G2706: to despise, scorn, and show it by active insult, disregard.
From kata and phroneo; to think against, i.e. Disesteem.
G2708: From kata and cheo (to pour); to pour down (out).
G2709: From kata and chthon (the ground); subterranean, i.e. Infernal (belonging to the world of departed spirits).
G271: amethyst (a kind of rock crystal: the best specimens are the color of unmixed wine, whence perhaps the name), believed to stave off drunkenness.
From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of methuo; the "amethyst" (supposed to prevent intoxication).
G2710: to use to the full, use up.
From kata and chraomai; to overuse, i.e. Misuse.
G2711: From kata and psucho; to cool down (off), i.e. Refresh.
G2712: full of images of idols, grossly idolatrous.
From kata (intensively) and eidolon; utterly idolatrous.
G2713: From kata and enanti; directly opposite.
G2714: before the face of, over against.
From kata and enopion; directly in front of.
before (the presence of), in the sight of.
G2715: From kata and exousiazo; to have (wield) full privilege over.
G2716: to effect by labor, achieve, work out, bring about.
From kata and ergazomai; to work fully, i.e. Accomplish; by implication, to finish, fashion.
G2718: to come down from sky to earth, or from high land to lower land (or to the coast), or from the high seas to the shore.
From kata and erchomai (including its alternate); to come (or go) down (literally or figuratively).
come (down), depart, descend, go down, land.
G2719: to eat up, eat till it is finished, devour, squander, annoy, injure.
From kata and esthio (including its alternate); to eat down, i.e. Devour (literally or figuratively).
G272: to neglect, be careless of, disregard.
From a (as a negative particle) and melo; to be careless of.
make light of, neglect, be negligent, no regard.
G2720: (a) to make straight, (b) met: to put in the right way, direct.
From kata and euthuno; to straighten fully, i.e. (figuratively) direct.
G2721: to rush, assault, rise up against.
From kata and ephistemi; to stand over against, i.e. Rush upon (assault).
G2722: (a) to hold fast, bind, arrest, (b) to take possession of, lay hold of, (c) to hold back, detain, restrain, (d) to hold a ship, keep its head.
From kata and echo; to hold down (fast), in various applications (literally or figuratively).
have, hold (fast), keep (in memory), let, X make toward, possess, retain, seize on, stay, take, withhold.
G2723: From kategoros; to be a plaintiff, i.e. To charge with some offence.
G2724: From kategoros; a complaint ("category"), i.e. Criminal charge.
G2725: From kata and agora; against one in the assembly, i.e. A complainant at law; specially, Satan.
G2726: a downcast countenance as a sign of sorrow, gloominess, gloom, dejection.
From a compound of kata and perhaps a derivative of the base of phaino (meaning downcast in look); demureness, i.e. (by implication) sadness.
G2727: From kata and echos; to sound down into the ears, i.e. (by implication) to indoctrinate ("catechize") or (genitive case) to apprise of.
G2728: to rust; pass: to be rusted, tarnished.
From kata and a derivative of ios; to rust down, i.e. Corrode.
G2729: to prevail against, overpower, get the upper hand.
From kata and ischuo; to overpower.
G273: blameless, free from fault or defect.
From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of memphomai; irreproachable.
G2730: to dwell in, settle in, be established in (permanently), inhabit.
From kata and oikeo; to house permanently, i.e. Reside (literally or figuratively).
G2731: From katoikeo; residence (properly, the act; but by implication, concretely, the mansion).
G2732: From a derivative of katoikeo; a dwelling-place.
G2733: Residence (properly, the condition; but by implication, the abode itself).
G2734: Middle voice from a compound of kata and a derivative of optanomai (compare esoptron); to mirror oneself, i.e. To see reflected (figuratively).
G2735: anything happily and successfully accomplished, a beneficial and worthy deed.
From a compound of kata and a derivative of orthos (compare diorthosis); something made fully upright, i.e. (figuratively) rectification (specially, good public administration).
G2736: (a) down, below, also: downwards, (b) lower, under, less, of a length of time.
Also (compare) katotero (kat-o-ter'-o); (compare katoteros); adverb from kata; downwards.
G2737: Comparative from kato; inferior (locally, of Hades).
G2738: From kaio; properly, a burn (concretely), but used (abstractly) of a glow.
G2741: From kausis; to set on fire.
G2743: to cauterize, burn with a hot iron; hence met: to sear.
From a derivative of kaio; to brand ("cauterize"), i.e. (by implication) to render unsensitive (figuratively).
G2744: From some (obsolete) base akin to that of aucheo (to boast) and euchomai; to vaunt (in a good or a bad sense).
G2745: a boasting; a ground of boasting (glorying, exultation).
From kauchaomai; a boast (properly, the object; by implication, the act) in a good or a bad sense.
G2746: the act of boasting, glorying, exultation.
From kauchaomai; boasting (properly, the act; by implication, the object), in a good or a bad sense.
boasting, whereof I may glory, glorying, rejoicing.
G2747: Cenchreae, the port of Corinth on the Saronic Gulf.
Probably from kegchros (millet); Cenchreae, a port of Corinth.
G2748: Kidron, a brook and wadi near Jer.
Of Hebrew origin (Qidrown); Cedron (i.e. Kidron), a brook near Jerusalem.
G2749: to lie, recline, be placed, be laid, set, specially appointed, destined.
Middle voice of a primary verb; to lie outstretched (literally or figuratively).
be (appointed, laid up, made, set), lay, lie. Compare tithemi.
G275: free from anxiety (though anxiety is rather too strong a word) or care.
From a (as a negative particle) and merimna; not anxious.
G2750: a kind of girdle made of cords; a bandage, grave clothes.
Of uncertain affinity; a swathe, i.e. Winding-sheet.
G2751: to shear, cut the hair of; mid: to cut own hair, have hair cut.
G2752: a word of command, a call, an arousing outcry.
From keleuo; a cry of incitement.
G2753: From a primary kello (to urge on); "hail"; to incite by word, i.e. Order.
G2754: From kenodoxos; empty glorying, i.e. Self-conceit.
G2755: From kenos and doxa; vainly glorifying, i.e. Self-conceited.
G2756: (a) empty, (b) met: empty (in moral content), vain, ineffective, foolish, worthless, (c) false, unreal, pretentious, hollow.
Apparently a primary word; empty (literally or figuratively).
G2757: From a presumed compound of kenos and phone; empty sounding, i.e. Fruitless discussion.
G2758: (a) to empty, (b) to deprive of content, make unreal.
From kenos; to make empty, i.e. (figuratively) to abase, neutralize, falsify.
make (of none effect, of no reputation, void), be in vain.
G2759: a sting, goad; met: of death.
From kenteo (to prick); a point ("centre"), i.e. A sting (figuratively, poison) or goad (figuratively, divine impulse).
G276: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of metatithemi; unchangeable, or (neuter as abstract) unchangeability.
G2760: a centurion, an officer commanding about a hundred infantry in the Roman army.
Of Latin origin; a centurion, i.e. Captain of one hundred soldiers.
G2761: falsely, in vain, to no purpose.
Adverb from kenos; vainly, i.e. To no purpose.
G2762: a little hook, an apostrophe on letters of the alphabet, distinguishing them from other little letters, or a separation stroke between letters.
Feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of keras; something horn-like, i.e. (specially) the apex of a Hebrew letter (figuratively, the least particle).
G2764: of clay, made by a potter, earthen.
From keramos; made of clay, i.e. Earthen.
G2765: Neuter of a presumed derivative of keramos; an earthenware vessel, i.e. Jar.
G2766: Probably from the base of kerannumi (through the idea of mixing clay and water); earthenware, i.e. A tile (by analogy, a thin roof or awning).
G2767: to mix, mingle, pour out for drinking.
Prolonged form of a more primary kerao ker-ah'-o (which is used in certain tenses); to mingle, i.e. (by implication) to pour out (for drinking).
G2768: (a) a horn, (b) a horn-like projection at the corner of an altar, (c) a horn as a symbol of power.
From a primary kar (the hair of the head); a horn (literally or figuratively).
G2769: Neuter of a presumed derivative of keras; something horned, i.e. (specially) the pod of the carob-tree.
G277: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of metakineo; immovable.
G2770: to gain, acquire, win (over), avoid loss.
From kerdos; to gain (literally or figuratively).
G2771: Of uncertain affinity; gain (pecuniary or genitive case).
G2772: a small coin; plur: small change.
From keiro; a clipping (bit), i.e. (specially) a coin.
G2773: properly: a changer of large into smaller coins, a money-changer.
From a derivative of kerma; a handler of coins, i.e. Money-broker.
G2774: (a) the chief matter, the main point, (b) a sum of money.
Neuter of a derivative of kephale; a principal thing, i.e. Main point; specially, an amount (of money).
G2775: From the same as kephalaion; (specially) to strike on the head.
G2776: (a) the head, (b) met: a corner stone, uniting two walls; head, ruler, lord.
From the primary kapto (in the sense of seizing); the head (as the part most readily taken hold of), literally or figuratively.
G2777: (lit: little head, then: the knob at the end of the wooden core of a roll of papyrus, then) a roll, volume, division (of a book).
From kephale; properly, a knob, i.e. (by implication) a roll (by extension from the end of a stick on which the manuscript was rolled).
G2778: Of Latin origin; properly, an enrollment ("census"), i.e. (by implication) a tax.
G2779: a garden, any place planted with trees and herbs.
G278: not to be repented of, about which no change of mind can take place, not affected by change of mind.
From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of metamellomai; irrevocable.
without repentance, not to be repented of.
G2780: From kepos and ouros (a warden); a garden-keeper, i.e. Gardener.
G2781: Diminutive from keos (wax); a cell for honey, i.e. (collectively) the comb.
G2782: From kerusso; a proclamation (especially of the gospel; by implication, the gospel itself).
G2783: From kerusso; a herald, i.e. Of divine truth (especially of the gospel).
G2784: Of uncertain affinity; to herald (as a public crier), especially divine truth (the gospel).
G2785: a sea monster, huge sea fish, whale.
Probably from the base of chasma; a huge fish (as gaping for prey).
G2786: Cephas (Aramaic for rock), the new name given to Simon Peter, the apostle.
Of Chaldee origin (compare keph); the Rock; Cephas (i.e. Kepha), a surname of Peter.
G2787: (properly: a wooden box, hence) the Ark, in which Noah sailed; the Ark of the Covenant.
Of uncertain derivation; a box, i.e. The sacred ark and that of Noah.
G2789: intrans. and trans: to play on the harp, to harp, with acc. of the tune.
From kithara; to play on a lyre.
G279: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of metanoeo; unrepentant.
G2790: a harpist, one who sings with harp as accompaniment.
From kithara and a derivative of the same as oide; a lyre-singer(-player), i.e. Harpist.
G2791: Cilicia, a Roman province between the Taurus range of mountains and the coast in the south-east corner of Asia Minor, linked up with the province of Syria.
Probably of foreign origin; Cilicia, a region of Asia Minor.
G2793: to be in danger or peril.
be in danger, be (stand) in jeopardy.
G2795: to set in motion, move, remove, excite, stir up.
From kio (poetic for eimi, to go); to stir (transitively), literally or figuratively.
G2797: Kish, the father of King Saul.
Of Hebrew origin (Qiysh); Cis (i.e. Kish), an Israelite.
G2798: a young tender shoot, then: a branch; met: of descendants.
From klao; a twig or bough (as if broken off).
G2799: to weep, weep for, mourn, lament.
Of uncertain affinity; to sob, i.e. Wail aloud (whereas dakruo is rather to cry silently).
G28: Hagar, the servant of Sarah, concubine of Abraham.
Of Hebrew origin (Hagar); Hagar, the concubine of Abraham.
G280: not measurable, immeasurable, to a limitless degree.
From a (as a negative particle) and metron; immoderate.
G2802: Cauda, Clauda, an island twenty-three miles south of the western end of Crete.
Of uncertain derivation; Claude, an island near Crete.
G2803: Claudia, a Christian woman in Rome; probably a freedwoman of the imperial household.
Feminine of Klaudios; Claudia, a Christian woman.
G2804: (a) Claudius, the fourth of the Roman Emperors, Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, who ruled A.D. 41-54, (b) Claudius Lysias, a tribune at Jerusalem.
Of Latin origin; Claudius, the name of two Romans.
G2806: A primary verb; to break (specially, of bread).
G2807: From kleio; a key (as shutting a lock), literally or figuratively.
G2808: A primary verb; to close (literally or figuratively).
G2809: From klepto; stealing (properly, the thing stolen, but used of the act).
G281: verily, truly, amen; at the end of sentences may be paraphrased by: So let it be.
Of Hebrew origin ('amen); properly, firm, i.e. (figuratively) trustworthy; adverbially, surely (often as interjection, so be it).
G2810: Cleopas, one of the two companions of the risen Jesus from Jerusalem to Emmaus.
Probably contracted from Kleopatros (compound of kleos and pater); Cleopas, a Christian.
G2811: glory, fame, praise; rumor, report, credit.
From a shorter form of kaleo; renown (as if being called).
G2812: From klepto; a stealer (literally or figuratively).
G2814: From klao; a limb or shoot (as if broken off).
G2815: Clement, a fellow-worker of Paul in Rome.
Of Latin origin; merciful; Clemes (i.e. Clemens), a Christian.
G2816: to inherit, obtain (possess) by inheritance, acquire.
From kleronomos; to be an heir to (literally or figuratively).
G2817: an inheritance, an heritage, regularly the gift of God to His chosen people, in the Old Testament: the Promised Land, in NT a possession viewed in one sense as present, in another as future; a share, participation.
From kleronomos; heirship, i.e. (concretely) a patrimony or (genitive case) a possession.
G2818: From kleros and the base of nomos (in its original sense of partitioning, i.e. (reflexively) getting by apportionment); a sharer by lot, i.e. Inheritor (literally or figuratively); by implication, a possessor.
G2819: (a) a lot, (b) a portion assigned; hence: a portion of the people of God assigned to one's care, a congregation.

Probably from klao (through the idea of using bits of wood, etc., for the purpose; a die (for drawing chances); by implication, a portion (as if so secured); by extension, an acquisition (especially a patrimony, figuratively).
G282: (lit: motherless), whose mother's name is not recorded (or known).
From a (as a negative particle) and meter; motherless, i.e. Of unknown maternity.
G2820: to cast lots, choose by lot, assign by lot, assign a portion, receive a share.
From kleros; to allot, i.e. (figuratively) to assign (a privilege).
G2821: a calling, invitation; in the NT, always of a divine call.
From a shorter form of kaleo; an invitation (figuratively).
G2822: called, invited, summoned by God to an office or to salvation.
From the same as klesis; invited, i.e. Appointed, or (specially), a saint.
G2823: Of uncertain derivation; an earthen pot used for baking in.
G2824: a small geographical division, district, or territory.
From klino; a slope, i.e. (specially) a "clime" or tract of country.
G2825: a couch, bed, portable bed or mat, a couch for reclining at meals, possibly also a bier.
From klino; a couch (for sleep, sickness, sitting or eating).
G2826: a couch or litter of a sick person.
Neuter of a presumed derivative of kline; a pallet or little couch.
G2827: trans: to rest, recline; to bend, incline; to cause to give ground, make to yield; intrans: to decline, approach end.
A primary verb; to slant or slope, i.e. Incline or recline (literally or figuratively).
bow (down), be far spent, lay, turn to flight, wear away.
G2828: properly: a dining couch; hence: a group of diners.
From a derivative of klino; properly, reclination, i.e. (concretely and specially), a party at a meal.
G283: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of miaino; unsoiled, i.e. (figuratively) pure.
G2830: rough water, a wave, billow, surge.
From kluzo (to billow or dash over); a surge of the sea (literally or figuratively).
G2831: to be tossed by waves, met: to be tossed to and fro.
Middle voice from kludon; to surge, i.e. (figuratively) to fluctuate.
G2832: Clopas, husband of one Mary, who stood by the cross.
Of Chaldee origin (corresponding to 'Ach'ab); Clopas, an Israelite.
G2833: to rub, tickle, scratch; pass: to itch.
From a primary knao (to scrape); to scratch, i.e. (by implication) to tickle.
G2834: Cnidus, a town on the coast of Caria (south-west Asia Minor) near the island of Cos.
Probably of foreign origin; Cnidus, a place in Asia Minor.
G2835: a quadrans, the smallest Roman copper coin, a quarter of an as, the sixteenth part of a sesterius.
Of Latin origin; a quadrans, i.e. The fourth part of an as.
G2836: belly, abdomen, heart, a general term covering any organ in the abdomen, e.g. stomach, womb; met: the inner man.
From koilos ("hollow"); a cavity, i.e. (especially) the abdomen; by implication, the matrix; figuratively, the heart.
G2837: to fall asleep, be asleep, sometimes of the sleep of death.
From keimai (g2749); to put to sleep, i.e. (passively or reflexively) to slumber; figuratively, to decease.
(be a-, fall a-, fall on) sleep, be dead.
G2838: From koimao; sleeping, i.e. (by implication) repose.
G2839: (a) common, shared, (b) Hebraistic use: profane; dirty, unclean, unwashed.
Probably from sun; common, i.e. (literally) shared by all or several, or (ceremonially) profane.
G284: Amminadab, son of Ram and father of Nahshon, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
Of Hebrew origin (Ammiynadab); Aminadab, an Israelite.
G2840: to make unclean, pollute, desecrate, mid: to regard (treat) as unclean.
From koinos; to make (or consider) profane (ceremonially).
G2841: (a) to share, communicate, contribute, impart, (b) to share in, have a share of, have fellowship with.
From koinonos; to share with others (objectively or subjectively).
G2842: (lit: partnership) (a) contributory help, participation, (b) sharing in, communion, (c) spiritual fellowship, a fellowship in the spirit.
From koinonos; partnership, i.e. (literally) participation, or (social) intercourse, or (pecuniary) benefaction.
G2843: willing to share, sociable, ready to communicate, beneficent.
G2844: From koinos; a sharer, i.e. Associate.
G2845: (a) a bed, (b) a marriage bed; plur: repeated (immoral) sexual intercourse.
From keimai; a couch; by extension, cohabitation; by implication, the male sperm.
G2847: crimson, scarlet, dyed with Kermes (coccum), the female coccus of the Kermes oak.
From kokkos (from the kernel-shape of the insect); crimson-colored.
G2848: Apparently a primary word; a kernel of seed.
G2849: to chastise, curtail, punish; mid: to cause to be punished.
From kolos (dwarf); properly, to curtail, i.e. (figuratively) to chastise (or reserve for infliction).
G285: Perhaps from hama; sand (as heaped on the beach).
G2850: flattery, with a view to advantage or gain.
From a derivative of kolax (a fawner); flattery.
G2851: chastisement, punishment, torment, perhaps with the idea of deprivation.
G2852: to strike with the fist, buffet; hence: to mistreat violently.
From a derivative of the base of kolazo; to rap with the fist.
G2853: (lit: to glue); hence: mid. and pass: to join myself closely, cleave, adhere (to), to keep company (with), of friendly intercourse.
From kolla ("glue"); to glue, i.e. (passively or reflexively) to stick (figuratively).
G2854: Neuter of a presumed derivative of kollura (a cake; prob akin to the base of kollao); properly, a poultice (as made of or in the form of crackers), i.e. (by analogy) a plaster.
G2855: a money-changer, who changed heathen into Jewish money, for payment into the Temple treasury.
From a presumed derivative of kollubos (a small coin; probably akin to kollourion); a coin-dealer.
G2856: (lit: to maim, mutilate), to cut short, shorten, abbreviate.
From a derivative of the base of kolazo; to dock, i.e. (figuratively) abridge.
G2857: Colossae, a town of the Roman province Asia, in the Lycus valley, near Laodicea and Hierapolis.
Apparently feminine plural of kolossos ("colossal"); Colossae, a place in Asia Minor.
G2858: From Kolossai; a Colossaean, (i.e. Inhabitant of Colossae.
G2859: (a) sing. and plur: bosom; (sinus) the overhanging fold of the garment used as a pocket, (b) a bay, gulf.
Apparently a primary word; the bosom; by analogy, a bay.
G286: a lamb (as a type of innocence, and with sacrificial connotation).
Apparently a primary word; a lamb.
G2860: From kolumbos (a diver); to plunge into water.
G2861: (lit: a diving or swimming place), a pool.
A diving-place, i.e. Pond for bathing (or swimming).
G2862: a colony, a city settlement of Roman (soldier) citizens; a garrison city.
Of Latin origin; a Roman "colony" for veterans.
G2863: to wear the hair long, allow the hair to grow out.
From kome; to wear tresses of hair.
G2864: Apparently from the same as komizo; the hair of the head (locks, as ornamental, and thus differing from thrix; which properly denotes merely the scalp).
G2865: (a) act: to convey, bring, carry, (b) mid: to receive back, receive what has belonged to myself but has been lost, or else promised but kept back, or: to get what has come to be own by earning, recover.
From a primary komeo (to tend, i.e. Take care of); properly, to provide for, i.e. (by implication) to carry off (as if from harm; genitive case obtain).
G2866: Neuter comparative of a derivative of the base of komizo (meaning, properly, well dressed, i.e. Nice); figuratively, convalescent.
G2867: From konia (dust; by analogy, lime); to whitewash.
G2868: From the base of koniao and ornumi (to "rouse"); pulverulence (as blown about).
G2869: to abate, cease raging, be stilled.
From kopos; to tire, i.e. (figuratively) to relax.
G287: a change, an exchange; hence plur: reciprocal good deeds (services), a fitting requital.
G2870: beating of the breast or head in lamentation, lamentation.
From kopto; mourning (properly, by beating the breast).
G2872: (a) to grow weary, (b) to toil, work with effort (of bodily and mental labor alike).
From a derivative of kopos; to feel fatigue; by implication, to work hard.
G2873: (a) trouble, (b) toil, labor, laborious toil, involving weariness and fatigue.
From kopto; a cut, i.e. (by analogy) toil (as reducing the strength), literally or figuratively; by implication, pains.
G2874: From kopros (ordure; perhaps akin to kopto); manure.
G2875: (a) to cut, cut off, strike, smite, (b) mid: to beat breast or head in lamentation, lament, mourn, sometimes with acc. of person whose loss is mourned.
A primary verb; to "chop"; specially, to beat the breast in grief.
cut down, lament, mourn, (be-)wail. Compare the base of tomoteros.
G2876: Perhaps from korennumi; a crow (from its voracity).
G2877: a little girl, a young girl; a girl, maiden.
Neuter of a presumed derivative of kore (a maiden); a (little) girl.
G2878: a gift, offering, anything consecrated to God.

Korbanas (kor-ban-as') of Hebrew and Chaldee origin respectively (qorban); a votive offering and the offering; a consecrated present (to the Temple fund); by extension (the latter term) the Treasury itself, i.e. The room where the contribution boxes stood.
G2879: Of Hebrew origin (Qorach); Core (i.e. Korach), an Israelite.
G288: Probably from the base of amphoteros and that of halon; a vine (as coiling about a support).
G2880: to fill, sate, glut, feed full, satisfy.
A primary verb; to cram, i.e. Glut or sate.
G2881: From Korinthos; a Corinthian, i.e. Inhabitant of Corinth.
G2882: Corinth, in north-east Peloponnese, the capital of the Roman province Achaia.
Of uncertain derivation; Corinthus, a city of Greece.
G2883: Cornelius, a centurion of the Roman army, stationed at Caesarea.
Of Latin origin; Cornelius, a Roman.
G2884: a cor (a Hebrew measure equiv. to about 15 bushels).
Of Hebrew origin (kor); a cor, i.e. A specific measure.
G2885: to put into order; to decorate, deck, adorn.
From kosmos; to put in proper order, i.e. Decorate (literally or figuratively); specially, to snuff (a wick).
G2886: earthly, worldly (belonging to the present earthly world as opposed to the heavenly and future).
From kosmos (in its secondary sense); terrene ("cosmic"), literally (mundane) or figuratively (corrupt).
G2887: From kosmos (in its primary sense); orderly, i.e. Decorous.
G2888: ruler of this world, that is, of the world as asserting its independence of God; used of the angelic or demonic powers controlling the sublunary world.
From kosmos and krateo; a world-ruler, an epithet of Satan.
G2889: the world, universe; worldly affairs; the inhabitants of the world; adornment.
Probably from the base of komizo; orderly arrangement, i.e. Decoration; by implication, the world (in a wide or narrow sense, including its inhabitants, literally or figuratively (morally)).
G289: From ampelos and ergon; a vine-worker, i.e. Pruner.
G2890: Quartus, a Christian, brother of Erastus the Corinthian.
Of Latin origin (fourth); Quartus, a Christian.
G2892: Of Latin origin; "custody", i.e. A Roman sentry.
G2893: From kouphos (light in weight); to unload.
G2895: a bed, mattress, mat of a poor man.
Probably of foreign origin; a mattress.
G2896: A primary verb; properly, to "croak" (as a raven) or scream, i.e. (genitive case) to call aloud (shriek, exclaim, intreat).
G2897: Probably from the same as harpazo; properly, a headache (as a seizure of pain) from drunkenness, i.e. (by implication) a debauch (by analogy, a glut).
G2898: Diminutive of a derivative of the base of keras; a skull ("cranium").
G2899: Of uncertain derivation; a margin, i.e. (specially), a fringe or tassel.
G29: to impress (into service), send (on an errand).
Of foreign origin (compare 'iggra'); properly, to be a courier, i.e. (by implication) to press into public service.
G2901: to strengthen, confirm; pass: to grow strong, become strong.
From krataios; to empower, i.e. (passively) increase in vigor.
G2902: to be strong, mighty, hence: to rule, be master, prevail; to obtain, take hold of; to hold, hold fast.
From kratos; to use strength, i.e. Seize or retain (literally or figuratively).
hold (by, fast), keep, lay hand (hold) on, obtain, retain, take (by).
G2903: most excellent, an official epithet, used in addressing a Roman of high rank, and in the second century one of equestrian (as distinguished from senatorial) rank.
Superlative of a derivative of kratos; strongest, i.e. (in dignity) very honorable.
G2904: dominion, strength, power; a mighty deed.
Perhaps a primary word; vigor ("great") (literally or figuratively).
G2906: (a) a shout, cry, clamor, (b) outcry, clamoring against another.
From krazo; an outcry (in notification, tumult or grief).
G2907: flesh; plur: pieces of flesh, kinds of flesh.
G2908: Neuter of an alternate form of kreitton; (as noun) better, i.e. Greater advantage.
G2909: Comparative of a derivative of kratos; stronger, i.e. (figuratively) better, i.e. Nobler.
G291: Ampliatus (Amplias), a male member of the church at Rome, probably of the imperial household.
Contracted for Latin ampliatus (enlarged); Amplias, a Roman Christian.
G2910: to hang, hang up, suspend; mid: to be hanging, hang.
A prolonged form of a primary verb; to hang.
G2911: From kremannumi; overhanging, i.e. A precipice.
G2912: a Cretan, an inhabitant of Crete.
From Krete; a Cretan, i.e. Inhabitant of Crete.
G2913: Crescens, a Christian, coadjutor of Paul.
Of Latin origin; growing; Cresces (i.e. Crescens), a Christian.
G2914: Crete, an island in the Mediterranean.
Of uncertain derivation; Crete, an island in the Mediterranean.
G2917: (a) a judgment, a verdict; sometimes implying an adverse verdict, a condemnation, (b) a case at law, a lawsuit.
From krino; a decision (the function or the effect, for or against ("crime")).
avenge, condemned, condemnation, damnation, + go to law, judgment.
G2918: a lily growing wild, variously identified with the red anemone, the whole lily, the sword lily.
Perhaps a prim word; a lily.
G2919: (a) to judge, whether in a law-court or privately: sometimes with cognate nouns emphasizing the notion of the verb, (b) to decide, to think (it) good.
Properly, to distinguish, i.e. Decide (mentally or judicially); by implication, to try, condemn, punish.
avenge, conclude, condemn, damn, decree, determine, esteem, judge, go to (sue at the) law, ordain, call in question, sentence to, think.
G292: to ward off, defend myself against, resist, defend, assist.
Middle voice of a primary verb; to ward off (for oneself), i.e. Protect.
G2920: judging, judgment, decision, sentence; generally: divine judgment; accusation.
Decision (subjectively or objectively, for or against); by extension, a tribunal; by implication, justice (especially, divine law).
G2921: Crispus, ruler of the synagogue at Corinth, converted and baptized by Paul.
Of Latin origin; "crisp"; Crispus, a Corinthian.
G2922: criterion; a law-court; a law-case before an arbiter; a cause, controversy.
Neuter of a presumed derivative of krites; a rule of judging ("criterion"), i.e. (by implication) a tribunal.
G2923: From krino; a judge (genitive case or specially).
G2924: critical, able to judge or discern.
G2925: to knock, beat a door with a stick, to gain admittance.
Apparently a primary verb; to rap.
G2926: a cellar, vault, hidden place, crypt.
Feminine of kruptos; a hidden place, i.e. Cellar ("crypt").
G2927: hidden, secret; as subst: the hidden (secret) things (parts), the inward nature (character).
G2928: A primary verb; to conceal (properly, by covering).
G2929: to be clear as crystal, brilliant like crystal.
From krustallos; to make (i.e. Intransitively, resemble) ice ("crystallize").
G293: prop: something thrown around; a fishing-net, drag-net.
From a compound of the base of amphoteros and ballo; a (fishing) net (as thrown about the fish).
G2930: From a derivative of kruos (frost); ice, i.e. (by analogy) rock "crystal".
G2932: (a) to acquire, win, get, purchase, buy, (b) to possess, win mastery over.
A primary verb; to get, i.e. Acquire (by any means; own).
G2933: a piece of landed property, a field; plur: possessions, property, possibly landed property, property in land.
From ktaomai; an acquirement, i.e. Estate.
G2934: a beast of burden (generally, a horse or mule) either for riding or for carrying loads on its back, or for yoking to a cart or carriage.
From ktaomai; property, i.e. (specially) a domestic animal.
G2936: to create, form, shape, make, always of God.
Probably akin to ktaomai (through the idea of proprietorship of the manufacturer); to fabricate, i.e. Found (form originally).
G2937: (often of the founding of a city), (a) abstr: creation, (b) concr: creation, creature, institution; always of Divine work, (c) an institution, ordinance.
From ktizo; original formation (properly, the act; by implication, the thing, literally or figuratively).
G2938: From ktizo; an original formation (concretely), i.e. Product (created thing).
G2939: (often of the founder of a city), creator, God.
From ktizo; a founder, i.e. God (as author of all things).
G294: From the base of amphoteros and hennumi (to invest); to enrobe.
G2940: (lit: playing with dice, gaming, hence) trickery, sleight.
From kubos (a "cube", i.e. Die for playing); gambling, i.e. (figuratively) artifice or fraud.
G2941: From kubernao (of Latin origin, to steer); pilotage, i.e. (figuratively) directorship (in the church).
G2942: a steersman, pilot; met: a guide, governor.
From the same as kubernesis; helmsman, i.e. (by implication) captain.
G2943: in a circle round, round about.
Adverb from the same as kukloi; from the circle, i.e. All around.
G2944: From the same as kukloi; to encircle, i.e. Surround.
G2945: As if dative case of kuklos (a ring, "cycle"; akin to kulioo); i.e. In a circle (by implication, of en), i.e. (adverbially) all around.
G2946: From kulioo; a wallow (the effect of rolling), i.e. Filth.
G2947: From the base of kuma (through the idea of circularity; compare kukloi, heilisso); to roll about.
G2948: crippled, lame, especially in the hands.
From the same as kulioo; rocking about, i.e. Crippled (maimed, in feet or hands).
G2949: From kuo (to swell (with young), i.e. Bend, curve); a billow (as bursting or toppling).
G295: Amphipolis, a leading city of Macedonia.
From the base of amphoteros and polis; a city surrounded by a river; Amphipolis, a place in Macedonia.
G2950: From a derivative of the base of kuma; a "cymbal" (as hollow).
G2951: cumin, a plant used as a spice.
Of foreign origin (compare kammon); dill or fennel ("cummin").
G2952: a little dog, a house dog.
Neuter of a presumed derivative of kuon; a puppy.
G2953: From Kupros; a Cyprian (Cypriot), i.e. Inhabitant of Cyprus.
G2954: Cyprus, an island at the east end of the Mediterranean Sea.
Of uncertain origin; Cyprus, an island in the Mediterranean.
G2955: to bend, stoop down, bow the head.
Probably from the base of kuma; to bend forward.
G2956: From Kurene; i.e. Cyrenaean, i.e. Inhabitant of Cyrene.
G2957: Cyrene, a district west of Egypt on the Mediterranean coast, forming with Crete a Roman province.
Of uncertain derivation; Cyrene, a region of Africa.
G2958: Cyrenius or Quirinius, governor of Syria.
Of Latin origin; Cyrenius (i.e. Quirinus), a Roman.
G2959: Feminine of kurios; Cyria, a Christian woman.
G296: prop: a road around anything; the street of a village.
From the base of amphoteros and hodos; a fork in the road.
G2960: of the Lord, special to the Lord.
From kurios; belonging to the Lord (Jehovah or Jesus).
G2961: have dominion over, lord, be lord of, exercise lordship over.
G2962: From kuros (supremacy); supreme in authority, i.e. (as noun) controller; by implication, Master (as a respectful title).
G2963: (a) abstr: lordship, (b) concr: divine or angelic lordship, domination, dignity, usually with reference to a celestial hierarchy.
From kurios; mastery, i.e. (concretely and collectively) rulers.
G2964: to ratify, confirm, make valid, reaffirm, assure.
From the same as kurios; to make authoritative, i.e. Ratify.
G2965: a dog, universally despised in the East.
A primary word; a dog ("hound") (literally or figuratively).
G2966: a limb, member of a body; fig: a corpse, carcass.
From the base of kolazo; a limb of the body (as if lopped).
G2967: to prevent, debar, hinder; with infin: from doing so and so.
From the base of kolazo; to estop, i.e. Prevent (by word or act).
forbid, hinder, keep from, let, not suffer, withstand.
G2968: From keimai; a hamlet (as if laid down).
G2969: a large village, a city which in constitution has only the status of a village; a country town.
From kome and polis; an unwalled city.
G2970: From keimai; a carousal (as if letting loose).
G2971: a gnat, mosquito, referred to proverbially as something small.
Apparently a derivative of the base of kentron and a derivative of optanomai; a mosquito (from its stinging proboscis).
G2972: Cos, an island in the Aegean Sea, south-west of Asia Minor.
Of uncertain origin; Cos, an island in the Mediterranean.
G2973: Cosam, son of Elmadam and father of Addi.
Of Hebrew origin (compare qecem); Cosam (i.e. Kosam) an Israelite.
G2974: From kopto; blunted, i.e. (figuratively) of hearing (deaf) or speech (dumb).
G2975: (a) to obtain (receive) by lot, lot (turn) is, (b) to draw lots.
A prolonged form of a primary verb, which is only used as an alternate in certain tenses; to lot, i.e. Determine (by implication, receive) especially by lot.
his lot be, cast lots, obtain.
G2976: Lazarus, Eliezer, (a) the beggar, (b) the brother of Martha and Mary, of Bethany.
Probably of Hebrew origin (El'azar); Lazarus (i.e. Elazar), the name of two Israelites (one imaginary).
G2978: a sudden storm, squall, whirlwind, hurricane.
G298: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of momaomai; unblamable.
G2980: (to talk, chatter in classical Greek, but in NT a more dignified word) to speak, say.
A prolonged form of an otherwise obsolete verb; to talk, i.e. Utter words.
preach, say, speak (after), talk, tell, utter. Compare lego.
G2981: (in classical Greek: babble, chattering) speech, talk; manner of speech, dialect.
G2982: Or lamma lam-mah'; of Hebrew origin (mah with prepositional prefix); lama (i.e. Why).
G2983: (a) to receive, get, (b) to take, lay hold of.

A prolonged form of a primary verb, which is use only as an alternate in certain tenses; to take (in very many applications, literally and figuratively (properly objective or active, to get hold of; whereas dechomai is rather subjective or passive, to have…
accept, + be amazed, assay, attain, bring, X when I call, catch, come on (X unto), + forget, have, hold, obtain, receive (X after), take (away, up).
G2984: (Hebrew), Lamech, son of Methuselah and father of Noah.
Of Hebrew origin (Lemek); Lamech (i.e. Lemek), a patriarch.
G2986: From the same as lampas; radiant; by analogy, limpid; figuratively, magnificent or sumptuous (in appearance).
bright, clear, gay, goodly, gorgeous, white.
G2988: Adverb from lampros; brilliantly, i.e. Figuratively, luxuriously.
G2989: A primary verb; to beam, i.e. Radiate brilliancy (literally or figuratively).
G299: From a (as a negative particle) and momos; unblemished (literally or figuratively).
without blame (blemish, fault, spot), faultless, unblamable.
G2990: to be hidden (concealed), lie hid, escape notice, sometimes with acc. of person from whom concealment takes place; to do so and so unconsciously, unknown to myself, to shut eyes to so and so.
A prolonged form of a primary verb, which is used only as an alternate in certain tenses; to lie hid (literally or figuratively); often used adverbially, unwittingly.
be hid, be ignorant of, unawares.
G2991: From a compound of las (a stone) and the base of xeros (in its original sense of scraping); rock-quarried.
G2992: (a) a people, characteristically of God's chosen people, first the Jews, then the Christians, (b) sometimes, but rarely, the people, the crowd.
Apparently a primary word; a people (in general; thus differing from demos, which denotes one's own populace).
G2993: Laodicea, a city in the Lycos valley in the Roman province Asia, near Colossae and Hierapolis.
From a compound of laos and dike; Laodicia, a place in Asia Minor.
G2994: a Laodicean, an inhabitant of Laodicea.
From Laodikeia; a Laodicean, i.e. Inhabitant of Laodicia.
G2996: Lasea, a city in Crete, about the middle of the south coast.
Of uncertain origin; Lasaea, a place in Crete.
G2997: to burst asunder with a loud noise.
A strengthened form of a primary verb, which only occurs in this and another prolonged form as alternate in certain tenses; to crack open (from a fall).
G2998: From the same as the first part of laxeutos and the base of tomoteros; to quarry.
G2999: service rendered to God, perhaps simply: worship.
From latreuo; ministration of God, i.e. Worship.
G3: Abaddon, Destroyer (i.e. Destroying Angel) or place of destruction (personified).
Of Hebrew origin ('abaddown); a destroying angel.
G30: From aggos (a pail, perhaps as bent; compare the base of agkale); a receptacle.
G300: Amon (Amos), son of Manasseh and father of Josiah, an ancestor of Jesus.
Of Hebrew origin ('Amown); Amon, an Israelite.
G3000: to serve, especially God, perhaps simply: to worship.
From latris (a hired menial); to minister (to God), i.e. Render religious homage.
G3002: Lebbaeus, a pet-name for Thaddaeus, one of the twelve apostles of Jesus; the full form of the name is not known.
Of uncertain origin; Lebbaeus, a Christian.
G3003: properly: a division of the Roman army, numbering about 6,000 infantry with additional cavalry; hence: a very large number; a legion.
Of Latin origin; a "legion", i.e. Roman regiment (figuratively).
G3004: (denoting speech in progress), (a) to say, speak; to mean, mention, tell, (b) to call, name, especially in the pass., (c) to tell, command.

A primary verb; properly, to "lay" forth, i.e. (figuratively) relate (in words (usually of systematic or set discourse; whereas epo and phemi generally refer to an individual expression or speech respectively; while rheo is properly to break silence merely,…
ask, bid, boast, call, describe, give out, name, put forth, say(-ing, on), shew, speak, tell, utter.
G3006: Apparently a primary word; smooth, i.e. "level".
G3007: (earlier: to leave behind, abandon), (a) to be wanting, (b) mid: e.g. with gen: to come behind (in a race), be left behind in, fall short of (some standard), be wanting in.
A primary verb; to leave, i.e. (intransitively or passively) to fail or be absent.
G3008: to act in the public service, render service, minister, in the widest sense, of some special public religious service, but also of the service of priests and Levites.
From leitourgos; to be a public servant, i.e. (by analogy) to perform religious or charitable functions (worship, obey, relieve).
G3009: a charitable gift, public service in the widest sense; service as of priest or Levite ritual.
From leitourgeo; public function (as priest ("liturgy") or almsgiver).
G301: Amos, son of Manasseh and father of Josiah, an ancestor of Jesus.
Of Hebrew origin ('Amowts); Amos, an Israelite.
G3010: From the same as leitourgeo; functional publicly ("liturgic"); i.e. Beneficient.
G3011: a minister, servant, of an official character; of priests and Levites.
From a derivative of laos and ergon; a public servant, i.e. A functionary in the Temple or Gospel, or (genitive case) a worshipper (of God) or benefactor (of man).
G3012: Of Latin origin; a "linen" cloth, i.e. Apron.
G3013: a scale, a scaly substance thrown off from the body.
G3014: From the same as lepis; scaliness, i.e. "leprosy".
G3015: From the same as lepra; scaly, i.e. Leprous (a leper).
G3016: a small piece of money, probably the smallest piece of money.
Neuter of a derivative of the same as lepis; something scaled (light), i.e. A small coin.
G3017: (Hebrew), Levi, (a) an ancestor of Jesus, (b) another ancestor of Jesus, (c) third son of Jacob, the patriarch, and founder of a tribe named after him, (d) son of Alphaeus, and called Matthew, a revenue officer and one…
Of Hebrew origin (Leviy); Levi, the name of three Israelites.
G3018: (Hebrew), Levi, son of Alphaeus, the publican.
A form of Leui; Lewis (i.e. Levi), a Christian.
G3019: a Levite, properly a man of the tribe of Levi; hence: a priest's assistant, an under priest, as the members of that tribe were charged with this duty.
From Leui; a Levite, i.e. Descendant of Levi.
G302: an untranslatable word (under the circumstances, in that case, anyhow), the general effect of which is to make a statement contingent, which would otherwise be definite: it is thus regularly used with the subjunctive…
A primary particle, denoting a supposition, wish, possibility or uncertainty.
(what-, where-, wither-, who-)soever. Usually unexpressed except by the subjunctive or potential mood. Also contracted for ean.
G3020: belonging to the tribe of Levi; Levitical.
From Leuites; Levitic, i.e. Relating to the Levites.
G3025: Apparently a primary word; a trough, i.e. Wine-vat.
G3026: Apparently a primary word; twaddle, i.e. An incredible story.
G303: prep. Rare in NT; prop: upwards, up; among, between; in turn; apiece, by; as a prefix: up, to, anew, back.

and, apiece, by, each, every (man), in, through. In compounds (as a prefix) it often means (by implication) repetition, intensity, reversal, etc.
G3030: Of foreign origin (lbownah); the incense-tree, i.e. (by implication) incense itself.
G3031: From libanos; frankincense, i.e. (by extension) a censer for burning it.
G3032: a freedman, one of the class of manumitted slaves; a synagogue at Jerusalem appears to have been reserved for them.
Of Latin origin; a Roman freedman.
G3033: "the west bank of the Nile", Libya, a region in N. Africa.
Probably from lips; Libye, a region of Africa.
G3035: From lithos; stony, i.e. Made of stone.
G3036: to stone, cast stones (at), kill by stoning.
From a compound of lithos and ballo; to throw stones, i.e. Lapidate.
G3037: a stone; met: of Jesus as the chief stone in a building.
Apparently a primary word; a stone (literally or figuratively).
G3038: (adj: paved with stone), a mosaic pavement.
From lithos and a derivative of stronnumi; stone-strewed, i.e. A tessellated mosaic on which the Roman tribunal was placed.
G3039: to crush to powder, scatter like chaff.
From likmos, the equivalent of liknon (a winnowing fan or basket); to winnow, i.e. (by analogy), to triturate.
G304: a step, a flight of steps; the well-known stairs leading up from the temple to the tower of Antonia at Jerusalem.
G3040: Apparently a primary word; a harbor.
G3041: Probably from limen (through the idea of nearness of shore); a pond (large or small).
G3042: Probably from leipo (through the idea of destitution); a scarcity of food.
G3043: Probably a primary word; flax, i.e. (by implication) "linen".
G3044: Perhaps from linon; Linus, a Christian.
G3046: a pound (in weight, by Rom. standards).
Of Latin origin (libra); a pound in weight.
G3047: the south-west wind, and thus the quarter from which it comes.
Probably from leibo (to pour a "libation"); the south(- west) wind (as bringing rain, i.e. (by extension) the south quarter).
G3048: a collection, collecting (of money), particularly of an irregular local contribution for religious purposes.
From logos (in the commercial sense); a contribution.
G3049: to reckon, count, charge with; reason, decide, conclude; think, suppose.
Middle voice from logos; to take an inventory, i.e. Estimate (literally or figuratively).
conclude, (ac-)count (of), + despise, esteem, impute, lay, number, reason, reckon, suppose, think (on).
G305: to go up, mount, ascend; of things: to rise, spring up, come up.
From ana and the base of basis; to go up (literally or figuratively).
arise, ascend (up), climb (go, grow, rise, spring) up, come (up).
G3050: (a) reasonable, rational, (b) metaphorical, as contrasted with the literal.
G3051: plur: oracles, divine responses or utterances (it can include the entire Old Testament).
Neuter of logios; an utterance (of God).
G3052: From logos; fluent, i.e. An orator.
G3053: From logizomai; computation, i.e. (figuratively) reasoning (conscience, conceit).
G3054: From a compound of logos and machomai; to be disputatious (on trifles).
G3055: contention about words, an unprofitable controversy.
From the same as logomacheo; disputation about trifles ("logomachy").
G3056: a word (as embodying an idea), a statement, a speech.

account, cause, communication, X concerning, doctrine, fame, X have to do, intent, matter, mouth, preaching, question, reason, + reckon, remove, say(-ing), shew, X speaker, speech, talk, thing, +…
G3058: to revile a person to his face, abuse insultingly.
From loidoros; to reproach, i.e. Vilify.
G306: to postpone, defer, especially: to postpone the trial of.
Middle voice from ana and ballo; to put off (for oneself).
G3060: From loidos (mischief); abusive, i.e. A blackguard.
G3061: Of uncertain affinity; a plague (literally, the disease, or figuratively, a pest).
G3062: left, left behind, the remainder, the rest, the others.
Masculine plural of a derivative of leipo; remaining ones.
other, which remain, remnant, residue, rest.
G3063: finally, from now on, henceforth, beyond that.
Neuter singular of the same as loipoy; something remaining (adverbially).
besides, finally, furthermore, (from) henceforth, moreover, now, + it remaineth, then.
G3064: Genitive case singular of the same as loipoy; remaining time.
G3065: Lucas, Luke, Christian physician and writer of the Third Gospel and Acts.
Contracted from Latin Lucanus; Lucas, a Christian.
G3066: Lucius, (a) of Cyrene, an early Christian, in the church of Antioch, by some identified with the evangelist Luke, (b) a Christian with Paul at Corinth, by some identified with (a).
Of Latin origin; illuminative; Lucius, a Christian.
G3067: a bath (of water, not the vessel), water for washing, washing.
From louo; a bath, i.e. (figuratively), baptism.
G3068: (lit. or merely ceremonially), to wash, bathe (the body); mid: of washing, bathing one's self; met: to cleanse from sin.
A primary verb; to bathe (the whole person; whereas nipto means to wet a part only, and pluno to wash, cleanse garments exclusively).
G3069: Lydda, Diospolis, Lod (modern Ludd), a city on the way to Joppa within a day's journey of Jerusalem.
Of Hebrew origin (Lod); Lydda (i.e. Lod), a place in Palestine.
G307: to draw up, as a net to shore.
From ana and a derivative of the base of basis; to cause to go up, i.e. Haul (a net).
G3070: Lydia, a lady resident of Philippi, native of Thyatira in Lydia (Asia Minor), and engaged in the clothing trade.
Properly, feminine of Ludios (of foreign origin) (a Lydian, in Asia Minor).
G3071: Lycaonia, the country of the Lykaones, a district of Asia Minor, comprised within the Roman province Galatia and including the cities of Derbe and Lystra.
Perhaps remotely from lukos; Lycaonia, a region of Asia Minor.
G3072: Adverb from a derivative of Lukaonia; Lycaonistically, i.e. In the language of the Lycaonians.
G3073: Lycia, a small Roman province on the south coast of Asia Minor.
Probably remotely from lukos; Lycia, a province of Asia Minor.
G3074: a wolf, of perhaps a jackal; often applied to persons of wolfish proclivities.
Perhaps akin to the base of leukos (from the whitish hair); a wolf.
G3075: Middle voice from a probably derivative of luo (meaning filth); properly, to soil, i.e. (figuratively) insult (maltreat).
G3076: From lupe; to distress; reflexively or passively, to be sad.
cause grief, grieve, be in heaviness, (be) sorrow(-ful), be (make) sorry.
G3077: pain of body or mind, grief, sorrow.
G3078: "ending sorrow", Lysanias, a governor of Abilene.

G3079: Claudius Lysias, a Roman tribune of the soldiers in Jerusalem.
Of uncertain affinity; Lysias, a Roman.
G308: From ana and blepo; to look up; by implication, to recover sight.
G3080: From luo; a loosening, i.e. (specially), divorce.
G3081: it is advantageous to, it profits.
Third person singular present indicative active of a derivative of a compound of lusis and telos; impersonally, it answers the purpose, i.e. Is advantageous.
G3082: Lystra, a Lycaonian city in the southern part of the Roman province Galatia.
Of uncertain origin; Lystra, a place in Asia Minor.
G3083: the purchasing money for manumitting slaves, a ransom, the price of ransoming; especially the sacrifice by which expiation is effected, an offering of expiation.
From luo; something to loosen with, i.e. A redemption price (figuratively, atonement).
G3084: to release on receipt of ransom; mid: to redeem, release by paying ransom, liberate.

G3085: (in the Old Testament: ransoming from imprisonment for debt, or from slavery, release from national misfortune, etc.), liberation, deliverance, release.
G3087: From luchnos; a lamp-stand (literally or figuratively).
G3088: From the base of leukos; a portable lamp or other illuminator (literally or figuratively).
G3089: (a) to loose, untie, release, (b) met: to break, destroy, set at naught, contravene; to break up a meeting, annul.

break (up), destroy, dissolve, (un-)loose, melt, put off. Compare rhegnumi.
G3090: Of uncertain origin; Lois, a Christian woman.
G3091: Of Hebrew origin (Lowt); Lot, a patriarch.
G3092: Probably of Hebrew origin; Maath, an Israelite.
G3093: Magadan, an unidentified place near the Sea of Galilee.

G3094: Magdalene, of Magdala, a place on the coast of the Sea of Galilee near Tiberias.
Feminine of a derivative of Magdala; a female Magdalene, i.e. Inhabitant of Magdala.
G3097: a Magian, an (Oriental) astrologer, by implication a magician.

G3098: (Hebrew), Magog, sometimes as name of a people, sometimes as name of a country in the Old Testament, probably the Scythians; hence: used in apocalyptic literature.
Of Hebrew origin (Magowg); Magog, a foreign nation, i.e. (figuratively) an Antichristian party.
G3099: (Hebrew), Midian, generally taken to mean or to include the peninsula of Sinai.
Of Hebrew origin (Midyan); Madian (i.e. Midian), a region of Arabia.
G31: From aggelos; an announcement, i.e. (by implication) precept.
G310: to shout upwards, cry out, raise voice.
From ana and boao; to halloo.
G3100: to make a disciple of, train in discipleship; pass: to be trained, discipled, instructed.

G3101: From manthano; a learner, i.e. Pupil.
G3102: Feminine from mathetes; a female pupil.

G3104: Probably of Hebrew origin; Mainan, an Israelite.
G3105: to be raving mad, speak as a madman.

As if from xeo (properly, to smooth; by implication, (of friction) to boil or heat); a vessel (as fashioned or for cooking) (or perhaps by corruption from the Latin sextarius, the sixth of a modius, i.e. About a pint), i.e. (specially), a measure for liquids…
G3583: to dry up, parch, be ripened, wither, waste away.
From xeros; to desiccate; by implication, to shrivel, to mature.
dry up, pine away, be ripe, wither (away).
G3584: From the base of xestes (through the idea of scorching); arid; by implication, shrunken, earth (as opposed to water).
G3586: anything made of wood, a piece of wood, a club, staff; the trunk of a tree, used to support the cross-bar of a cross in crucifixion.
