From pros and lambano; to take to oneself, i.e. Use (food), lead (aside), admit (to friendship or hospitality).
G4356: a receiving, a taking to one's self, acceptance.
G4357: to remain; to abide in, remain in, persist in, adhere to.
From pros and meno; to stay further, i.e. Remain in a place, with a person; figuratively, to adhere to, persevere in.
abide still, be with, cleave unto, continue in (with).
G4358: to bring (a ship) to anchor at.
From pros and a derivative of the same as horme (meaning to tie (anchor) or lull); to moor to, i.e. (by implication) land at.
G4359: From pros and opheilo; to be indebted additionally.
G436: to set against; to withstand, resist, oppose.
From anti and histemi; to stand against, i.e. Oppose.
G4360: to be displeased or offended with.
From pros and a form of ochtheo (to be vexed with something irksome); to feel indignant at.
G4361: From pros and the same as peinao; hungering further, i.e. Intensely hungry.
G4362: to fasten to, applied to Christ's being fastened to the cross.
From pros and pegnumi; to fasten to, i.e. (specially), to impale (on a cross).
G4363: (a) to fall down before, (b) to beat against, rush violently upon.
From pros and pipto; to fall towards, i.e. (gently) prostrate oneself (in supplication or homage), or (violently) to rush upon (in storm).
G4364: to attach to, take to oneself, to pretend.
Middle voice from pros and poieo; to do forward for oneself, i.e. Pretend (as if about to do a thing).
G4365: From pros and poreuomai; to journey towards, i.e. Approach (not the same as proporeuomai).
G4366: From pros and rhegnumi; to tear towards, i.e. Burst upon (as a tempest or flood).
G4367: (a) to instruct, command, (b) to appoint, assign.
From pros and tasso; to arrange towards, i.e. (figuratively) enjoin.
G4368: Feminine of a derivative of proistemi; a patroness, i.e. Assistant.
G4369: to place (put) to, add; to do again.
From pros and tithemi; to place additionally, i.e. Lay beside, annex, repeat.
add, again, give more, increase, lay unto, proceed further, speak to any more.
G437: to make a mutual agreement; to confess, acknowledge, formally admit, give thanks to.
From anti and the middle voice of homologeo; to confess in turn, i.e. Respond in praise.
G4370: From pros and trecho (including its alternate); to run towards, i.e. Hasten to meet or join.
G4371: anything eaten with bread, especially fish or meat.
Neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of pros and phago; something eaten in addition to bread, i.e. A relish (specially, fish; compare opsarion).
G4372: (originally: newly slaughtered, freshly killed), recent, new.
From pro and a derivative of sphazo; previously (recently) slain (fresh), i.e. (figuratively) lately made.
G4374: (a) to bring to, (b) characteristically: to offer (of gifts, sacrifices, etc).
From pros and phero (including its alternate); to bear towards, i.e. Lead to, tender (especially to God), treat.
bring (to, unto), deal with, do, offer (unto, up), present unto, put to.
G4375: From a presumed compound of pros and phileo; friendly towards, i.e. Acceptable.
G4376: From prosphero; presentation; concretely, an oblation (bloodless) or sacrifice.
G4377: to call to, summon; to call (out) to, address, give a speech to, harangue.
From pros and phoneo; to sound towards, i.e. Address, exclaim, summon.
G4378: a pouring upon, an effusion, a sprinkling.
From a comparative of pros and cheo (to pour); a shedding forth, i.e. Affusion.
G4379: From pros and psauo (to touch); to impinge, i.e. Lay a finger on (in order to relieve).
G438: bloom, possibly a reference to the bright flowers, such as poppies (among the grass).
G4380: From prosopoleptes; to favor an individual, i.e. Show partiality.
G4381: an accepter of a face, a respecter of persons.
From prosopon and lambano; an accepter of a face (individual), i.e. (specially), one exhibiting partiality.
G4383: From pros and ops (the visage, from optanomai); the front (as being towards view), i.e. The countenance, aspect, appearance, surface; by implication, presence, person.
(outward) appearance, X before, countenance, face, fashion, (men's) person, presence.
G4384: From pro and tasso; to pre-arrange, i.e. Prescribe.
G4385: to stretch out, tie up (for scourging), extend before.
From pro and teino (to stretch); to protend, i.e. Tie prostrate (for scourging).
G4386: Neuter of proteros as adverb (with or without the article); previously.
G4387: Comparative of pro; prior or previous.
G4388: Middle voice from pro and tithemi; to place before, i.e. (for oneself) to exhibit; (to oneself) to propose (determine).
G4389: Middle voice from pro and the base of trope; to turn forward for oneself, i.e. Encourage.
G439: a coal-fire, a heap of burning coals.
From anthrax; a bed of burning coals.
G4390: to run before, outrun, run in advance.
From pro and trecho (including its alternate); to run forward, i.e. Outstrip, precede.
G4391: to have been already, have been previously.
From pro and huparcho; to exist before, i.e. (adverbially) to be or do something previously.
G4392: From a compound of pro and phaino; an outward showing, i.e. Pretext.
G4393: From pro and phero; to bear forward, i.e. Produce.
G4394: prophecy, prophesying; the gift of communicating and enforcing revealed truth.
G4395: to foretell, prophesy; to set forth matter of divine teaching by special faculty.
From prophetes; to foretell events, divine, speak under inspiration, exercise the prophetic office.
G4396: a prophet (an interpreter or forth-teller of the divine will).
From a compound of pro and phemi; a foreteller ("prophet"); by analogy, an inspired speaker; by extension, a poet.
G4397: From prophetes; pertaining to a foreteller ("prophetic").
G4398: Feminine of prophetes; a female foreteller or an inspired woman.
G4399: From pro and phthano; to get an earlier start of, i.e. Anticipate.
G44: From the same as agkale; a hook (as bent).
G440: Of uncertain derivation; a live coal.
G4400: to put into the hand, to take into one's hand, to determine.
Middle voice from pro and a derivative of cheir; to handle for oneself in advance, i.e. (figuratively) to purpose.
G4401: From pro and cheirotoneo; to elect in advance.
G4402: Prochorus, one of the seven original deacons at Jerusalem.
From pro and choros; before the dance; Prochorus, a Christian.
G4403: Feminine of prumnus (hindmost); the stern of a ship.
G4404: early in the morning, at dawn.
Adverb from pro; at dawn; by implication, the day-break watch.
G4405: Feminine of a derivative of proi as noun; day-dawn.
G4406: From proi; dawning, i.e. (by analogy) autumnal (showering, the first of the rainy season).
G4407: From proi; pertaining to the dawn, i.e. Matutinal.
G4408: Feminine of a presumed derivative of pro as noun; the prow, i.e. Forward part of a vessel.
G4409: to have preeminence, be chief, be first.
From protos; to be first (in rank or influence).
G441: desirous of pleasing men, a renderer of service to human beings (as opposed to God).
From anthropos and aresko; man-courting, i.e. Fawning.
G4410: From protos and kathedra; a sitting first (in the front row), i.e. Preeminence in council.
G4411: the chief place at a banquet or table.
From protos and klisia; a reclining first (in the place of honor) at the dinner-bed, i.e. Preeminence at meals.
G4412: first, in the first place, before, formerly.
Neuter of protos as adverb (with or without ho); firstly (in time, place, order, or importance).
before, at the beginning, chiefly (at, at the) first (of all).
G4413: Contracted superlative of pro; foremost (in time, place, order or importance).
before, beginning, best, chief(-est), first (of all), former.
G4414: one who stands in the front rank, hence: a leader, ringleader, chief.
From protos and histemi; one standing first in the ranks, i.e. A captain (champion).
G4415: the birthright, the rights of the first-born.
G4416: From protos and the alternate of tikto; first-born (usually as noun, literally or figuratively).
G4417: to stumble, fall, sin, err, transgress.
A form of pipto; to trip, i.e. (figuratively) to err, sin, fail (of salvation).
G4419: a little wing, (anything like a wing) a battlement.
Neuter of a presumed derivative of pterux; a winglet, i.e. (figuratively) extremity (top corner).
G442: belonging to human beings (especially as contrasted with God), human (as contrasted with divine).
human, common to man, man(-kind), (man-)kind, men's, after the manner of men.
G4420: From a derivative of petomai (meaning a feather); a wing.
G4422: to terrify, scare, strike with panic.
Probably akin to the alternate of pipto (through the idea of causing to fall) or to petomai (through that of causing to fly away); to scare.
G4424: Ptolemais, a coast city of Phoenicia, midway between Tyre and Caesarea.
From Ptolemaios (Ptolemy, after whom it was named); Ptolemais, a place in Palestine.
G4425: a simple wooden pitchfork; a winnowing-shovel or fan.
From ptuo; a winnowing-fork (as scattering like spittle).
G4426: From a presumed derivative of ptuo (and thus akin to ptoeo); to frighten.
G4428: to fold, roll up (as a scroll).
Probably akin to petannumi (to spread; and thus apparently allied to petomai through the idea of expansion, and to ptuo through that of flattening; compare pateo); to fold, i.e. Furl a scroll.
G4429: A primary verb (compare ptusso); to spit.
G443: From anthropos and kteino (to kill); a manslayer.
G4430: a fall; a carcass, corpse, dead body.
From the alternate of pipto; a ruin, i.e. (specially), lifeless body (corpse, carrion).
G4431: From the alternate of pipto; a crash, i.e. Downfall (literally or figuratively).
G4432: From ptocheuo; beggary, i.e. Indigence (literally or figuratively).
G4433: to be in poverty, be a beggar.
From ptochos; to be a beggar, i.e. (by implication) to become indigent (figuratively).
G4434: poor, destitute, spiritually poor, either in a good sense (humble devout persons) or bad.

From ptosso (to crouch); akin to ptoeo and the alternate of pipto); a beggar (as cringing), i.e. Pauper (strictly denoting absolute or public mendicancy, although also used in a qualified or relative sense; whereas penes properly means only straitened…
G4435: From a primary pux (the fist as a weapon); the clenched hand, i.e. (only in dative case as adverb) with the fist (hard scrubbing).
G4436: a divining spirit, Python, called after the Pythian serpent said to have guarded the oracle at Delphi and been slain by Apollo.
From Putho (the name of the region where Delphi, the seat of the famous oracle, was located); a Python, i.e. (by analogy, with the supposed diviner there) inspiration (soothsaying).
G4437: From the same as skenopoios; clasped (thick), i.e. (figuratively) frequent; neuter plural (as adverb) frequently.
G4438: From a derivative of the same as pugme; to box (with the fist), i.e. Contend (as a boxer) at the games (figuratively).
G4439: Apparently a primary word; a gate, i.e. The leaf or wing of a folding entrance (literally or figuratively).
G444: a man, one of the human race.
From aner and ops (the countenance; from optanomai); man-faced, i.e. A human being.
G4440: a large gate; a gateway, porch, vestibule.
From pule; a gate-way, door-way of a building or city; by implication, a portal or vestibule.
G4441: to ask, inquire, ascertain by inquiry, understand.

Middle voice prolonged from a primary putho (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); to question, i.e. Ascertain by inquiry (as a matter of information merely; and thus differing from erotao, which properly means a request as a favor; and from…
G4442: fire; the heat of the sun, lightning; fig: strife, trials; the eternal fire.
A primary word; "fire" (literally or figuratively, specially, lightning).
G4443: a fire, pile of burning fuel.
G4444: Apparently a primary word ("burgh"); a tower or castle.
G4445: to be on fire, to be ill of a fever.
From pura; to be on fire, i.e. (specially), to have a fever.
G4446: From puresso; inflamed, i.e. (by implication) feverish (as noun, fever).
G4447: From pura; fiery, i.e. (by implication) flaming.
G4448: pass: to burn, be set on fire, be inflamed; glow with heat, be purified by fire.
From pur; to kindle, i.e. (passively) to be ignited, glow (literally), be refined (by implication), or (figuratively) to be inflamed (with anger, grief, lust).
burn, fiery, be on fire, try.
G445: to act as proconsul, be a deputy.
From anthupatos; to act as proconsul.
G4450: From pur; fire-like, i.e. (specially), flame- colored.
G4451: From puroo; ignition, i.e. (specially), smelting (figuratively, conflagration, calamity as a test).
G4452: Another form of the base of pos; an enclitic particle of indefiniteness; yet, even; used only in the comparative. See medepo, mepo, oudepo, oupo, popote..
yet, even; used only in the comparative. See medepo, mepo, oudepo, oupo, popote.
G4453: to exchange or barter, to sell.
Probably ultimately from pelomai (to be busy, to trade); to barter (as a pedlar), i.e. To sell.
G4454: Apparently a primary word; a "foal" or "filly", i.e. (specially), a young ass.
G4455: From po and pote; at any time, i.e. (with negative particle) at no time.
at any time, + never (...to any man), + yet, never man.
G4456: Apparently from poros (a kind of stone); to petrify, i.e. (figuratively) to indurate (render stupid or callous).
G4457: a covering with a callous, blindness.
G4458: Adverb from the base of pou; an enclitic particle of indefiniteness of manner; somehow or anyhow; used only in composition.
haply, by any (some) means, perhaps. See ei pos, mepos. Compare pos.
G4459: how, in what manner, by what means.
Adverb from the base of pou; an interrogative particle of manner; in what way? (sometimes the question is indirect, how?); also as exclamation, how much!.
how, after (by) what manner (means), that. (Occasionally unexpressed in English).
G446: From anti and a superlative of huper; instead of the highest officer, i.e. (specially) a Roman proconsul.
G4460: Rahab, a Canaanitess, who rescued the Hebrew spies at Jericho.
Of Hebrew origin (Rachab); Raab (i.e. Rachab), a Canaanitess.
G4461: Rabbi, master, teacher; a title of respect often applied to Christ.
Of Hebrew origin (rab with pronominal suffix); my master, i.e Rabbi, as an official title of honor.
G4462: Rabbi, master, teacher; a title of respect often applied to Christ.
Or rhabbouni (hrab-boo-nee') of Chaldee origin; corresponding to rhabbi.
G4463: From rhabdos; to strike with a stick, i.e. Bastinado.
G4464: a rod, staff, staff of authority, scepter.
From the base of rhapizo; a stick or wand (as a cudgel, a cane or a baton of royalty).
G4465: a rod holder, (a Roman) lictor (one holding the rod of office).
From rhabdos and echo; a rod- (the Latin fasces) holder, i.e. A Roman lictor (constable or executioner).
G4466: Ragau (or Reu), an ancestor of Jesus.
Of Hebrew origin (r'uw); Ragau (i.e. Reu), a patriarch.
G4467: a careless action, an act of villainy.
From a comparative of rhaidios (easy, i.e. Reckless) and ergon; easy-going behavior, i.e. (by extension) a crime.
G4468: ease in doing, laziness, recklessness, wickedness.
From the same as rhaidiourgema; recklessness, i.e. (by extension) malignity.
G4469: Of Chaldee origin (compare reyq); O empty one, i.e. Thou worthless (as a term of utter vilification).
G447: to send up, produce, send back; to let go; to relax, loosen, hence met: to give up, desist from.
From ana and hiemi (to send); to let up, i.e. (literally) slacken or (figuratively) desert, desist from.
G4470: a piece of cloth, a remnant torn off.
From rhegnumi; a "rag," i.e. Piece of cloth.
G4471: Rama, a place in Ephraim, two hours north of Jerusalem.
Of Hebrew origin (Ramah); Rama (i.e. Ramah), a place in Palestine.
G4472: to sprinkle, cleanse ceremonially by sprinkling.
From a derivative of rhaino (to sprinkle); to render besprinkled, i.e. Asperse (ceremonially or figuratively).
G4474: to strike with a rod, to strike with the palm of the hand.
From a derivative of a primary rhepo (to let fall, "rap"); to slap.
smite (with the palm of the hand). Compare tupto.
G4475: a blow (with a stick or the palm of the hand).
(+ strike with the) palm of the hand, smite with the hand.
G4476: From a primary rhapto (to sew; perhaps rather akin to the base of rhapizo through the idea of puncturing); a needle.
G4477: Rahab, a Canaanitess, who rescued the Hebrew spies at Jericho.
From the same as Rhaab; Rachab, a Canaanitess.
G4478: Rachel, younger wife of the patriarch Jacob.
Of Hebrew origin (Rachel); Rachel, the wife of Jacob.
G4479: Rebecca, wife of the patriarch Isaac.
Of Hebrew origin (Ribqah); Rebecca (i.e. Ribkah), the wife of Isaac.
G448: From a (as a negative particle) and hileos; inexorable.
G4480: Of Latin origin; a rheda, i.e. Four-wheeled carriage (wagon for riding).
G4481: Rephan, the Saturn of later mythology.
By incorrect transliteration for a word of Hebrew origin (Kiyuwn); Remphan (i.e. Kijun), an Egyptian idol.
G4482: A primary verb; for some tenses of which a prolonged form rheuo (hryoo'-o) is used to flow ("run"; as water).
G4483: For certain tenses of which a prolonged form ereo (er-eh'-o) is used; and both as alternate for epo; perhaps akin (or identical) with rheo (through the idea of pouring forth); to utter, i.e. Speak or say.
command, make, say, speak (of). Compare lego.
G4484: Rhegium, a city in the south-west corner of Italy opposite Sicily (modern Reggio).
Of Latin origin; Rhegium, a place in Italy.
G4485: From rhegnumi; something torn, i.e. A fragment (by implication and abstractly, a fall).
G4486: to rend, break asunder; to break forth (into speech); to throw or dash down.

Or rhesso (hrace'-so) both prolonged forms of rheko (which appears only in certain forms, and is itself probably a strengthened form of agnumi (see in katagnumi)) to "break," "wreck" or "crack", i.e. (especially) to sunder (by separation of the parts;…
G4487: a thing spoken, (a) a word or saying of any kind, as command, report, promise, (b) a thing, matter, business.
From rheo; an utterance (individually, collectively or specially); by implication, a matter or topic (especially of narration, command or dispute); with a negative naught whatever.
G4488: Probably of Hebrew origin (apparently for Rphayah); Resa (i.e. Rephajah), an Israelite.
G4489: From rheo; a speaker, i.e. (by implication) a forensic advocate.
G449: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of nipto; without ablution.
G4490: expressly, explicitly, in so many words.
Adverb from a derivative of rheo; out-spokenly, i.e. Distinctly.
G4491: a root, shoot, source; that which comes from the root, a descendent.
Apparently a primary word; a "root" (literally or figuratively).
G4492: to cause to take root; met: to plant, fix firmly, establish.
From rhiza; to root (figuratively, become stable).
G4493: a glance, twinkle or flash of the eye; a rush of wind or flame; any rapid movement.
From rhipto; a jerk (of the eye, i.e. (by analogy) an instant).
G4494: to fan, generally to make a breeze.
From a derivative of rhipto (meaning a fan or bellows); to breeze up, i.e. (by analogy) to agitate (into waves).
G4495: to throw off or away, cast, hurl.
From a derivative of rhipto; to toss up.
G4496: to throw, cast, toss, set down; pass: to be dispersed.

A primary verb (perhaps rather akin to the base of rhapizo, through the idea of sudden motion); to fling (properly, with a quick toss, thus differing from ballo, which denotes a deliberate hurl; and from teino (see in ekteino), which indicates an extended…
G4497: Rehoboam, son of Solomon, and King of Israel.
Of Hebrew origin (Rchab'am); Roboam (i.e. Rechobam), an Israelite.
G4498: Rhoda, a maidservant in the house of John Mark's mother at Jerusalem.
Probably for rhode (a rose); Rode, a servant girl.
G4499: Rhodes, an island in the Aegean sea, south-west of Asia Minor.
Probably from rhodon (a rose); Rhodus, an island of the Mediterranean.
G45: From the same as agkale; an "anchor" (as crooked).
G450: to raise up, set up; to rise from among (the) dead; to arise, appear.
From ana and histemi; to stand up (literal or figurative, transitive or intransitive).
arise, lift up, raise up (again), rise (again), stand up(-right).
G4500: with a great noise, with a rushing sound.
Adverb from a derivative of rhoizos (a whir); whizzingly, i.e. With a crash.
G4501: a sword, scimitar; fig: war, piercing grief.
Probably of foreign origin; a sabre, i.e. A long and broad cutlass (any weapon of the kind, literally or figuratively).
G4502: Reuben, eldest son of the patriarch Jacob and founder of a tribe.
Of Hebrew origin (r'uwben); Ruben (i.e. Reuben), an Israelite.
G4503: Ruth, a Moabitess and an ancestor of Christ.
Of Hebrew origin (Ruwth); Ruth, a Moabitess.
G4504: Rufus, a Christian man in Rome, probably to be identified with the brother of Alexander and son of Simon of Cyrene.
Of Latin origin; red; Rufus, a Christian.
G4505: the rush (of a moving body), a (crowded) street.
Prolongation from rhoumai in its original sense; an alley or avenue (as crowded).
G4506: to rescue, deliver (from danger or destruction).
Middle voice of an obsolete verb, akin to rheo (through the idea of a current; compare rhusis); to rush or draw (for oneself), i.e. Rescue.
G4508: From rhupos; dirty, i.e. (relatively) cheap or shabby; morally, wicked.
G4509: Of uncertain affinity; dirt, i.e. (morally) depravity.
G451: Anna, a prophetess, who visited the infant Jesus.
Of Hebrew origin (Channah); Anna, an Israelitess.
G4510: to be filthy; hence (morally): to be stained with sin.
From rhupos; to soil, i.e. (intransitively) to become dirty (morally).
G4511: From rhoumai in the sense of its congener rheo; a flux (of blood).
G4512: a wrinkle; fig: a spiritual defect, flaw.
From rhoumai; a fold (as drawing together), i.e. A wrinkle (especially on the face).
G4514: From Rhome; Romaean, i.e. Roman (as noun).
G4515: Adverb from a presumed derivative of Rhome; Romaistically, i.e. In the Latin language.
G4516: Rome, the capital of Italy and the Rom. Empire (named after Romulus, the legendary founder).
From the base of rhonnumi; strength; Roma, the capital of Italy.
G4517: to strengthen, render firm; imperative at the end of letters: farewell.
Prolongation from rhoomai (to dart; probably akin to rhoumai); to strengthen, i.e. (impersonal passive) have health (as a parting exclamation, good-bye).
G4518: Of Chaldee or (shbaq with pronominal suffix); thou hast left me; sabachthani (i.e. Shebakthani), a cry of distress.
G4519: Of Hebrew origin (tsaba' in feminine plural); armies; sabaoth (i.e. Tsebaoth), a military epithet of God.
G452: Of Hebrew origin (Chananyah); Annas (i.e. Ananias), an Israelite.
G4520: a keeping of the Sabbath, a Sabbath rest.
From a derivative of sabbaton; a "sabbatism", i.e. (figuratively) the repose of Christianity (as a type of heaven).
G4521: the Sabbath, the seventh day (of the week).

Of Hebrew origin (shabbath); the Sabbath (i.e. Shabbath), or day of weekly repose from secular avocations (also the observance or institution itself); by extension, a se'nnight, i.e. The interval between two Sabbaths; likewise the plural in all the above…
G4522: From a derivative of satto (to equip) meaning furniture, especially a pack-saddle (which in the East is merely a bag of netted rope); a "seine" for fishing.
G4523: a Sadducee, a member of the aristocratic party among the Jews, from whom the high-priests were almost invariably chosen.
Probably from Sadok; a Sadducaean (i.e. Tsadokian), or follower of a certain heretical Israelite.
G4524: Of Hebrew origin (Tsadowq); Sadoc (i.e. Tsadok), an Israelite.
G4525: to fawn upon, flatter, beguile; pass: to be perturbed.
Akin to seio; to wag (as a dog its tail fawningly), i.e. (generally) to shake (figuratively, disturb).
G4526: Of Hebrew origin (saq); "sack"-cloth, i.e. Mohair (the material or garments made of it, worn as a sign of grief).
G4527: Shelah, an ancestor of Christ, also Salmon, an ancestor of Christ.
Of Hebrew origin (Shelach); Sala (i.e. Shelach), a patriarch.
G4528: Of Hebrew origin (Sh'altiy'el); Salathiel (i.e. Shealtiel), an Israelite.
G4529: Salamis, a city at the eastern end of Cyprus.
Probably from salos (from the surge on the shore); Salamis, a place in Cyprus.
G453: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of noieo; unintelligent; by implication, sensual.
G4530: Probably from the same as saleuo; Salim, a place in Palestine.
G4531: to shake, excite, disturb in mind, stir up, drive away.
From salos; to waver, i.e. Agitate, rock, topple or (by implication) destroy; figuratively, to disturb, incite.
move, shake (together), which can(-not) be shaken, stir up.
G4532: Of Hebrew origin (Shalem); Salem (i.e. Shalem), a place in Palestine.
G4533: Salmon, son of Nahshon and father of Boaz.
Of Hebrew origin (Salmown); Salmon, an Israelite.
G4534: Salmone, a promontory on the east of Crete.
Perhaps of similar origin to Salamis; Salmone, a place in Crete.
G4535: the tossing of the sea in a tempest; agitation, rolling.
Probably from the base of saino; a vibration, i.e. (specially), billow.
G4536: a trumpet, the sound of a trumpet.
Perhaps from salos (through the idea of quavering or reverberation); a trumpet.
G4537: From salpigx; to trumpet, i.e. Sound a blast (literally or figuratively).
G4539: Salome, wife of Zebedee and mother of James and John, the apostles.
Probably of Hebrew origin; Salome (i.e. Shelomah), an Israelitess.
G454: From a compound of a (as a negative particle) and nous; stupidity; by implication, rage.
G4540: Samaria, a small district of Palestine, bounded by Galilee on the north, and by Judaea on the south, and taking its name from the city of Samaria, the ancient capital of the kingdom of (northern) Israel.
Of Hebrew origin (Shomrown); Samaria (i.e. Shomeron), a city and region of Palestine.
G4541: a Samaritan, an inhabitant of the region of Samaria.
From Samareia; a Samarite, i.e. Inhabitant of Samaria.
G4542: (the region of) Samaria, a Samaritan woman.
Feminine of Samareites; a Samaritess, i.e. Woman of Samaria.
G4543: "Samos of Thrace", Samothrace, an island in the Aegean.
From Samos and Thraike (Thrace); Samo-thrace (Samos of Thrace), an island in the Mediterranean.
G4544: Samos, an island in the Aegean sea off the coast of Asia Minor, near Ephesus and Miletus.
Of uncertain affinity; Samus, an island of the Mediterranean.
G4545: Samuel, a prophet and judge in Isr.
Of Hebrew origin (Shmuw'el); Samuel (i.e. Shemuel), an Israelite.
G4546: Samson, one of the Judges of Israel.
Of Hebrew origin (Shimshown); Sampson (i.e. Shimshon), an Israelite.
G4547: Neuter of a derivative of sandalon (a "sandal"; of uncertain origin); a slipper or sole-pad.
G4549: Saul, (a) the first king of Israel, (b) the Hebrew name of the Apostle to the Gentiles.
Of Hebrew origin (Sha'uwl); Saul (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul.
G455: From ana and oigo (to open); to open up (literally or figuratively, in various applications).
G4550: From sepo; rotten, i.e. Worthless (literally or morally).
G4551: Sapphira, wife of Ananias, an early Christian.
Feminine of sappheiros; Sapphire, an Israelitess.
G4552: Of Hebrew origin (cappiyr); a "sapphire" or lapis-lazuli gem.
G4553: a basket, generally of twisted cords.
Apparently of Hebrew origin (sarag); a basket (as interwoven or wicker-work.
G4554: Sardis, an ancient city of Lydia in the province of Asia.
Plural of uncertain derivation; Sardis, a place in Asia Minor.
G4555: From the same as sardios; sardine (lithos being implied), i.e. A gem, so called.
G4556: Properly, an adjective from an uncertain base; sardian (lithos being implied), i.e. (as noun) the gem so called.
G4557: sardonyx, a precious stone, white streaked with red.
From the base of sardios and onux (the nail of a finger; hence the "onyx" stone); a "sardonyx", i.e. The gem so called.
G4558: Zarephath, a town in the district of Sidon in Phoenicia.
Of Hebrew origin (Tsarphath); Sarepta (i.e. Tsarephath), a place in Palestine.
G4559: From sarx; pertaining to flesh, i.e. (by extension) bodily, temporal, or (by implication) animal, unregenerate.
G456: to rebuild, build up (what has fallen or been razed to the ground), sometimes merely: to build.
From ana and oikodomeo; to rebuild.
G4560: From sarx; similar to flesh, i.e. (by analogy) soft.
G4561: flesh, body, human nature, materiality; kindred.

Probably from the base of saroo; flesh (as stripped of the skin), i.e. (strictly) the meat of an animal (as food), or (by extension) the body (as opposed to the soul (or spirit), or as the symbol of what is external, or as the means of kindred), or (by…
G4562: Of Hebrew origin (Sruwg); Saruch (i.e. Serug), a patriarch.
G4563: From a derivative of sairo (to brush off; akin to suro); meaning a broom; to sweep.
G4564: Of Hebrew origin (Sarah); Sarra (i.e. Sarah), the wife of Abraham.
G4565: Sharon, the maritime plain between Carmel and Joppa.
Of Hebrew origin (Sharown); Saron (i.e. Sharon), a district of Palestine.
G4566: Of Hebrew origin (satan); Satan, i.e. The devil.
G4567: Of Chaldee origin corresponding to ma'bad (with the definite affix); the accuser, i.e. The devil.
G4568: seah, a (Hebrew) measure (equiv. to about one and a half pecks).
Of Hebrew origin (c'ah); a certain measure for things dry.
G4569: Saul, the Jewish name of the apostle Paul.
Of Hebrew origin, the same as Saoul; Saulus (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul.
G4570: (a) to extinguish, quench, (b) to suppress, thwart.
A prolonged form of an apparently primary verb; to extinguish (literally or figuratively).
G4571: Accusative case singular of su; thee.
G4572: Genitive case from se and autos, also dative case of the same, seautoi seh-ow-to', and accusative case seauton seh-ow-ton', likewise contracted sautou (sow-too'), sautoi (sow-to'), and sauton (sow-ton'), respectively of (with, to) thyself.
G4573: to fear, to have reverential awe.
Middle voice from a derivative of sebomai; to venerate, i.e. Adore.
G4574: an object of worship or veneration.
From sebazomai; something adored, i.e. An object of worship (god, altar, etc).
G4575: (official Greek equivalent of Augustus), venerated, august, a title of the Roman emperors; hence secondarily: Augustan, imperial.
From sebazomai; venerable (august), i.e. (as noun) a title of the Roman Emperor, or (as adjective) imperial.
G4576: Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to revere, i.e. Adore.
G4577: Probably from suro through its congener eiro (to fasten; akin to haireomai); a chain (as binding or drawing).
G4578: a shaking (as an earthquake); a storm.
From seio; a commotion, i.e. (of the air) a gale, (of the ground) an earthquake.
G4579: to shake; fig: to agitate, stir up.

Apparently a primary verb; to rock (vibrate, properly, sideways or to and fro), i.e. (generally) to agitate (in any direction; cause to tremble); figuratively, to throw into a tremor (of fear or concern).
G458: From anomos; illegality, i.e. Violation of law or (genitive case) wickedness.
iniquity, X transgress(-ion of) the law, unrighteousness.
G4580: Of Latin origin; "second"; Secundus, a Christian.
G4581: Seleucia, on the Syrian coast, the harbor of Syrian Antioch.
From Seleukos (Seleucus, a Syrian king); Seleuceia, a place in Syria.
G4582: From selas (brilliancy; probably akin to the alternate of haireomai, through the idea of attractiveness); the moon.
G4583: to be moonstruck, be epileptic (supposedly influenced by the moon).
Middle voice or passive from a presumed derivative of selene; to be moon-struck, i.e. Crazy.
G4584: Of Hebrew origin (Shim'iy); Semei (i.e. Shimi), an Israelite.
G4585: Probably of foreign origin; fine wheaten flour.
G4588: Sergius, the middle (gentile) name of the proconsul of Cyprus.
Of Latin origin; Sergius, a Roman.
G4589: Of Hebrew origin (Sheth); Seth (i.e. Sheth), a patriarch.
G459: From a (as a negative particle) and nomos; lawless, i.e. (negatively) not subject to (the Jewish) law; (by implication, a Gentile), or (positively) wicked.
without law, lawless, transgressor, unlawful, wicked.
G4590: Of Hebrew origin (Shem); Sem (i.e. Shem), a patriarch.
G4591: to signify, indicate, give a sign, make known.
From sema (a mark; of uncertain derivation); to indicate.
G4592: a sign, miracle, indication, mark, token.
Neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of semaino; an indication, especially ceremonially or supernaturally.
G4593: From semeion; to distinguish, i.e. Mark (for avoidance).
G4594: Neuter (as adverb) of a presumed compound of the article ho (t changed to s) and hemera; on the (i.e. This) day (or night current or just passed); generally, now (i.e. At present, hitherto).
G4595: to make corrupt, pass. become corrupt.
Apparently a primary verb; to putrefy, i.e. (figuratively) perish.
G4596: From Ser (an Indian tribe from whom silk was procured; hence the name of the silk-worm); Seric, i.e. Silken (neuter as noun, a silky fabric).
G4597: Apparently of Hebrew origin (cac); a moth.
G4598: From ses and a derivative of bibrosko; moth-eaten.
G4599: From sthenos (bodily vigor; probably akin to the base of histemi); to strengthen, i.e. (figuratively) confirm (in spiritual knowledge and power).
G46: From a (as a negative particle) and the same as gnapheus; properly, unfulled, i.e. (by implication) new (cloth).
G460: Adverb from anomos; lawlessly, i.e. (specially) not amenable to (the Jewish) law.
G4600: Of uncertain derivation; the jaw-bone, i.e. (by implication) the cheek or side of the face.
G4601: intrans: to be silent, keep silence; trans: to keep secret; pass: to be kept secret.
From sige; to keep silent (transitively or intransitively).
G4602: Apparently from sizo (to hiss, i.e. Hist or hush); silence.
G4605: Sidon, a great coast city of Phoenicia.
Of Hebrew origin (Tsiydown); Sidon (i.e. Tsidon), a place in Palestine.
G4606: From Sidon; a Sidonian, i.e. Inhabitant of Sidon.
G4607: an assassin, murderer, bandit; one of the Sicarii.
Of Latin origin; a dagger-man or assassin; a freebooter (Jewish fanatic outlawed by the Romans).
G4608: Of Hebrew origin (shekar); an intoxicant, i.e. Intensely fermented liquor.
G4609: Silas, a pet-form of the name Silvanus; a Roman citizen and a helper of Paul.
Contraction for Silouanos; Silas, a Christian.
G461: to make upright (straight) again, rear again, restore.
From ana and a derivative of the base of orthos; to straighten up.
G4610: "sylvan", Silvanus, alt. form of the name Silas.
Of Latin origin; "silvan"; Silvanus, a Christian.
G4611: Siloam, a spring within the walls, in the south-east corner of Jerusalem.
Of Hebrew origin (Shiloach); Siloam (i.e. Shiloach), a pool of Jerusalem.
G4612: Of Latin origin; a semicinctium or half-girding, i.e. Narrow covering (apron).
G4613: Simon, the name of several Israelites.
Of Hebrew origin (Shim'own); Simon (i.e. Shimon), the name of nine Israelites.
G4614: Sinai, a mountain probably on the Sinai Peninsula.
Of Hebrew origin (Ciynay); Sina (i.e. Sinai), a mountain in Arabia.
G4615: mustard (probably the shrub, not the herb).
Perhaps from sinomai (to hurt, i.e. Sting); mustard (the plant).
G4616: Of uncertain (perhaps foreign) origin; byssos, i.e. Bleached linen (the cloth or a garment of it).
G4617: to sift, prove by trials, winnow.
G4618: From a derivative of sitos; grain-fed, i.e. Fattened.
G4619: From a derivative of sitos; grained, i.e. Fatted.
G462: From a (as a negative particle) and hosios; wicked.
G4620: a measured portion of grain or food.
From sitos and metron; a grain-measure, i.e. (by implication) ration (allowance of food).
G4621: Also plural irregular neuter sita (see'-tah) of uncertain derivation; grain, especially wheat.
G4622: Zion, a mountain of Jerusalem or the city of Jer.
Of Hebrew origin (Tsiyown); Sion (i.e. Tsijon), a hill of Jerusalem; figuratively, the Church (militant or triumphant).
G4623: to keep silence, be silent, either voluntarily or involuntarily.

From siope (silence, i.e. A hush; properly, muteness, i.e. Involuntary stillness, or inability to speak; and thus differing from sige, which is rather a voluntary refusal or indisposition to speak, although the terms are often used synonymously); to be dumb…
G4624: to cause to stumble, cause to sin, cause to become indignant, shock, offend.
From skandalon; to entrap, i.e. Trip up (figuratively, stumble (transitively) or entice to sin, apostasy or displeasure).
G4625: a stick for bait (of a trap), generally a snare, a stumbling block, an offense.
Scandal; probably from a derivative of kampto; a trap-stick (bent sapling), i.e. Snare (figuratively, cause of displeasure or sin).
occasion to fall (of stumbling), offence, thing that offends, stumblingblock.
G4626: Apparently a primary verb; to dig.
G4627: anything scooped out, a light boat.
A "skiff" (as if dug out), or yawl (carried aboard a large vessel for landing).
G4628: Apparently from skello (to parch; through the idea of leanness); the leg (as lank).
G4629: From a derivative of skepas (a covering; perhaps akin to the base of skopos through the idea of noticeableness); clothing.
G463: forbearance, suspense or delay (of punishment), patience.
G4630: Apparently of Latin origin; left-handed; Scevas (i.e. Scoevus), an Israelite.
G4631: From skeuos; furniture, i.e. Spare tackle.
G4632: a vessel to contain liquid; a vessel of mercy or wrath; any instrument by which anything is done; a household utensil; of ships: tackle.
Of uncertain affinity; a vessel, implement, equipment or apparatus (literally or figuratively (specially, a wife as contributing to the usefulness of the husband)).
G4633: a tent, booth, tabernacle, abode, dwelling, mansion, habitation.
Apparently akin to skeuos and skia; a tent or cloth hut (literally or figuratively).
G4634: the feast of tabernacles, the great festival of the Jews, held in October.
From skenos and pegnumi; the Festival of Tabernacles (so called from the custom of erecting booths for temporary homes).
G4635: From skene and poieo; a manufacturer of tents.
G4636: a tent, tabernacle; fig: of the human body.
From skene; a hut or temporary residence, i.e. (figuratively) the human body (as the abode of the spirit).
G4637: to dwell as in a tent, encamp, have tabernacle.
From skenos; to tent or encamp, i.e. (figuratively) to occupy (as a mansion) or (specially), to reside (as God did in the Tabernacle of old, a symbol of protection and communion).
G4638: a tent pitched, a dwelling, tabernacle.
From skenoo; an encampment, i.e. (figuratively) the Temple (as God's residence), the body (as a tenement for the soul).
G4639: a shadow, shade, thick darkness, an outline.
Apparently a primary word; "shade" or a shadow (literally or figuratively (darkness of error or an adumbration)).
G464: From anti and agonizomai; to struggle against (figuratively) ("antagonize").
G4640: Akin to skairo (to skip); to jump, i.e. Sympathetically move (as the quickening of a fetus).
G4641: Feminine of a compound of skleros and kardia; hard-heartedness, i.e. (specially), destitution of (spiritual) perception.
G4642: From the base of skelos; dry, i.e. Hard or tough (figuratively, harsh, severe).
G4643: hardness, hardness of heart, obstinacy, perverseness.
G4644: From skleros and trachelos; hardnaped, i.e. (figuratively) obstinate.
G4645: to harden, make hard, make stubborn.
From skleros; to indurate, i.e. (figuratively) render stubborn.
G4646: From the base of skelos; warped, i.e. Winding; figuratively, perverse.
G4647: a stake or thorn; fig: a sharp affliction.
Perhaps from the base of skelos and optanomai; withered at the front, i.e. A point or prickle (figuratively, a bodily annoyance or disability).
G4648: to look at, regard attentively, take heed, beware, consider.
From skopos; to take aim at (spy), i.e. (figuratively) regard.
consider, take heed, look at (on), mark. Compare optanomai.
G4649: a watchman, a mark (on which to fix the eye).
From skeptomai (to peer about ("skeptic"); perhaps akin to skapto through the idea of concealment; compare skepasma); a watch (sentry or scout), i.e. (by implication) a goal.
G465: From a compound of anti and allasso; an equivalent or ransom.
G4650: to disperse, scatter abroad (as of sheep); to dissipate, waste; to distribute alms.
Apparently from the same as skorpios (through the idea of penetrating); to dissipate, i.e. (figuratively) put to flight, waste, be liberal.
G4651: Probably from an obsolete skerpo (perhaps strengthened from the base of skopos and meaning to pierce); a "scorpion" (from its sting).
G4653: From skotos; dimness, obscurity (literally or figuratively).
G4654: From skotos; to obscure (literally or figuratively).
G4655: From the base of skia; shadiness, i.e. Obscurity (literally or figuratively).
G4656: From skotos; to obscure or blind (literally or figuratively).
G4657: Neuter of a presumed derivative of eis and kuon and ballo; what is thrown to the dogs, i.e. Refuse (ordure).
G4658: a Scythian, an inhabitant of Scythia (considered the wildest of barbarians).
Probably of foreign origin; a Scythene or Scythian, i.e. (by implication) a savage.
G4659: From skuthros (sullen) and a derivative of optanomai; angry-visaged, i.e. Gloomy or affecting a mournful appearance.
G466: to fill up in place of someone else, complete, supply.
From anti and anapleroo; to supplement.
G4660: Apparently a primary verb; to flay, i.e. (figuratively) to harass.
G4661: arms stripped from a foe, spoils.
Neuter from skullo; something stripped (as a hide), i.e. Booty.
G4662: From skolex and a derivative of bibrosko; worm-eaten, i.e. Diseased with maggots.
G4663: Of uncertain derivation; a grub, maggot or earth-worm.
G4665: Of uncertain derivation; the emerald or green gem so called.
G4666: myrrh (used as an ointment and for embalming).
G4667: Smyrna, a great port of the Roman province Asia.
The same as smurna; Smyrna, a place in Asia Minor.
G4669: to be like myrrh, to mingle with myrrh.
From Smurna; to tincture with myrrh, i.e. Embitter (as a narcotic).
G467: to give back as an equivalent, recompense.
From anti and apodidomi; to requite (good or evil).
G4670: Sodom, an unidentified city in the Jordan Valley.
Plural of Hebrew origin (Cdom); Sodoma (i.e. Sedom), a place in Palestine.
G4671: Dative case of su; to thee.
G4672: Solomon, son of David King of Israel, and Bathsheba.
Of Hebrew origin (Shlomoh); Solomon (i.e. Shelomoh), the son of David.
G4673: a cinerary urn, by anal. a coffin.
Probably akin to the base of soreuo; a funereal receptacle (urn, coffin), i.e. (by analogy) a bier.
G4675: Genitive case of su; of thee, thy.
X home, thee, thine (own), thou, thy.
G4676: a handkerchief, a head cloth (for the dead).
Of Latin origin; a sudarium (sweat-cloth), i.e. Towel (for wiping the perspiration from the face, or binding the face of a corpse).
G4677: "lily", Susanna, one of the women accompanying Jesus on His journeys.
Of Hebrew origin (shuwshan feminine); lily; Susannah (i.e. Shoshannah), an Israelitess.
G4678: wisdom, insight, skill (human or divine), intelligence.
From sophos; wisdom (higher or lower, worldly or spiritual).
G4679: to make wise, instruct; pass: to be skillfully devised.
From sophos; to render wise; in a sinister acceptation, to form "sophisms", i.e. Continue plausible error.
G468: a gift in return (for another), a return, recompense, requital.
From antapodidomi; a requital (properly, the thing).
G4680: Akin to saphes (clear); wise (in a most general application).
G4681: Spain, roughly co-extensive with the modern country of the name.
Probably of foreign origin; Spania, a region of Europe.
G4682: Prolongation from spairo (to grasp; apparently strengthened from spao through the idea of spasmodic contraction); to mangle, i.e. Convluse with epilepsy.
G4683: to swathe, wrap in swaddling clothes.
From sparganon (a strip; from a derivative of the base of sparasso meaning to strap or wrap with strips); to swathe (an infant after the Oriental custom).
G4684: to live extravagantly, luxuriously; to be wanton.
G4686: anything wound up or coiled, a body (of soldiers), a cohort.

Of immediate Latin origin, but ultimately a derivative of haireomai in the sense of its cognate heilisso; a coil (spira, "spire"), i.e. (figuratively) a mass of men (a Roman military cohort; also (by analogy) a squad of Levitical janitors).
G4687: Probably strengthened from spao (through the idea of extending); to scatter, i.e. Sow (literally or figuratively).
G4688: Of Latin origin; a speculator, i.e. Military scout (spy or (by extension) life-guardsman).
G4689: to pour out (as a drink offering), to make a libation.
Apparently a primary verb; to pour out as a libation, i.e. (figuratively) to devote (one's life or blood, as a sacrifice) ("spend").
G4690: (a) seed, commonly of cereals, (b) offspring, descendents.
From speiro; something sown, i.e. Seed (including the male "sperm"); by implication, offspring; specially, a remnant (figuratively, as if kept over for planting).
G4691: a babbler, gossiper, one who picks up seeds and trifles as does a bird.
From sperma and lego; a seed-picker (as the crow), i.e. (figuratively) a sponger, loafer (specially, a gossip or trifler in talk).
G4692: to hasten, urge on, desire earnestly.
Probably strengthened from pous; to "speed" ("study"), i.e. Urge on (diligently or earnestly); by implication, to await eagerly.
G4693: Neuter of a presumed derivative of speos (a grotto); a cavern; by implication, a hiding-place or resort.
G4694: a ledge of rock (over which the sea dashes), a reef.
Of uncertain derivation; a ledge or reef of rock in the sea.
G4695: From spilos; to stain or soil (literally or figuratively).
G4696: Of uncertain derivation; a stain or blemish, i.e. (figuratively) defect, disgrace.
G4697: to be moved in the inward parts, to feel compassion.
Middle voice from splagchnon; to have the bowels yearn, i.e. (figuratively) feel sympathy, to pity.
G4698: the inward parts; the heart, affections, seat of the feelings.
Probably strengthened from splen (the "spleen"); an intestine (plural); figuratively, pity or sympathy.
G47: From hagnos; cleanliness (the quality), i.e. (specially) chastity.
G470: to contradict, reply against, give a hostile answer.
From anti and apokrinomai; to contradict or dispute.
G4701: From speiro; a sowing, i.e. (by implication) parentage.
G4702: From sporos; sown, i.e. (neuter plural) a planted field.
G4703: From speiro; a scattering (of seed), i.e. (concretely) seed (as sown).
G4704: to make haste, to give diligence.
From spoude; to use speed, i.e. To make effort, be prompt or earnest.
do (give) diligence, be diligent (forward), endeavour, labour, study.
G4706: Neuter of spoudaioteros as adverb; more earnestly than others), i.e. Very promptly.
G4707: Comparative of spoudaios; more prompt, more earnest.
G4708: Adverb from spoudaioteros; more speedily, i.e. Sooner than otherwise.
G471: to speak or say in opposition, contradict (oppose, resist).
From anti and epo; to refute or deny.
G4710: From speudo; "speed", i.e. (by implication) despatch, eagerness, earnestness.
G4711: From speiro (as woven); a hamper or lunch-receptacle.
G4712: (a) a stadium, one eighth of a Roman mile, (b) a race-course for public games.
Or masculine (in plural) stadios (stad'-ee-os) from the base of histemi (as fixed); a stade or certain measure of distance; by implication, a stadium or race-course.
G4713: an earthen jar (for racking off wine).
From the base of histemi (as stationary); a jar or earthen tank.
G4714: an insurrection, dissension; originally: standing, position, place.
From the base of histemi; a standing (properly, the act), i.e. (by analogy) position (existence); by implication, a popular uprising; figuratively, controversy.
G4715: an Attic silver coin equal in value to the Jewish shekel.
From the base of kauchesis; a stander (standard of value), i.e. (specially), a stater or certain coin.
G4716: an upright stake, a cross (the Rom. instrument of crucifixion).

From the base of histemi; a stake or post (as set upright), i.e. (specially), a pole or cross (as an instrument of capital punishment); figuratively, exposure to death, i.e. Self-denial; by implication, the atonement of Christ.
G4717: to fix to the cross, crucify; fig: to destroy, mortify.
From stauros; to impale on the cross; figuratively, to extinguish (subdue) passion or selfishness.
G4718: Probably from the base of stephanos; a cluster of grapes (as if intertwined).
G4719: From the base of histemi; a head of grain (as standing out from the stalk).
G472: trans: to hold against; intrans: to withstand; mid: to hold out against, hold firmly to, cleave to.
From anti and the middle voice of echo; to hold oneself opposite to, i.e. (by implication) adhere to; by extension to care for.
G4720: Stachys, a Christian man at Rome.
The same as stachus; Stachys, a Christian.
G4721: a flat roof of a house.
Strengthened from a primary tegos (a "thatch" or "deck" of a building); a roof.
G4722: to cover closely (so as to keep water out), generally to bear up under.
From stege; to roof over, i.e. (figuratively) to cover with silence (endure patiently).
G4723: A contraction from stereos (as stiff and unnatural); "sterile".
G4724: to set, arrange; mid: to provide for, take care, withdraw from, hold aloof, avoid.
Probably strengthened from the base of histemi; properly, to set fast ("stall"), i.e. (figuratively) to repress (reflexively, abstain from associating with).
G4725: From the base of stephanos; a wreath for show.
G4727: to groan, expressing grief, anger, or desire.
From stenos; to make (intransitively, be) in straits, i.e. (by implication) to sigh, murmur, pray inaudibly.
G4728: Probably from the base of histemi; narrow (from obstacles standing close about).
G4729: (to keep some one in a tight place), to press upon, cramp, restrain.
From the same as stenochoria; to hem in closely, i.e. (figuratively) cramp.
G473: (a) instead of, in return for, over against, opposite, in exchange for, as a substitute for, (b) on behalf, (c) wherefore, because.
A primary particle; opposite, i.e. Instead or because of (rarely in addition to).
for, in the room of. Often used in composition to denote contrast, requital, substitution, correspondence, etc.
G4730: a narrow space, great distress, anguish.
From a compound of stenos and chora; narrowness of room, i.e. (figuratively) calamity.
G4731: From histemi; stiff, i.e. Solid, stable (literally or figuratively).
G4732: From stereos; to solidify, i.e. Confirm (literally or figuratively).
G4733: a solid body, a support, strength, firmness.
From stereoo; something established, i.e. (abstractly) confirmation (stability).
G4734: Probably contraction for stephanotos (crowned; from stephanoo); Stephanas, a Christian.
G4735: From an apparently primary stepho (to twine or wreathe); a chaplet (as a badge of royalty, a prize in the public games or a symbol of honor generally; but more conspicuous and elaborate than the simple fillet, diadema), literally or figuratively.
G4736: Stephen, one of the seven original deacons at Jerusalem, and the first martyr.
The same as stephanos; Stephanus, a Christian.
G4737: From stephanos; to adorn with an honorary wreath (literally or figuratively).
G4738: From histemi (as standing prominently); the (entire external) bosom, i.e. Chest.
G4739: to stand fast, stand firm, persevere.
From the perfect tense of histemi; to be stationary, i.e. (figuratively) to persevere.
G474: to throw at in opposition, exchange (words) with, perhaps: to compare.
From anti and ballo; to bandy.
G4741: (a) to fix firmly, direct myself towards, (b) generally met: to buttress, prop, support; to strengthen, establish.
From a presumed derivative of histemi (like stereos); to set fast, i.e. (literally) to turn resolutely in a certain direction, or (figuratively) to confirm.
G4742: a bed of leaves or rushes.
From a primary stizo (to "stick", i.e. Prick); a mark incised or punched (for recognition of ownership), i.e. (figuratively) scar of service.
G4743: a moment, point of time, an instant.
Feminine of stigma; a point of time, i.e. An instant.
G4744: to shine, glisten, flash, be radiant.
Apparently a primary verb; to gleam, i.e. Flash intensely.
G4745: Probably from histemi; a colonnade or interior piazza.
G4746: a bough, branch of a tree.
From a primary steibo (to "step" or "stamp"); a spread (as if tramped flat) of loose materials for a couch, i.e. (by implication) a bough of a tree so employed.
G4747: (a) plur: the heavenly bodies, (b) a rudiment, an element, a rudimentary principle, an elementary rule.

Neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of stoicheo; something orderly in arrangement, i.e. (by implication) a serial (basal, fundamental, initial) constituent (literally), proposition (figuratively).
G4748: to be in rows, to walk by rule.
From a derivative of steicho (to range in regular line); to march in (military) rank (keep step), i.e. (figuratively) to conform to virtue and piety.
G4749: a long robe, worn by the upper classes in the East.
From stello; equipment, i.e. (specially), a "stole" or long-fitting gown (as a mark of dignity).
G475: to oppose, set oneself in opposition.
From anti and diatithemai; to set oneself opposite, i.e. Be disputatious.
G4750: the mouth, speech, eloquence in speech, the point of a sword.

Probably strengthened from a presumed derivative of the base of tomoteros; the mouth (as if a gash in the face); by implication, language (and its relations); figuratively, an opening (in the earth); specially, the front or edge (of a weapon).
G4751: From stoma; an orifice (the gullet), i.e. (specially), the "stomach".
G4752: warfare, military service; of Christian warfare.
From strateuomai; military service, i.e. (figuratively) the apostolic career (as one of hardship and danger).
G4753: an expedition, an army, a company of soldiers.
From strateuomai; an armament, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops (more or less extensive or systematic).
G4754: to wage war, fight, serve as a soldier; fig: of the warring lusts against the soul.
Middle voice from the base of stratia; to serve in a military campaign; figuratively, to execute the apostolate (with its arduous duties and functions), to contend with carnal inclinations.
G4755: (a) a general or leader of the army, (b) a magistrate or governor, (c) captain of the temple.
From the base of stratia and ago or hegeomai; a general, i.e. (by implication or analogy) a (military) governor (praetor), the chief (praefect) of the (Levitical) temple-wardens.
G4756: an army; met: a host of angels, the hosts of heaven (i.e. the stars).
Feminine of a derivative of stratos (an army; from the base of stronnumi, as encamped); camp-likeness, i.e. An army, i.e. (figuratively) the angels, the celestial luminaries.
G4757: From a presumed derivative of the same as stratia; a camper-out, i.e. A (common) warrior (literally or figuratively).
G4758: to collect an army, enlist troops.
From a compound of the base of stratia and lego (in its original sense); to gather (or select) as a warrior, i.e. Enlist in the army.
G4759: commander of the Roman emperor's body-guard.
From stratopedon and archo; a ruler of an army, i.e. (specially), a Praetorian praefect.
G476: From anti and dike; an opponent (in a lawsuit); specially, Satan (as the arch-enemy).
G4760: From the base of stratia and the same as pedinos; a camping-ground, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops.
G4761: to twist, torture; met: to twist or pervert language.
From a derivative of strepho; to wrench, i.e. (specially), to torture (by the rack), but only figuratively, to pervert.
G4762: to turn, be converted, change, change direction.
Strengthened from the base of trope; to twist, i.e. Turn quite around or reverse (literally or figuratively).
convert, turn (again, back again, self, self about).
G4763: From a presumed derivative of strenos; to be luxurious.
G4764: Akin to stereos; a "straining", "strenuousness" or "strength", i.e. (figuratively) luxury (voluptuousness).
G4765: Diminutive of strouthos (a sparrow); a little sparrow.
G4766: Or simpler stronnuo (strone-noo'-o), prolongation from a still simpler stroo (stro'-o), (used only as an alternate in certain tenses) (probably akin to stereos through the idea of positing); to "strew," i.e. Spread (as a carpet or couch).
G4767: From a derivative of an obsolete apparently primary stugo (to hate); hated, i.e. Odious.
G4768: to be gloomy, have a somber countenance, be shocked.
From the same as stugnetos; to render gloomy, i.e. (by implication) glower (be overcast with clouds, or sombreness of speech).
G4769: From stuo (to stiffen; properly akin to the base of histemi); a post ("style"), i.e. (figuratively) support.
G477: a proposition, tenet, opinion advanced by one party against another; opposition.
From a compound of anti and tithemi; opposition, i.e. A conflict (of theories).
G4770: From stoa; a "Stoic" (as occupying a particular porch in Athens), i.e. Adherent of a certin philosophy.
G4771: The person pronoun of the second person singular; thou.
thou. See also se, soi, sou; and for the plural humas, humeis, humin, humon.
G4773: akin to, related; subst: fellow countryman, kinsman.
From sun and genos; a relative (by blood); by extension, a fellow countryman.
G4774: From a compound of sun and ginosko; fellow knowledge, i.e. Concession.
G4775: From sun and kathemai; to seat oneself in company with.
G4776: to cause to sit down with, sit down together.
From sun and kathizo; to give (or take) a seat in company with.
G4777: to bear evil treatment along with.
From sun and kakopatheo; to suffer hardship in company with.
G4778: From sun and kakoucheo; to maltreat in company with, i.e. (passively) endure persecution together.
G4779: From sun and kaleo; to convoke.
G478: to set down against, to replace, oppose.
From anti and kathistemi; to set down (troops) against, i.e. Withstand.
G4780: to conceal closely, cover up wholly.
From sun and kalupto; to conceal altogether.
G4781: From sun and kampto; to bend together, i.e. (figuratively) to afflict.
G4782: From sun and katabaino; to descend in company with.
G4783: From sugkatatithemai; a deposition (of sentiment) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) accord with.
G4784: to deposit together, to agree with.
Mid from sun and katatithemi; to deposit (one's vote or opinion) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to accord with.
G4785: to condemn with, to vote (one) a place among.
From sun and a compound of kata and psephizo; to count down in company with, i.e. Enroll among.
G4786: to mix together, to agree with.
From sun and kerannumi; to commingle, i.e. (figuratively) to combine or assimilate.
G4787: to move together, stir up, excite.
From sparasso and kineo; to move together, i.e. (specially), to excite as a mass (to sedition).
G4788: to enclose, shut in, make subject to.
From sun and kleio; to shut together, i.e. Include or (figuratively) embrace in a common subjection to.
G4789: From sun and kleronomos; a co-heir, i.e. (by analogy) participant in common.
G479: From anti and kaleo; to invite in return.
G4790: to be a partaker with, have fellowship with, be an accomplice in.
From sun and koinoneo; to share in company with, i.e. Co-participate in.
communicate (have fellowship) with, be partaker of.
G4791: From sun and koinonos; a co-participant.
G4792: to bear away together with, as in carrying away a corpse.
From sun and komizo; to convey together, i.e. Collect or bear away in company with others.
G4793: to join together, combine, compare, interpret, explain.

From sun and krino; to judge of one thing in connection with another, i.e. Combine (spiritual ideas with appropriate expressions) or collate (one person with another by way of contrast or resemblance).
G4794: to be bowed together, bent double.
From sun and kupto; to stoop altogether, i.e. Be completely overcome by.
G4795: From a comparative of sun and kureo (to light or happen; from the base of kurios); concurrence, i.e. Accident.
G4796: From sun and chairo; to sympathize in gladness, congratulate.
G4797: to pour together, to confuse, throw into confusion.
Or sugchuno (soong-khoo'-no) from sun and cheo (to pour) or its alternate; to commingle promiscuously, i.e. (figuratively) to throw (an assembly) into disorder, to perplex (the mind).
confound, confuse, stir up, be in an uproar.
G4798: to use together with, to associate with.
From sun and chraomai; to use jointly, i.e. (by implication) to hold intercourse in common.
G4799: From sugcheo; commixture, i.e. (figuratively) riotous disturbance.
G48: to cleanse, purify, either ceremonially, actually, or morally.
From hagnos; to make clean, i.e. (figuratively) sanctify (ceremonially or morally).
G480: to resist, oppose, withstand, lie opposite to.
From anti and keimai; to lie opposite, i.e. Be adverse (figuratively, repugnant) to.
G4800: From sun and zao; to continue to live in common with, i.e. Co-survive (literally or figuratively).
G4801: to yoke together, unite (as man and wife).
From sun and the base of zeugos; to yoke together, i.e. (figuratively) conjoin (in marriage).
G4802: From sun and zeteo; to investigate jointly, i.e. Discuss, controvert, cavil.
G4803: From suzeteo; mutual questioning, i.e. Discussion.
G4804: a disputer, as the Greek sophists.
From suzeteo; a disputant, i.e. Sophist.
G4805: From suzeugnumi; co-yoked, i.e. (figuratively) as noun, a colleague; probably rather as a proper name; Syzygus, a Christian.
G4806: From sun and zoopoieo; to reanimate conjointly with (figuratively).
G4807: a sycamore tree, black mulberry tree.
Of Hebrew origin (shaqam) in imitation of sukomoraia; a sycamore-fig tree.
G4809: From sukon and moron (the mulberry); the "sycamore"-fig tree.
G481: right opposite, off (nautical sense), over against.
G4810: Apparently a primary word; a fig.
G4811: From a compound of sukon and a derivative of phaino; to be a fig-informer (reporter of the law forbidding the exportation of figs from Greece), "sycophant", i.e. (genitive and by extension) to defraud (exact unlawfully, extort).
accuse falsely, take by false accusation.
G4812: to plunder, lead captive; met: to make victim by fraud.
From the base of sulao and (the reduplicated form of) ago; to lead away as booty, i.e. (figuratively) seduce.
G4813: From a derivative of sullo (to strip; probably akin to haireomai; compare skulon); to despoil.
G4814: From sun and laleo; to talk together, i.e. Converse.
G4815: to collect, to take, by implication to take part with, to conceive.
From sun and lambano; to clasp, i.e. Seize (arrest, capture); specially, to conceive (literally or figuratively); by implication, to aid.
G4816: From sun and lego in its original sense; to collect.
G4817: to reason, reckon with myself, consider.
From sun and logizomai; to reckon together (with oneself), i.e. Deliberate.
G4818: to be moved to grief with (pass.).
From sun and lupeo; to afflict jointly, i.e. (passive) sorrow at (on account of) someone.
G4819: to come together, (of events) to come to pass.
From sun and the base of basis; to walk (figuratively, transpire) together, i.e. Concur (take place).
G482: to take hold of, help, share in, partake of, enjoy.
From anti and the middle voice of lambano; to take hold of in turn, i.e. Succor; also to participate.
G4820: properly: to throw together, hence: to ponder, come up with, encounter, with or without hostile intent; to dispute with; mid: to confer, consult with, contribute.
From sun and ballo; to combine, i.e. (in speaking) to converse, consult, dispute, (mentally) to consider, (by implication) to aid, (personally) to join, attack.
confer, encounter, help, make, meet with, ponder.
G4821: From sun and basileuo; to be co-regent (figuratively).
G4822: (a) to unite or knit together, (b) to put together in reasoning, and so: to conclude, prove, (c) to teach, instruct.
From sun and bibazo (to force; causative (by reduplication) of the base of basis); to drive together, i.e. Unite (in association or affection), (mentally) to infer, show, teach.
compact, assuredly gather, intrust, knit together, prove.
G4823: to give advice, exhort; mid: to take counsel together, consult.
From sun and bouleuo; to give (or take) advice jointly, i.e. Recommend, deliberate or determine.
G4824: (a) a body of advisers (assessors) in a court, a council, (b) abstr: consultation, counsel, advice; resolution, decree.
Neuter of a presumed derivative of sumboulos; advisement; specially, a deliberative body, i.e. The provincial assessors or lay-court.
G4825: From sun and boule; a consultor, i.e. Adviser.
G4826: Symeon, Simeon, the name of several Israelites, also a tribe of Isr.
From the same as Simon; Symeon (i.e. Shimon), the name of five Israelites.
G4827: From a compound of sun and manthano; a co-learner (of Christianity).
G4828: to testify or bear witness with.
From sun and martureo; to testify jointly, i.e. Corroborate by (concurrent) evidence.
G4829: to partake with, divide together with, have a share in.
Middle voice from sun and merizo; to share jointly, i.e. Participate in.
G483: to speak or say in opposition, contradict (oppose, resist).
From anti and lego; to dispute, refuse.
answer again, contradict, deny, gainsay(-er), speak against.
G4830: partaking with, subst. a joint partaker.
From sun and metochos; a co-participant.
G4831: From a presumed compound of sun and mimeomai; a co-imitator, i.e. Fellow votary.
G4832: From sun and morphe; jointly formed, i.e. (figuratively) similar.
G4833: to bring to the same form with, conform.
From summorphos; to render like, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate.
G4834: to have a fellow feeling with, sympathize with.
From sumpathes; to feel "sympathy" with, i.e. (by implication) to commiserate.
have compassion, be touched with a feeling of.
G4835: From sumpascho; having a fellow-feeling ("sympathetic"), i.e. (by implication) mutually commiserative.
G4836: to come together with, stand by one, help.
From sun and paraginomai; to be present together, i.e. To convene; by implication, to appear in aid.
G4837: to invite, encourage along with others; pass: to share in encouragement with.
From sun and parakaleo; to console jointly.
G4838: to take along as a companion.
From sun and paralambano; to take along in company.
G4839: to remain or continue together with.
From sun and parameno; to remain in company, i.e. Still live.
G4840: From sun and pareimi; to be at hand together, i.e. Now present.
G4841: From sun and pascho (including its alternate); to experience pain jointly or of the same kind (specially, persecution; to "sympathize").
G4842: From sun and pempo; to despatch in company.
G4843: From sun and a compound of peri and lambano; to take by enclosing altogether, i.e. Earnestly throw the arms about one.
G4844: From sun and pino; to partake a beverage in company.
G4845: to fill completely; pass: to be completed.
From sun and pleroo; to implenish completely, i.e. (of space) to swamp (a boat), or (of time) to accomplish (passive, be complete).
G4846: to choke utterly, as weeds do plants; to crowd upon.
From sun and pnigo; to strangle completely, i.e. (literally) to drown, or (figuratively) to crowd.
G4847: From sun and polites; a native of the same town, i.e. (figuratively) co-religionist (fellow-Christian).
G4848: to journey together with; to come together, assemble.
From sun and poreuomai; to journey together; by implication, to assemble.
G4849: a drinking party, company (guests at a party).
Neuter of a derivative of the alternate of sumpino; a drinking-party ("symposium"), i.e. (by extension) a room of guests.
G485: From a derivative of antilego; dispute, disobedience.
G4850: From sun and presbuteros; a co-presbyter.
G4851: to bring together, collect; to be profitable to.
From sun and phero (including its alternate); to bear together (contribute), i.e. (literally) to collect, or (figuratively) to conduce; especially (neuter participle as a noun) advantage.
be better for, bring together, be expedient (for), be good, (be) profit(-able for).
G4852: to assent to, consent, confess, agree with.
From sun and phemi; to say jointly, i.e. Assent to.
G4853: one of the same tribe, a fellow country-man.
From sun and a derivative of phule; a co-tribesman, i.e. Native of the same country.
G4854: From sun and a derivative of phuo; grown along with (connate), i.e. (figuratively) closely united to.
G4855: From sun and phuo; passive, to grow jointly.
G4856: to call out with, to be in harmony, generally to agree.
From sumphonos; to be harmonious, i.e. (figuratively) to accord (be suitable, concur) or stipulate (by compact).
G4858: From sumphonos; unison of sound ("symphony"), i.e. A concert of instruments (harmonious note).
G4859: From sun and phone; sounding together (alike), i.e. (figuratively) accordant (neuter as noun, agreement).
G486: to abuse in return, give abuse for abuse.
From anti and loidoreo; to rail in reply.
G4860: to compute, reckon up, count together.
From sun and psephizo; to compute jointly.
G4861: From sun and psuche; co-spirited, i.e. Similar in sentiment.
G4862: A primary preposition denoting union; with or together (but much closer than meta or para), i.e. By association, companionship, process, resemblance, possession, instrumentality, addition, etc..
beside, with. In composition it has similar applications, including completeness.
G4863: to gather together, collect, assemble, receive with hospitality, entertain.
From sun and ago; to lead together, i.e. Collect or convene; specially, to entertain (hospitably).
+ accompany, assemble (selves, together), bestow, come together, gather (selves together, up, together), lead into, resort, take in.
G4864: an assembly, congregation, synagogue, either the place or the people gathered together in the place.
From (the reduplicated form of) sunago; an assemblage of persons; specially, a Jewish "synagogue" (the meeting or the place); by analogy, a Christian church.
G4865: to struggle in company with, aid.
From sun and agonizomai; to struggle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to be a partner (assistant).
G4866: to compete together with others, cooperate vigorously with.
From sun and athleo; to wrestle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to seek jointly.
G4867: From sun and athroizo (to hoard); to convene.
G4868: to compare (settle) accounts, make a reckoning.
From sun and airo; to make up together, i.e. (figuratively) to compute (an account).
G4869: From sun and aichmalotos; a co-captive.
G487: From anti and lutron; a redemption-price.
G4870: From sun and akoloutheo; to accompany.
G4871: From sun and halizo (to throng); to accumulate, i.e. Convene.
G4872: From sun and anabaino; to ascend in company with.
G4873: From sun and anakeimai; to recline in company with (at a meal).
sit (down, at the table, together) with (at meat).
G4874: to mingle together with, keep company with.
From sun and a compound of ana and mignumi; to mix up together, i.e. (figurative) associate with.
G4875: to lie down to rest with, to be refreshed in spirit with.
Middle from sun and anapano; to recruit oneself in company with.
G4876: to meet, encounter, fall in with.
From sun and a derivative of anti; to meet with; figuratively, to occur.
G4878: to lend a hand along with, take interest in (a thing) along with (others), assist jointly to perform some task, cooperate with, take share in, help, aid.
From sun and antilambanomai; to take hold of opposite together, i.e. Co-operate (assist).
G4879: to lead away with, carry along with (in good or bad sense according to context); mid: to conform myself willingly to.
From sun and apago; to take off together, i.e. Transport with (seduce, passively, yield).
G488: to measure in return, give equivalent measure.
From anti and metreo; to mete in return.
G4880: From sun and apothnesko; to decease (literally) in company with, or (figuratively), similarly to.
G4881: to destroy with, mid. to perish together.
From sun and apollumi; to destroy (middle voice or passively, be slain) in company with.
G4882: From sun and apostello; to despatch (on an errand) in company with.
G4883: From sun and a derivative of a compound of harmos and lego (in its original sense of laying); to render close-jointed together, i.e. Organize compactly.
G4884: From sun and harpazo; to snatch together, i.e. Seize.
G4885: to cause to grow together, pass. to grow together.
From sun and auzano; to increase (grow up) together.
G4886: that which binds together; a band, bond.
From sun and desmon; a joint tie, i.e. Ligament, (figuratively) uniting principle, control.
G4887: to bind together; pass: to be bound together with, as of prisoners in chains.
From sun and deo; to bind with, i.e. (passively) be a fellow-prisoner (figuratively).
G4888: to join in approving, to glorify together.
From sun and doxazo; to exalt to dignity in company (i.e. Similarly) with.
G4889: a fellow slave, fellow servant; of Christians: a fellow worker, colleague.
From sun and doulos; a co-slave, i.e. Servitor or ministrant of the same master (human or divine).
G489: From a compound of anti and misthos; requital, correspondence.
G4890: a running together, a concourse (esp. of a riotous gathering).
From (the alternate of) suntrecho; a running together, i.e. (riotous) concourse.
G4891: From sun and egeiro; to rouse (from death) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to revivify (spirtually) in resemblance to.
G4892: a council, tribunal; the Sanhedrin, the meeting place of the Sanhedrin.
Neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of sun and the base of hedraios; a joint session, i.e. (specially), the Jewish Sanhedrin; by analogy, a subordinate tribunal.
G4893: From a prolonged form of suneido; co-perception, i.e. Moral consciousness.
G4894: From sun and eido; to see completely; used (like its primary) only in two past tenses, respectively meaning to understand or become aware, and to be conscious or (clandestinely) informed of.
consider, know, be privy, be ware of.
G4895: to be with, come together with.
From sun and eimi (including its various inflections); to be in company with, i.e. Present at the time.
G4896: From sun and eimi (to go); to assemble.
G4897: to enter together with, embark with.
From sun and eiserchomai; to enter in company with.
go in with, go with into.
G4898: From sun and the base of ekdemeo; a co-absentee from home, i.e. Fellow-traveller.
G4899: From a compound of sun and eklegomai; chosen in company with, i.e. Co-elect (fellow Christian).
G49: From hagnizo; a cleansing (the act), i.e. (ceremonially) lustration.
G490: Antioch, (a) Antioch on the river Orontes, capital of the Province Syria, (b) Pisidian Antioch, not in Pisidia, but near Pisidia, in the Roman Province Galatia.
From Antiochus (a Syrian king); Antiochia, a place in Syria.
G4900: From sun and elauno; to drive together, i.e. (figuratively) exhort (to reconciliation).
G4901: to testify or bear witness together with.
From sun and epimartureo; to testify further jointly, i.e. Unite in adding evidence.
G4902: Middle voice from sun and a primary hepo (to follow); to attend (travel) in company with.
G4903: From sunergos; to be a fellow-worker, i.e. Co-operate.
G4904: From a presumed compound of sun and the base of ergon; a co-laborer, i.e. Coadjutor.
companion in labour, (fellow-)helper(-labourer, -worker), labourer together with, workfellow.
G4905: to come or go with, accompany; to come together, assemble.
From sun and erchomai; to convene, depart in company with, associate with, or (specially), cohabit (conjugally).
accompany, assemble (with), come (together), come (company, go) with, resort.
G4906: From sun and esthio (including its alternate); to take food in company with.
G4907: a putting together in the mind, hence: understanding, practical discernment, intellect.
From suniemi; a mental putting together, i.e. Intelligence or (concretely) the intellect.
G4908: From suniemi; mentally put (or putting) together, i.e. Sagacious.
G4909: to consent, agree, be of one mind with, be willing.
From sun and eudokeo; to think well of in common, i.e. Assent to, feel gratified with.
allow, assent, be pleased, have pleasure.
G491: an Antiochian, an inhabitant of Antioch.
From Antiocheia; an Antiochian or inhabitant of Antiochia.
G4910: to entertain together, pass. feast together.

From sun and a derivative of a presumed compound of eu and a derivative of echo (meaning to be in good condition, i.e. (by implication) to fare well, or feast); to entertain sumptuously in company with, i.e. (middle voice or passive) to revel together.
G4911: From sun and ephistemi; to stand up together, i.e. To resist (or assault) jointly.
G4912: (a) to press together, close, (b) to press on every side, confine, (c) to hold fast, (d) to urge, impel, (e) pass: to be afflicted with (sickness).
From sun and echo; to hold together, i.e. To compress (the ears, with a crowd or siege) or arrest (a prisoner); figuratively, to compel, perplex, afflict, preoccupy.
constrain, hold, keep in, press, lie sick of, stop, be in a strait, straiten, be taken with, throng.
G4913: Middle voice from sun and the base of hedone; to rejoice in with oneself, i.e. Feel satisfaction concerning.
G4914: From a compound of sun and ethos; mutual habituation, i.e. Usage.
G4915: From sun and a derivative of helikia; a co-aged person, i.e. Alike in years.
G4916: From sun and thapto; to inter in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate spiritually (to Christ by a sepulture as to sin).
G4917: to break, break in pieces, crush, shatter.
From sun and thlao (to crush); to dash together, i.e. Shatter.
G4918: to press on all sides, crowd upon.
From sun and thlibo; to compress, i.e. Crowd on all sides.
G4919: to break in pieces, crush, thoroughly weaken.
From sun and thrupto (to crumble); to crush together, i.e. (figuratively) to dispirit.
G492: to pass opposite, on the opposite side of the road.
From anti and parerchomai; to go along opposite.
pass by on the other side.
G4920: From sun and hiemi (to send); to put together, i.e. (mentally) to comprehend; by implication, to act piously.
G4921: to place together, commend, prove, exhibit; instrans: to stand with; to be composed of, cohere.

Or (strengthened) sunistano (soon-is-tan'-o), or sunistemi (soon-is'-tay-mee) from sun and histemi (including its collateral forms); to set together, i.e. (by implication) to introduce (favorably), or (figuratively) to exhibit; intransitively, to stand near,…
G4922: From sun and hodeuo; to travel in company with.
G4923: a journey in company, a company (of travelers).
From a compound of sun and hodos ("synod"); companionship on a journey, i.e. (by implication), a caravan.
G4924: to dwell with, live in wedlock with.
From sun and oikeo; to reside together (as a family).
G4925: to build together, to build up together.
From sun and oikodomeo; to construct, i.e. (passively) to compose (in company with other Christians, figuratively).
G4926: From sun and homileo; to converse mutually.
G4927: to be contiguous with, be next door to.
From sun and a derivative of a compound of the base of homou and the base of horion; to border together, i.e. Adjoin.
G4929: to arrange with, direct, appoint, prescribe, ordain.
From sun and tasso; to arrange jointly, i.e. (figuratively) to direct.
G493: Antipas, a Christian martyr of Pergamum.
Contracted for a compound of anti and a derivative of pater; Antipas, a Christian.
G4930: a joint payment (for public service), joint action, completion.
From sunteleo; entire completion, i.e. Consummation (of a dispensation).
G4931: to bring to an end, fulfill, accomplish.
From sun and teleo; to complete entirely; generally, to execute (literally or figuratively).
G4932: to cut short, bring to swift accomplishment, determine, decide.
From sun and the base of tomoteros; to contract by cutting, i.e. (figuratively) do concisely (speedily).
G4933: to preserve, keep safe, keep in mind, keep close.
From sun and tereo; to keep closely together, i.e. (by implication) to conserve (from ruin); mentally, to remember (and obey).
G4934: mid. and pass: to make a compact (agreement) with (together), covenant with, agree.
