Middle voice from sun and tithemi; to place jointly, i.e. (figuratively) to consent (bargain, stipulate), concur.
G4935: Adverb from a derivative of suntemno; concisely (briefly).
G4936: From sun and trecho (including its alternate); to rush together (hastily assemble) or headlong (figuratively).
G4937: to break by crushing, break in pieces, shatter, crush, bruise.
From sun and the base of tribos; to crush completely, i.e. To shatter (literally or figuratively).
break (in pieces), broken to shivers (+ -hearted), bruise.
G4938: From suntribo; concussion or utter fracture (properly, concretely), i.e. Complete ruin.
G4939: one brought up with, a foster brother or an intimate friend.
From sun and trophos (in a passive sense); a fellow-nursling, i.e. Comrade.
G494: Antipatris, a town, where was a Roman colony, on the road between Caesarea and Jerusalem.
From the same as Antipas; Antipatris, a place in Palestine.
G4940: to meet with, come to, fall in with.
From sun and tugchano; to chance together, i.e. Meet with (reach).
G4941: "happy event", Syntyche, a Christian woman at Philippi.
From suntugchano; an accident; Syntyche, a Christian female.
G4942: to dissemble with, play a part with.
From sun and hupokrinomai; to act hypocritically in concert with.
G4943: to help together, join in serving.
From sun and a derivative of a compound of hupo and the base of ergon; to be a co-auxiliary, i.e. Assist.
G4944: From sun and odino; to have (parturition) pangs in company (concert, simultaneously) with, i.e. (figuratively) to sympathize (in expectation of relief from suffering).
G4945: From a compound of sun and omnuo; a swearing together, i.e. (by implication) a plot.
G4946: Syracuse, a large maritime city of Sicily.
Plural of uncertain derivation; Syracuse, the capital of Sicily.
G4947: Syria, a great Roman imperial province, united with Cilicia.
Probably of Hebrew origin (Tsor); Syria (i.e. Tsyria or Tyre), a region of Asia.
G4948: From the same as Suria; a Syran (i.e. Probably Tyrian), a native of Syria.
G4949: Syrophoenician, i.e. Phoenician (of Syria, in contrast to Carthage and its territory in North Africa).
Feminine of a compound of Suros and the same as Phoinike; a Syro-phoenician woman, i.e. A female native of Phoenicia in Syria.
G495: on the opposite side or shore.
From anti and peran; on the opposite side.
G4950: "shoal", Syrtis, the name of two large sandbanks on the Lybian coast.
From suro; a shoal (from the sand drawn thither by the waves), i.e. The Syrtis Major or great bay on the north coast of Africa.
G4951: Probably akin to haireomai; to trail.
G4952: to throw violently on the ground.
From sun and sparasso; to rend completely, i.e. (by analogy) to convulse violently.
G4953: Neuter of a compound of sun and the base of semaino; a sign in common, i.e. Preconcerted signal.
G4954: belonging to the same body; fig: of Jews and Gentiles belonging to the same Church.
From sun and soma; of a joint body, i.e. (figuratively) a fellow-member of the Christian community.
G4955: From a compound of sun and a derivative of stasis; a fellow-insurgent.
G4956: From a derivative of sunistao; introductory, i.e. Recommendatory.
G4957: From sun and stauroo; to impale in company with (literally or figuratively).
G4958: to contract, shorten, wrap around, swathe.
From sun and stello; to send (draw) together, i.e. Enwrap (enshroud a corpse for burial), contract (an interval).
G4959: From sun and stenazo; to moan jointly, i.e. (figuratively) experience a common calamity.
G496: to resist, oppose, fall against or upon.
From anti and pipto (including its alternate); to oppose.
G4960: to be in the same rank with; to answer to, correspond to.
From sun and stoicheo; to file together (as soldiers in ranks), i.e. (figuratively) to correspond to.
G4961: a fellow soldier (in the Christian faith).
From sun and stratiotes; a co-campaigner, i.e. (figuratively) an associate in Christian toil.
G4962: to twist together, to gather together (pass.).
From sun and strepho; to twist together, i.e. Collect (a bundle, a crowd).
G4963: a gathering together, riotous concourse, conspiracy.
From sustrepho; a twisting together, i.e. (figuratively) a secret coalition, riotous crowd.
G4964: From sun and a derivative of schema; to fashion alike, i.e. Conform to the same pattern (figuratively).
conform to, fashion self according to.
G4965: Of Hebrew origin (shekar); Sychar (i.e. Shekar), a place in Palestine.
G4966: Of Hebrew origin (Shkem); Sychem (i.e. Shekem), the name of a Canaanite and of a place in Palestine.
G4967: From sphazo; butchery (of animals for food or sacrifice, or (figuratively) of men (destruction)).
G4968: Neuter of a derivative of sphage; a victim (in sacrifice).
G4969: to slay, kill by violence, slaughter, wound mortally.
A primary verb; to butcher (especially an animal for food or in sacrifice) or (generally) to slaughter, or (specially), to maim (violently).
G497: From anti and strateuomai; (figuratively) to attack, i.e. (by implication) destroy.
G4970: Neuter plural of sphodros (violent; of uncertain derivation) as adverb; vehemently, i.e. In a high degree, much.
G4971: Adverb from the same as sphodra; very much.
G4972: to seal, set a seal upon.
From sphragis; to stamp (with a signet or private mark) for security or preservation (literally or figuratively); by implication, to keep secret, to attest.
(set a, set to) seal up, stop.
G4973: a seal, signet ring, the impression of a seal, that which the seal attests, the proof.

Probably strengthened from phrasso; a signet (as fencing in or protecting from misappropriation); by implication, the stamp impressed (as a mark of privacy, or genuineness), literally or figuratively.
G4974: Neuter of a presumed derivative probably of the same as sphaira (a ball, "sphere"; compare the feminine sphura, a hammer); the ankle (as globular).
G4975: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the alternate of echo as adverb; nigh, i.e. Nearly.
G4976: From the alternate of echo; a figure (as a mode or circumstance), i.e. (by implication) external condition.
G4977: Apparently a primary verb; to split or sever (literally or figuratively).
break, divide, open, rend, make a rent.
G4978: a rent, as in a garment; a division, dissention.
From schizo; a split or gap ("schism"), literally or figuratively.
G4979: Diminutive of schoinos (a rush or flag-plant; of uncertain derivation); a rushlet, i.e. Grass-withe or tie (generally).
G498: to range in battle against, to set oneself against.
From anti and the middle voice of tasso; to range oneself against, i.e. Oppose.
G4980: (a) to have leisure, (b) to stand empty (of a house).
From schole; to take a holiday, i.e. Be at leisure for (by implication, devote oneself wholly to); figuratively, to be vacant (of a house).
G4981: leisure, disputation (that for which leisure is used), school.

Probably feminine of a presumed derivative of the alternate of echo; properly, loitering (as a withholding of oneself from work) or leisure, i.e. (by implication) a "school" (as vacation from physical employment).
G4982: From a primary sos (contraction for obsolete saos, "safe"); to save, i.e. Deliver or protect (literally or figuratively).
heal, preserve, save (self), do well, be (make) whole.
G4983: body, flesh; the body of the Church.
From sozo; the body (as a sound whole), used in a very wide application, literally or figuratively.
G4985: bodily, corporeally, belonging to the body.
Adverb from somatikos; corporeally or physically.
G4986: "of a safe father", Sopater, a Christian from Berea.
From the base of sozo and pater; of a safe father; Sopatrus, a Christian.
G4987: From another form of soros; to pile up (literally or figuratively).
G4988: "of safe strength", Sosthenes, the name of a ruler of a synagogue and of a Christian.
From the base of sozo and that of sthenoo; of safe strength; Sosthenes, a Christian.
G4989: "of a safe father", Sosipater, a Christian.
Prolongation for Sopatros; Sosipatrus, a Christian.
G499: typical of, representing by type (or pattern), corresponding to, an image.
Neuter of a compound of anti and tupos; corresponding ("antitype"), i.e. A representative, counterpart.
G4990: From sozo; a deliverer, i.e. God or Christ.
G4991: welfare, prosperity, deliverance, preservation, salvation, safety.
Feminine of a derivative of soter as (properly, abstract) noun; rescue or safety (physically or morally).
G4992: Neuter of the same as soteria as (properly, concretely) noun; defender or (by implication) defence.
G4993: to be of sound mind, be sober-minded, exercise self-control.
From sophron; to be of sound mind, i.e. Sane, (figuratively) moderate.
be in right mind, be sober (minded), soberly.
G4994: From sophron; to make of sound mind, i.e. (figuratively) to discipline or correct.
G4996: Adverb from sophron; with sound mind, i.e. Moderately.
G4997: soundness of mind, sanity; self-control, sobriety.
From sophron; soundness of mind, i.e. (literally) sanity or (figuratively) self-control.
G4998: of sound mind, self-controlled, temperate, sober-minded, modest, chaste.
From the base of sozo and that of phren; safe (sound) in mind, i.e. Self-controlled (moderate as to opinion or passion).
G4999: taverns; Three Taverns, the name of a village or town on the Appian Way, about thirty-three miles from Rome.
Plural of Latin origin; huts or wooden-walled buildings; Tabernoe.
G5: Of Chaldee origin ('ab); father as a vocative.
G50: to not know, be ignorant of (a person, thing, or fact), sometimes with the idea of willful ignorance.
From a (as a negative particle) and noieo; not to know (through lack of information or intelligence); by implication, to ignore (through disinclination).
(be) ignorant(-ly), not know, not understand, unknown.
G500: antichrist, either one who puts himself in the place of, or the enemy (opponent) of the Messiah.
From anti and Christos; an opponent of the Messiah.
G5000: "gazelle", Tabitha (also called Dorcas), a Christian woman.
Of Chaldee origin (compare tsbiyah); the gazelle; Tabitha (i.e. Tabjetha), a Christian female.
G5001: that which has been arranged in order, a division, rank.
From tasso; something orderly in arrangement (a troop), i.e. (figuratively) a series or succession.
G5002: From tasso; arranged, i.e. Appointed or stated.
G5003: to endure severe hardship, be harassed, complain.
From talaiporos; to be wretched, i.e. Realize one's own misery.
G5005: From the base of talanton and a derivative of the base of peira; enduring trial, i.e. Miserable.
G5006: worth a talent, of a talent's weight.
G5007: a balance, that which is weighed, a talent (about 3000 shekels in weight).

Neuter of a presumed derivative of the original form of tlao (to bear; equivalent to phero); a balance (as supporting weights), i.e. (by implication) a certain weight (and thence a coin or rather sum of money) or "talent".
G5008: Of Chaldee origin (compare taleh); the fresh, i.e. Young girl; talitha (O maiden).
G5009: a store-chamber, secret chamber, closet; a granary, barn.

Neuter contraction of a presumed derivative of tamias (a dispenser or distributor; akin to temno, to cut); a dispensary or magazine, i.e. A chamber on the ground-floor or interior of an Oriental house (generally used for storage or privacy, a spot for…
G501: to draw (generally water from a deep well in the ground); perhaps: to draw out.
From antlos (the hold of a ship); to bale up (properly, bilge water), i.e. Dip water (with a bucket, pitcher, etc.).
G5010: order, (a) regular arrangement, (b) appointed succession, (c) position, rank.
From tasso; regular arrangement, i.e. (in time) fixed succession (of rank or character), official dignity.
G5011: humble, lowly, in position or spirit (in a good sense).
Of uncertain derivation; depressed, i.e. (figuratively) humiliated (in circumstances or disposition).
base, cast down, humble, of low degree (estate), lowly.
G5012: From a compound of tapeinos and the base of phren; humiliation of mind, i.e. Modesty.
humbleness of mind, humility (of mind, loneliness (of mind).
G5013: to make or bring low, humble, humiliate; pass: to be humbled.
From tapeinos; to depress; figuratively, to humiliate (in condition or heart).
G5014: From tapeinoo; depression (in rank or feeling).
humiliation, be made low, low estate, vile.
G5015: to disturb, agitate, stir up, trouble.
Of uncertain affinity; to stir or agitate (roil water).
G5016: Feminine from tarasso; disturbance, i.e. (of water) roiling, or (of a mob) sedition.
G5017: Masculine from tarasso; a disturbance, i.e. (popular) tumult.
G5018: From Tarsos; a Tarsean, i.e. Native of Tarsus.
G5019: Tarsus, the capital of the Roman province Cilicia.
Perhaps the same as tarsos (a flat basket); Tarsus, a place in Asia Minor.
G502: what is drawn; a vessel or bucket to draw with.
G5020: to thrust down to Tartarus or Gehenna.
From Tartaros (the deepest abyss of Hades); to incarcerate in eternal torment.
G5021: (a) to assign, arrange, (b) to determine; mid: to appoint.
A prolonged form of a primary verb (which latter appears only in certain tenses); to arrange in an orderly manner, i.e. Assign or dispose (to a certain position or lot).
G5022: Apparently a primary word (compare towr, "steer"); a bullock.
G5023: Nominative or accusative case neuter plural of houtos; these things.
+ afterward, follow, + hereafter, X him, the same, so, such, that, then, these, they, this, those, thus.
G5024: Neuter plural of ho and autos as adverb; in the same way.
G5025: And tautas (tow'-tas) dative case and accusative case feminine plural respectively of houtos; (to or with or by, etc.) These.
G5026: And tauten (tow'-tane), and tautes (tow'-tace) dative case, accusative case and genitive case respectively of the feminine singular of houtos; (towards or of) this.
her, + hereof, it, that, + thereby, the (same), this (same).
G5028: Masculine from thapto; a grave (the place of interment).
G5029: As if neuter plural of tachus (adverbially); shortly, i.e. (figuratively) possibly.
G503: to face (lit: to present eye to), resist, withstand; as nautical term: to bear up against the wind.
From a compound of anti and ophthalmos; to face.
G5030: Adverb from tachus; briefly, i.e. (in time) speedily, or (in manner) rapidly.
G5032: Neuter singular of the comparative of tachus (as adverb); more swiftly, i.e. (in manner) more rapidly, or (in time) more speedily.
G5033: most swiftly, most quickly, as quickly as possible.
Neuter plural of the superlative of tachus (as adverb); most quickly, i.e. (with hos prefixed) as soon as possible.
G5034: From the same as tachus; a brief space (of time), i.e. (with en prefixed) in haste.
G5035: Neuter singular of tachus (as adverb); shortly, i.e. Without delay, soon, or (by surprise) suddenly, or (by implication, of ease) readily.
G5036: Of uncertain affinity; fleet, i.e. (figuratively) prompt or ready.
G5037: A primary particle (enclitic) of connection or addition; both or also (properly, as correlation of kai).
also, and, both, even, then, whether. Often used in composition, usually as the latter participle.
G5038: a wall, especially of a city.
Akin to the base of tikto; a wall (as formative of a house).
G5039: Neuter of a presumed derivative of tekmar (a goal or fixed limit); a token (as defining a fact), i.e. Criterion of certainty.
G504: without water, dry; subst: dry places, desert.
From a (as a negative particle) and hudor; waterless, i.e. Dry.
G5040: Diminutive of teknon; an infant, i.e. (plural figuratively) darlings (Christian converts).
G5041: to bear children, beget, rear a family.
From a compound of teknon and the base of ginomai; to be a child-bearer, i.e. Parent (mother).
G5042: child bearing, the rearing of a family.
From the same as teknogoneo; childbirth (parentage), i.e. (by implication) maternity (the performance of maternal duties).
G5043: From the base of timoria; a child (as produced).
G5044: to bring up children, rear young.
From a compound of teknon and trepho; to be a childrearer, i.e. Fulfil the duties of a female parent.
G5045: From the base of timoria; an artificer (as producer of fabrics), i.e. (specially), a craftsman in wood.
G5046: perfect, (a) complete in all its parts, (b) full grown, of full age, (c) specially of the completeness of Christian character.
From telos; complete (in various applications of labor, growth, mental and moral character, etc.); neuter (as noun, with ho) completeness.
G5047: From teleios; (the state) completeness (mentally or morally).
G5048: (a) as a course, a race, or the like: to complete, finish (b) as of time or prediction: to accomplish, (c) to make perfect; pass: to be perfected.
From teleios; to complete, i.e. (literally) accomplish, or (figuratively) consummate (in character).
G5049: Adverb from teleios; completely, i.e. (of hope) without wavering.
G505: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of hupokrinomai; undissembled, i.e. Sincere.
G5050: From phusioo; (the act) completion, i.e. (of prophecy) verification, or (of expiation) absolution.
G5051: From teleioo; a completer, i.e. Consummater.
G5052: to bring fruit to perfection, to bear perfect offspring.
From a compound of telos and phero; to be a bearer to completion (maturity), i.e. To ripen fruit (figuratively).
G5053: to complete, to come to an end, to die.
From a presumed derivative of teleo; to finish life (by implication, of bios), i.e. Expire (demise).
G5055: (a) to end, finish, (b) to fulfill, accomplish, (c) to pay.
From telos; to end, i.e. Complete, execute, conclude, discharge (a debt).
accomplish, make an end, expire, fill up, finish, go over, pay, perform.
G5056: (a) an end, (b) event or issue, (c) the principal end, aim, purpose, (d) a tax.

From a primary tello (to set out for a definite point or goal); properly, the point aimed at as a limit, i.e. (by implication) the conclusion of an act or state (termination (literally, figuratively or indefinitely), result (immediate, ultimate or prophetic),…
+ continual, custom, end(-ing), finally, uttermost. Compare phoros.
G5057: From telos and oneomai; a tax-farmer, i.e. Collector of public revenue.
G5058: Neuter of a presumed derivative of telones; a tax-gatherer's place of business.
G5059: Of uncertain affinity; a prodigy or omen.
G506: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of hupotasso; unsubdued, i.e. Insubordinate (in fact or temper).
disobedient, that is not put under, unruly.
G5060: Tertius, who wrote the Epistle to the Romans at Paul's dictation.
Of Latin origin; third; Tertius, a Christian.
G5061: Tertullus, a barrister acting as professional prosecutor of Paul at Caesarea.
Of uncertain derivation; Tertullus, a Roman.
G5063: From tessarakonta and etos; of forty years of age.
G5064: Or neuter tessara (tes'-sar-ah) a plural number; four.
G5065: From tessares and kai and dekatos; fourteenth.
G5066: of the fourth day, four days since.
From tessares; pertaining to the fourth day.
G5068: a tetrarch (the governor of a fourth part of a region).
From tessares and gonia; four-cornered, i.e. Square.
G5069: a group of four, a quaternion (a guard of four soldiers).
Neuter of a presumed derivative of tetras (a tetrad; from tessares); a quaternion or squad (picket) of four Roman soldiers.
G507: up, above, up to the top, up to the brim, things above, heaven, the heavenly region.
Adverb from anti; upward or on the top.
G5070: From the multiplicative adverb of tessares and chilioi; four times a thousand.
G5072: of four months, a period of four months.
Neuter of a compound of tessares and men; a four months' space.
G5073: From tessares and a derivative of the base of pleistos; quadruple.
G5074: From tessares and pous; a quadruped.
G5075: to rule over as a tetrarch.
From tetrarches; to be a tetrarch.
G5076: a tetrarch, ruler over a fourth part of a region.
From tessares and archo; the ruler of a fourth part of a country ("tetrarch").
G5077: to reduce to ashes, consume, destroy.
From tephra (ashes); to incinerate, i.e. Consume.
G5078: From the base of tikto; art (as productive), i.e. (specially), a trade, or (generally) skill.
G5079: From techne; an artisan; figuratively, a founder (Creator).
G508: From ano and ge; above the ground, i.e. (properly) the second floor of a building; used for a dome or a balcony on the upper story.
G5080: to make liquid; pass: to melt (away).
Apparently a primary verb; to liquefy.
G5081: Adverb from a compound of a derivative of telos and auge; in a far-shining manner, i.e. Plainly.
G5082: such as this, of persons so old, of things so great.
Or feminine telikaute (tay-lik-ow'-tay) from a compound of ho with helikos and houtos; such as this, i.e. (in (figurative) magnitude) so vast.
G5083: to keep, guard, observe, watch over.

From teros (a watch; perhaps akin to theoreo); to guard (from loss or injury, properly, by keeping the eye upon; and thus differing from phulasso, which is properly to prevent escaping; and from koustodia, which implies a fortress or full military lines of…
hold fast, keep(- er), (pre-, re-)serve, watch.
G5084: From tereo; a watching, i.e. (figuratively) observance, or (concretely) a prison.
G5085: Tiberias, a town in Galilee on the western border of the sea called after it.
From Tiberios; Tiberias, the name of a town and a lake in Palestine.
G5086: Tiberius, the second Roman emperor (died A.D. 37).
Of Latin origin; probably pertaining to the river Tiberis or Tiber; Tiberius, a Roman emperor.
G5087: to put, place, lay, set, fix, establish.

A prolonged form of a primary theo (theh'-o) (which is used only as alternate in certain tenses) to place (in the widest application, literally and figuratively; properly, in a passive or horizontal posture, and thus different from histemi, which properly…
+ advise, appoint, bow, commit, conceive, give, X kneel down, lay (aside, down, up), make, ordain, purpose, put, set (forth), settle, sink down.
G5088: to bear, bring forth, produce, beget, yield.
A strengthened form of a primary teko tek'-o (which is used only as alternate in certain tenses); to produce (from seed, as a mother, a plant, the earth, etc.), literally or figuratively.
bear, be born, bring forth, be delivered, be in travail.
G5089: Perhaps akin to the alternate of haireomai, and thus to suro; to pull off.
G509: (a) from above, from heaven, (b) from the beginning, from their origin (source), from of old, (c) again, anew.
From ano; from above; by analogy, from the first; by implication, anew.
from above, again, from the beginning (very first), the top.
G5090: Timaeus, father of the blind beggar Bartimaeus.
Probably of Chaldee origin (compare tame'); Timoeus (i.e. Timay), an Israelite.
G5091: (a) to value at a price, estimate, (b) to honor, reverence.
From timios; to prize, i.e. Fix a valuation upon; by implication, to revere.
G5092: From tino; a value, i.e. Money paid, or (concretely and collectively) valuables; by analogy, esteem (especially of the highest degree), or the dignity itself.
G5093: Including the comparative timioteros (tim-ee-o'-ter-os), and the superlative timiotatos (tim-ee-o'-tat-os) from time; valuable, i.e. (objectively) costly, or (subjectively) honored, esteemed, or (figuratively) beloved.
dear, honourable, (more, most) precious, had in reputation.
G5094: From timios; expensiveness, i.e. (by implication) magnificence.
G5095: Timothy, a Christian of Lystra, helper of Paul.
From time and theos; dear to God; Timotheus, a Christian.
G5096: Timon, one of the seven original deacons at Jerusalem.
From time; valuable; Timon, a Christian.
G5097: From a comparative of time and ouros (a guard); properly, to protect one's honor, i.e. To avenge (inflict a penalty).
G5098: From timoreo; vindication, i.e. (by implication) a penalty.
G5099: to pay, to pay a penalty.
Strengthened for a primary tio (tee'-o) (which is only used as an alternate in certain tenses) to pay a price, i.e. As a penalty.
G51: an offence committed through ignorance, an error due to (willful or culpable) ignorance.
From agnoeo; a thing ignored, i.e. Shortcoming.
G510: From anoteros; superior, i.e. (locally) more remote.
G5100: any one, some one, a certain one or thing.
An enclitic indefinite pronoun; some or any person or object.

a (kind of), any (man, thing, thing at all), certain (thing), divers, he (every) man, one (X thing), ought, + partly, some (man, -body, - thing, -what), (+ that no-)thing, what(-soever), X wherewith,…
G5101: Probably emphatic of tis; an interrogative pronoun, who, which or what (in direct or indirect questions).
every man, how (much), + no(-ne, thing), what (manner, thing), where (-by, -fore, -of, -unto, - with, -withal), whether, which, who(-m, -se), why.
G5102: Of Latin origin; a titulus or "title" (placard).
G5103: Titus, a Greek Christian, helper of Paul, perhaps also brother of Luke.
Of Latin origin but uncertain significance; Titus, a Christian.
G5104: an enclitic particle of asseveration used as a prefix or suff. in the N.T.
Probably for the dative case of ho; an enclitic particle of asseveration by way of contrast; in sooth.
(used only with other particles in the comparative, as kaitoige, mentoi, toigaroun, toinun, etc.)
G5105: consequently, therefore, well then, so then.
From toi and gar and oun; truly for then, i.e. Consequently.
G5106: indeed now, therefore, accordingly, well then.
From toi and nun; truly now, i.e. Accordingly.
G5107: of this kind, such, such as follows.
(including the other inflections); from a derivative of toi and de; such-like then, i.e. So great.
G5108: (including the other inflections); from toi and houtos; truly this, i.e. Of this sort (to denote character or individuality).
G5109: Another form of teichos; a wall.
G511: higher, to a more honorable place (at the dinner table); previously, in an earlier passage (or a book), above.
Comparative degree of ano; upper, i.e. (neuter as adverb) to a more conspicuous place, in a former part of the book.
G5110: a bringing forth, birth, interest, usury.
From the base of tikto; interest on money loaned (as a produce).
G5111: to dare, endure, be bold, have courage, make up the mind.

From tolma (boldness; probably itself from the base of telos through the idea of extreme conduct); to venture (objectively or in act; while tharrheo is rather subjective or in feeling); by implication, to be courageous.
G5112: more boldly, more freely, with more confidence.
Neuter of the compound of a derivative of the base of tolmao (as adverb); more daringly, i.e. With greater confidence than otherwise.
G5114: Comparative of a derivative of the primary temno (to cut; more comprehensive or decisive than kopto, as if by a single stroke; whereas that implies repeated blows, like hacking); more keen.
G5115: From the base of tikto; a bow (apparently as the simplest fabric).
G5116: Neuter of a presumed derivative (alternately) of topazos (a "topaz"; of uncertain origin); a gem, probably the chrysolite.
G5117: a place, region, seat; an opportunity.

Apparently a primary word; a spot (general in space, but limited by occupancy; whereas chora is a large but participle locality), i.e. Location (as a position, home, tract, etc.); figuratively, condition, opportunity; specially, a scabbard.
coast, licence, place, X plain, quarter, + rock, room, where.
G5118: so great, so large, so long, so many.
From tosos (so much; apparently from ho and hos) and houtos (including its variations); so vast as this, i.e. Such (in quantity, amount, number of space).
as large, so great (long, many, much), these many.
G5119: From (the neuter of) ho and hote; the when, i.e. At the time that (of the past or future, also in consecution).
G512: From a (as a negative particle) and the base of ophelimos; useless or (neuter) inutility.
G5120: Properly, the genitive case of ho; sometimes used for toutou; of this person.
G5121: on the contrary, on the other hand.
Contraction for the neuter of ho and enantion; on the contrary.
G5122: Contraction for the neuter of ho and onoma; the name (is).
G5123: Contraction for touto and esti; that is.
G5124: Neuter singular nominative or accusative case of houtos; that thing.
here (-unto), it, partly, self(-same), so, that (intent), the same, there(-fore, -unto), this, thus, where(-fore).
G5125: Dative case plural masculine or neuter of houtos; to (for, in, with or by) these (persons or things).
such, them, there(-in, -with), these, this, those.
G5126: Accusative case singular masculine of houtos; this (person, as objective of verb or preposition).
G5127: Genitive case singular masculine or neuter of houtos; of (from or concerning) this (person or thing).
here(-by), him, it, + such manner of, that, thence(-forth), thereabout, this, thus.
G5128: Accusative case plural masculine of houtos; these (persons, as objective of verb or preposition).
G5129: Dative case singular masculine or neuter of houtos; to (in, with or by) this (person or thing).
here(-by, -in), him, one, the same, there(-in), this.
G513: Probably from agnumi (to break; compare rhegnumi); an axe.
G5130: Genitive case plural masculine or neuter of houtos; of (from or concerning) these (persons or things).
such, their, these (things), they, this sort, those.
G5131: From the base of trogo; a he-goat (as a gnawer).
G5132: a table, (a) for food or banqueting, (b) for money-changing or business.

Probably contracted from tessares and peze; a table or stool (as being four-legged), usually for food (figuratively, a meal); also a counter for money (figuratively, a broker's office for loans at interest).
G5133: From trapeza; a money-broker or banker.
G5134: From the base of titrosko (to wound; akin to the base of thrauo, tribos, trizo, etc.); a wound.
G5135: From trauma; to inflict a wound.
G5136: to take by the throat, to overthrow.
From trachelos; to seize by the throat or neck, i.e. To expose the gullet of a victim for killing (generally, to lay bare).
G5137: Probably from trecho (through the idea of mobility); the throat (neck), i.e. (figuratively) life.
G5138: Perhaps strengthened from the base of rhegnumi (as if jagged by rents); uneven, rocky (reefy).
G5139: Trachonitis, the north-east of the territory beyond Jordan.
From a derivative of trachus; rough district; Trachonitis, a region of Syria.
G514: worthy, worthy of, deserving, comparable, suitable.
Probably from ago; deserving, comparable or suitable (as if drawing praise).
G5140: Or neuter tria (tree'-ah) a primary (plural) number; "three".
G5141: Strengthened from a primary treo (to "dread", "terrify"); to "tremble" or fear.
G5142: to feed, nourish; to bring up, rear, provide for.

A primary verb (properly, threpho; but perhaps strengthened from the base of trope through the idea of convolution); properly, to stiffen, i.e. Fatten (by implication, to cherish (with food, etc.), pamper, rear).
G5143: to run, exercise myself, make progress.
Apparently a primary verb (properly, threcho; compare thrix); which uses dremo drem'-o (the base of dromos) as alternate in certain tenses; to run or walk hastily (literally or figuratively).
G5145: Plural from treis and hekaton; three hundred.
G5146: From treis and belos; properly, a crow-foot (three-pronged obstruction in war), i.e. (by analogy) a thorny plant (caltrop).
G5147: a worn path, beaten way, road, highway.
From tribo (to "rub"; akin to teiro, truo, and the base of tragos, trauma); a rut or worn track.
G5148: From a compound of treis and etos; a three years' period (triennium).
G5149: to cry, chirp, to grind the teeth.
Apparently a primary verb; to creak (squeak), i.e. (by analogy) to grate the teeth (in frenzy).
G515: to account or treat as worthy.
From axios; to deem entitled or fit.
G5150: Neuter of a compound of treis and men as noun; a three months' space.
G5152: having three stories; subst: the third story.
Neuter of a compound of treis and stege as noun; a third roof (story).
G5153: From tris and chilioi; three times a thousand.
G5154: Ordinal from treis; third; neuter (as noun) a third part, or (as adverb) a (or the) third time, thirdly.
G5155: From thrix; hairy, i.e. Made of hair (mohair).
G5156: From tremo; a "trembling", i.e. Quaking with fear.
G5157: From an apparently primary trepo to turn; a turn ("trope"), i.e. Revolution (figuratively, variation).
G5158: (a) way, manner, (b) manner of life, character.
From the same as trope; a turn, i.e. (by implication) mode or style (especially with preposition or relative prefix as adverb, like); figuratively, deportment or character.
(even) as, conversation, (+ like) manner, (+ by any) means, way.
G5159: to endure the ways of, put up with.
From tropos and phoreo; to endure one's habits.
G516: worthily, in a manner worthy of.
as becometh, after a godly sort, worthily(-thy).
G5160: From trepho; nourishment (literally or figuratively); by implication, rations (wages).
G5161: Trophimus, a Christian of Ephesus in Asia.
From trophe; nutritive; Trophimus, a Christian.
G5162: From trepho; a nourisher, i.e. Nurse.
G5163: the track of a wheel, a track, path.
From trochos; a track (as a wheel-rut), i.e. (figuratively) a course of conduct.
G5164: From trecho; a wheel (as a runner), i.e. (figuratively) a circuit of physical effects.
G5165: Neuter of a presumed derivative of uncertain affinity; a bowl.
G5166: From a derivative of trugo (to dry) meaning ripe fruit (as if dry); to collect the vintage.
G5167: From truzo (to murmur; akin to trizo, but denoting a duller sound); a turtle-dove (as cooing).
G5168: From a derivative of truo (to wear away; akin to the base of trauma, tribos and trogo); an orifice, i.e. Needle's eye.
G5169: a hole; the eye of a needle.
From a derivative of the base of trumalia; an aperture, i.e. A needle's eye.
G517: From a (as a negative particle) and horatos; invisible.
G5170: Tryphaena, a Christian woman in Rome.
From truphe; luxurious; Tryphoena, a Christian woman.
G5171: to live a luxurious life, live self-indulgently.
From truphe; to indulge in luxury.
G5172: From thrupto (to break up or (figuratively) enfeeble, especially the mind and body by indulgence); effeminacy, i.e. Luxury or debauchery.
G5173: Tryphosa, a Christian woman in Rome, perhaps a sister of Tryphaena.
From truphe; luxuriating; Tryphosa, a Christian female.
G5174: Troas, a city near the Hellespont (i.e. Dardanelles).
From Tros (a Trojan); the Troad (or plain of Troy), i.e. Troas, a place in Asia Minor.
G5175: Trogyllium, a promontory somewhat to the south of Ephesus.
Of uncertain derivation; Trogyllium, a place in Asia Minor.
G5176: to eat, partake of a meal.

Probably strengthened from a collateral form of the base of trauma and tribos through the idea of corrosion or wear; or perhaps rather of a base of trugon and trizo through the idea of a craunching sound; to gnaw or chew, i.e. (generally) to eat.
G5177: (a) gen: to obtain, (b) absol: to chance, happen; ordinary, everyday, it may chance, perhaps.

Probably for an obsolete tucho (for which the middle voice of another alternate teucho (to make ready or bring to pass) is used in certain tenses; akin to the base of tikto through the idea of effecting; properly, to affect; or (specially), to hit or light…
be, chance, enjoy, little, obtain, X refresh...self, + special. Compare tupto.
G5178: to torture, break on the wheel, beat to death.
From a derivative of tupto (meaning a drum, "tympanum"); to stretch on an instrument of torture resembling a drum, and thus beat to death.
G5179: (originally: the mark of a blow, then a stamp struck by a die), (a) a figure; a copy, image, (b) a pattern, model, (c) a type, prefiguring something or somebody.

From tupto; a die (as struck), i.e. (by implication) a stamp or scar; by analogy, a shape, i.e. A statue, (figuratively) style or resemblance; specially, a sampler ("type"), i.e. A model (for imitation) or instance (for warning).
en-(ex-)ample, fashion, figure, form, manner, pattern, print.
G518: to report (from one place to another), bring a report, announce, declare.
From apo and the base of aggelos; to announce.
bring word (again), declare, report, shew (again), tell.
G5180: to beat, strike, wound, inflict punishment.

A primary verb (in a strengthened form); to "thump", i.e. Cudgel or pummel (properly, with a stick or bastinado), but in any case by repeated blows; thus differing from paio and patasso, which denote a (usually single) blow with the hand or any instrument, or…
G5181: Tyrannus, an inhabitant of Ephesus, probably a rhetorician.
A provincial form of the derivative of the base of kurios; a "tyrant"; Tyrannus, an Ephesian.
G5182: to agitate or disturb in mind, trouble.
From turbe (Latin turba, a crowd; akin to thorubos); to make "turbid", i.e. Disturb.
G5183: a Tyrian, an inhabitant of Tyre.
From Turos; a Tyrian, i.e. Inhabitant of Tyrus.
G5184: Tyre, an ancient city, the capital of Phoenicia.
Of Hebrew origin (Tsor): Tyrus (i.e. Tsor), a place in Palestine.
G5185: From, tuphoo; opaque (as if smoky), i.e. (by analogy) blind (physically or mentally).
G5186: to make blind, physically or mentally.
From tuphlos; to make blind, i.e. (figuratively) to obscure.
G5187: to puff up, make haughty; pass: to be puffed up, be haughty.
From a derivative of tupho; to envelop with smoke, i.e. (figuratively) to inflate with self-conceit.
high-minded, be lifted up with pride, be proud.
G5188: Apparently a primary verb; to make a smoke, i.e. Slowly consume without flame.
G5189: From a derivative of tupho; stormy (as if smoky).
G519: to choke, strangle; mid: to strangle or hang myself.
From apo and agcho (to choke; akin to the base of agkale); to strangle oneself off (i.e. To death).
G5190: Tychicus, a Christian of the Roman province Asia.
From a derivative of tugchano; fortuitous, i.e. Fortunate; Tychicus, a Christian.
G5191: dark purple or blue, of the color of hyacinth.
From huakinthos; "hyacinthine" or "jacinthine", i.e. Deep blue.
G5192: jacinth, a precious stone of the color of hyacinth.
Of uncertain derivation; the "hyacinth" or "jacinth", i.e. Some gem of a deep blue color, probably the zirkon.
G5194: Perhaps from the same as huetos (as being transparent like rain); glass.
G5195: to run riot, to outrage, insult.
From hubris; to exercise violence, i.e. Abuse.
G5196: wantonness, insolence, an act of wanton violence.
From huper; insolence (as over-bearing), i.e. Insult, injury.
G5197: an insolent, insulting, or violent man.
From hubrizo; an insulter, i.e. Maltreater.
G5198: to be well, be in good health; to be right, reasonable, sound, pure, uncorrupted.
From hugies; to have sound health, i.e. Be well (in body); figuratively, to be uncorrupt (true in doctrine).
be in health, (be safe and) sound, (be) whole(-some).
G5199: From the base of auzano; healthy, i.e. Well (in body); figuratively, true (in doctrine).
G52: ignorance, inadvertence, sometimes with the idea of willful blindness.
G520: to lead, carry, take away; met: to be led astray, seduced.
From apo and ago; to take off (in various senses).
bring, carry away, lead (away), put to death, take away.
G5200: From the base of huetos; wet (as if with rain), i.e. (by implication) sappy (fresh).
G5201: a water pot, a pot or jar.
From hudor; a water-jar, i.e. Receptacle for family supply.
G5202: to be only a water drinker.
From a compound of hudor and a derivative of pino; to be a water-drinker, i.e. To abstain from vinous beverages.
G5203: From a compound of hudor and a derivative of optanomai (as if looking watery); to be "dropsical".
G5204: And genitive case, hudatos (hoo'-dat-os), etc. From the base of huetos; water (as if rainy) literally or figuratively.
G5205: From a primary huo (to rain); rain, especially a shower.
G5206: adoption, as a son into the divine family.
From a presumed compound of huios and a derivative of tithemi; the placing as a son, i.e. Adoption (figuratively, Christian sonship in respect to God).
G5207: Apparently a primary word; a "son" (sometimes of animals), used very widely of immediate, remote or figuratively, kinship.
G5208: Perhaps akin to xulon; a forest, i.e. (by implication) fuel.
G5209: Accusative case of humeis; you (as the objective of a verb or preposition).
G521: untrained, uneducated, showing a want of training or education, ignorant.
From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of paideuo; uninstructed, i.e. (figuratively) stupid.
G5210: Irregular plural of su; you (as subjective of verb).
G5211: Hymenaeus, a heretical teacher at Ephesus.
From Humen (the god of weddings); "hymeneal"; Hymeneus, an opponent of Christianity.
G5212: From humeis; yours, i.e. Pertaining to you.
G5213: Irregular dative case of humeis; to (with or by) you.
G5214: to sing, sing hymns to, praise.
From humnos; to hymn, i.e. Sing a religious ode; by implication, to celebrate (God) in song.
G5215: a hymn, sacred song, song of praise to God.
Apparently from a simpler (obsolete) form of hudeo (to celebrate; probably akin to aido; compare abowt); a "hymn" or religious ode (one of the Psalms).
G5216: Genitive case of humeis; of (from or concerning) you.
G5217: to lead or bring under, to lead on slowly, to depart.
From hupo and ago; to lead (oneself) under, i.e. Withdraw or retire (as if sinking out of sight), literally or figuratively.
G5218: From hupakouo; attentive hearkening, i.e. (by implication) compliance or submission.
G5219: to listen, hearken to, obey, answer.
From hupo and akouo; to hear under (as a subordinate), i.e. To listen attentively; by implication, to heed or conform to a command or authority.
G522: to take away, remove; pass: to be taken away, withdrawn.
From apo and airo; to lift off, i.e. Remove.
G5220: under the power of or subject to a man.
From hupo and aner; in subjection under a man, i.e. A married woman.
G5221: to go to meet, to meet.
From hupo and a derivative of anti; to go opposite (meet) under (quietly), i.e. To encounter, fall in with.
G5222: From hupantao; an encounter or concurrence (with eis for infinitive, in order to fall in with).
G5223: From huparcho; existency or proprietorship, i.e. (concretely) property, wealth.
G5224: goods, that which one has, things which one possesseth, substance, that hast.
Neuter plural of present participle active of huparcho as noun; things extant or in hand, i.e. Property or possessions.
goods, that which one has, things which (one) possesseth, substance, that hast.
G5225: to begin, to be ready or at hand, to be.

From hupo and archomai; to begin under (quietly), i.e. Come into existence (be present or at hand); expletively, to exist (as copula or subordinate to an adjective, participle, adverb or preposition, or as an auxiliary to a principal (verb).
G5226: From hupo and eiko (to yield, be "weak"); to surrender.
G5227: opposite to, adverse; subst: an adversary.
From hupo and enantios; under (covertly) contrary to, i.e. Opposed or (as noun) an opponent.
G5228: over, beyond, on behalf of, for the sake of, concerning.
A primary preposition; "over", i.e. (with the genitive case) of place, above, beyond, across, or causal, for the sake of, instead, regarding; with the accusative case superior to, more than.
(+ exceeding, abundantly) above, in (on) behalf of, beyond, by, + very chiefest, concerning, exceeding (above, -ly), for, + very highly, more (than), of, over, on the part of, for sake of, in stead,…
G5229: lit: to raise beyond, uplift; mid: to lift myself up, exalt myself, be arrogant.
Middle voice from huper and airo; to raise oneself over, i.e. (figuratively) to become haughty.
exalt self, be exalted above measure.
G523: to ask back, ask what is due, demand back.
From apo and aiteo; to demand back.
G5230: past the bloom of youth, of full age.
From huper and the base of akmen; beyond the "acme", i.e. Figuratively (of a daughter) past the bloom (prime) of youth.
G5231: From huper and ano; above upward, i.e. Greatly higher (in place or rank).
G5232: to increase exceedingly or beyond measure.
From huper and auzano; to increase above ordinary degree.
G5233: to transgress; to go beyond, overreach, defraud.
From huper and the base of basis; to transcend, i.e. (figuratively) to overreach.
G5234: Adverb from present participle active of huperballo; excessively.
G5235: to throw over or beyond, to run beyond.
From huper and ballo; to throw beyod the usual mark, i.e. (figuratively) to surpass (only active participle supereminent).
G5236: excess, surpassing excellence, preeminence; adv: exceedingly.
From huperballo; a throwing beyond others, i.e. (figuratively) supereminence; adverbially (with eis or kata) pre- eminently.
abundance, (far more) exceeding, excellency, more excellent, beyond (out of) measure.
G5237: to overlook, take no notice of, disregard.
From huper and eido; to overlook, i.e. Not punish.
G5238: From huper and the neuter plural of ekeinos; above those parts, i.e. Still farther.
G5239: to over-stretch, stretch out beyond the measure assigned to me.
From huper and ekteino; to extend inordinately.
G524: (lit: to cease to feel [my] pain), be past feeling, cease to care (suggesting sometimes despair, sometimes recklessness), become callous, reckless.
From apo and algeo (to smart); to grieve out, i.e. Become apathetic.
G5240: to pour out so that it overflows.
From huper and the alternate form of ekcheo; to pour out over, i.e. (passively) to overflow.
G5241: to intercede for, make petition for.
From huper and entugchano; to intercede in behalf of.
G5242: to hold above, to rise above, to be superior.
From huper and echo; to hold oneself above, i.e. (figuratively) to excel; participle (as adjective, or neuter as noun) superior, superiority.
G5244: From huper and phaino; appearing above others (conspicuous), i.e. (figuratively) haughty.
G5245: to be more than conqueror, prevail mightily.
From huper and nikao; to vanquish beyond, i.e. Gain a decisive victory.
G5246: From huper and ogkos; bulging over, i.e. (figuratively) insolent.
G5247: From huperecho; prominence, i.e. (figuratively) superiority (in rank or character).
G5248: (a) intrans: to abound exceedingly, (b) dep: to overflow.
From huper and perisseuo; to super-abound.
G5249: From huper and perissos; superabundantly, i.e. Exceedingly.
G525: to free (a person) from (anything), oftener in the middle voice: to be released from, be rid of (a person or thing), depart.
From apo and allasso; to change away, i.e. Release, (reflexively) remove.
G5250: to abound exceedingly, be exceedingly abundant.
From huper and pleonazo; to superabound.
G5251: From huper and hupsoo; to elevate above others, i.e. Raise to the highest position.
G5252: to be overly proud, to have high thoughts.
From huper and phroneo; to esteem oneself overmuch, i.e. Be vain or arrogant.
G5253: an upper room, the upper part of a house.
Neuter of a derivative of huper; a higher part of the house, i.e. Apartment in the third story.
G5254: to hold or put under, to undergo.
From hupo and echo; to hold oneself under, i.e. Endure with patience.
G5255: From hupakouo; attentively listening, i.e. (by implication) submissive.
G5256: to serve as a rower, to minister to, serve.
From huperetes; to be a subordinate, i.e. (by implication) subserve.
G5257: a servant, an attendant, (a) an officer, lictor, (b) an attendant in a synagogue, (c) a minister of the gospel.
From hupo and a derivative of eresso (to row); an under-oarsman, i.e. (generally) subordinate (assistant, sexton, constable).
G5258: From an obsolete primary (perhaps akin to hupo through the idea of subsilience); sleep, i.e. (figuratively) spiritual torpor.
G5259: A primary preposition; under, i.e. (with the genitive case) of place (beneath), or with verbs (the agency or means, through); (with the accusative case) of place (whither (underneath) or where (below) or time (when (at)).
among, by, from, in, of, under, with. In the comparative, it retains the same general applications, especially of inferior position or condition, and specially, covertly or moderately.
G526: to estrange, alienate; pass: to be alienated from.
From apo and a derivative of allotrios; to estrange away, i.e. (passively and figuratively) to be non-participant.
G5260: to throw or put under; met: to subject, submit, suggest, whisper, prompt, suborn, instigate.
From hupo and ballo; to throw in stealthily, i.e. Introduce by collusion.
G5261: From a compound of hupo and grapho; an underwriting, i.e. Copy for imitation (figuratively).
G5262: (a) a figure, copy, (b) an example, model.
From hupodeiknumi; an exhibit for imitation or warning (figuratively, specimen, adumbration).
G5263: to show secretly, to show by tracing out, to teach, make known.
From hupo and deiknuo; to exhibit under the eyes, i.e. (figuratively) to exemplify (instruct, admonish).
G5264: to receive as a guest, entertain hospitably, welcome.
From hupo and dechomai; to admit under one's roof, i.e. Entertain hospitably.
G5265: (lit: to bind under), mid: to put on feet, pass: to be shod.
From hupo and deo; to bind under one's feet, i.e. Put on shoes or sandals.
G5266: a sole bound under (the foot), a sandal.
From hupodeo; something bound under the feet, i.e. A shoe or sandal.
G5267: answerable to, liable to (brought under) the judgment of.
From hupo and dike; under sentence, i.e. (by implication) condemned.
G5268: a beast of burden, an ass or mule.
Neuter of a compound of hupo and zugos; an animal under the yoke (draught-beast), i.e. (specially), a donkey.
G5269: to under-gird, as to strengthen a ship against the waves.
From hupo and zonnumi; to gird under, i.e. Frap (a vessel with cables across the keel, sides and deck).
G527: soft, tender, as a shoot of a tree.
G5270: From hupo and kato; down under, i.e. Beneath.
G5271: to answer, reply, to answer on a stage, to pretend.
Middle voice from hupo and krino; to decide (speak or act) under a false part, i.e. (figuratively) dissemble (pretend).
G5272: (lit: stage-playing), a response, answer, hypocrisy, dissembling.
From hupokrinomai; acting under a feigned part, i.e. (figuratively) deceit ("hypocrisy").
G5273: (lit: a stage-player), a hypocrite, dissembler, pretender.
From hupokrinomai; an actor under an assumed character (stage-player), i.e. (figuratively) a dissembler ("hypocrite".
G5274: (a) to take up, (b) to welcome, entertain, (c) to answer, (d) to suppose, imagine.
From hupo and lambano; to take from below, i.e. Carry upward; figuratively, to take up, i.e. Continue a discourse or topic; mentally, to assume (presume).
G5275: to leave behind; pass: to be left surviving.
From hupotrecho and leipo; to leave under (behind), i.e. (passively) to remain (survive).
G5276: a vessel or trough beneath a winepress (to receive the juice).
Neuter of a presumed compound of hupo and lenos; vessel or receptacle under the press, i.e. Lower wine-vat.
G5277: A prolonged form for hupoleipo; to leave behind, i.e. Bequeath.
G5278: (a) to remain behind, (b) to stand ground, show endurance, (c) to endure, bear up against, persevere.
From hupo and meno; to stay under (behind), i.e. Remain; figuratively, to undergo, i.e. Bear (trials), have fortitude, persevere.
abide, endure, (take) patient(-ly), suffer, tarry behind.
G5279: to remind; pass: to remember, call to mind.
From hupo and mimnesko; to remind quietly, i.e. Suggest to the (middle voice, one's own) memory.
put in mind, remember, bring to (put in) remembrance.
G528: to go to meet, meet, encounter.
From apo and a derivative of anti; to meet away, i.e. Encounter.
G5280: remembrance, recollection, putting in mind; a reminder.
From hupomimnesko; a reminding or (reflexively) recollection.
G5281: From hupomeno; cheerful (or hopeful) endurance, constancy.
G5282: From hupo and noieo; to think under (privately), i.e. To surmise or conjecture.
G5284: to sail under (i.e. under the lee of).
From hupo and pleo; to sail under the lee of.
G5285: From hupo and pneo; to breathe gently, i.e. Breeze.
G5286: Neuter of a compound of hupo and pous; something under the feet, i.e. A foot-rest (figuratively).
G5287: (lit: an underlying), (a) confidence, assurance, (b) a giving substance (or reality) to, or a guaranteeing, (c) substance, reality.
From a compound of hupo and histemi; a setting under (support), i.e. (figuratively) concretely, essence, or abstractly, assurance (objectively or subjectively).
G5288: to withdraw, draw back, keep back, shun, conceal.
From hupo and stello; to withhold under (out of sight), i.e. (reflexively) to cower or shrink, (figuratively) to conceal (reserve).
G5289: a letting down, a shrinking back.
From hupostello; shrinkage (timidity), i.e. (by implication) apostasy.
G529: the act of meeting, to meet (a phrase seemingly almost technical for the reception of a newly arrived official).
G5290: From hupo and strepho; to turn under (behind), i.e. To return (literally or figuratively).
come again, return (again, back again), turn back (again).
G5291: From hupo and stronnumi; to strew underneath (the feet as a carpet).
G5293: to place under, subject to; mid, pass: to submit, put myself into subjection.
From hupo and tasso; to subordinate; reflexively, to obey.
be under obedience (obedient), put under, subdue unto, (be, make) subject (to, unto), be (put) in subjection (to, under), submit self unto.
G5294: to put under, lay down, suggest to, put in mind.
From hupo and tithemi; to place underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to hazard, (reflexively) to suggest.
G5295: From hupo and trecho (including its alternate); to run under, i.e. (specially), to sail past.
G5296: a pattern, example; a form, sample.
From a compound of hupo and a derivative of tupos; typification under (after), i.e. (concretely) a sketch (figuratively) for imitation.
G5297: to bear by being under, to endure.
From hupo and phero; to bear from underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to undergo hardship.
G5298: to withdraw, retire, go back, retreat.
From hupo and choreo; to vacate down, i.e. Retire quietly.
G5299: to strike under the eye, hence: to bruise, treat severely, discipline by hardship, molest, annoy, harass, worry, exhaust.

From a compound of hupo and a derivative of optanomai; to hit under the eye (buffet or disable an antagonist as a pugilist), i.e. (figuratively) to tease or annoy (into compliance), subdue (one's passions).
G53: (originally, in a condition prepared for worship), pure (either ethically, or ritually, ceremonially), chaste.
From the same as hagios; properly, clean, i.e. (figuratively) innocent, modest, perfect.
G530: Probably from hapas; one (or a single) time (numerically or conclusively).
G5300: Apparently a primary word; a hog ("swine").
G5301: hyssop, a stalk or stem of hyssop.
G5302: to fall behind, be lacking, fall short, suffer need, be inferior to.
From husteros; to be later, i.e. (by implication) to be inferior; generally, to fall short (be deficient).
come behind (short), be destitute, fail, lack, suffer need, (be in) want, be the worse.
G5303: (a) of things or persons: that which is lacking, a defect or shortcoming, (b) want, poverty.
From hustereo; a deficit; specially, poverty.
that which is behind, (that which was) lack(-ing), penury, want.
G5305: Neuter of husteros as adverb; more lately, i.e. Eventually.
G5306: Comparative from hupo (in the sense of behind); later.
G5307: From huphaino to weave; woven, i.e. (perhaps) knitted.
G5308: From hupsos; lofty (in place or character).
G5309: From a compound of hupselos and phren; to be lofty in mind, i.e. Arrogant.
G531: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of parabaino; not passing away, i.e. Untransferable (perpetual).
G5310: Superlative from the base of hupsos; highest, i.e. (masculine singular) the Supreme (God), or (neuter plural) the heavens.
G5311: From a derivative of huper; elevation, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, (specially), the sky, or (figuratively) dignity.
G5312: (a) to raise on high, lift up, (b) to exalt, set on high.
From hupsos; to elevate (literally or figuratively).
G5313: From hupsoo; an elevated place or thing, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, or (by implication) a barrier (figuratively).
G5315: to eat, partake of food; met: to devour, consume (e.g. as rust does); used only in fut. and 2nd aor. tenses.
A primary verb (used as an alternate of esthio in certain tenses); to eat (literally or figuratively).
G5316: (a) act: to shine, shed light, (b) pass: to shine, become visible, appear, (c) to become clear, appear, seem, show myself as.
Prolongation for the base of phos; to lighten (shine), i.e. Show (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative).
appear, seem, be seen, shine, X think.
G5317: Peleg, son of Eber, and one of the ancestors of Jesus.
Of Hebrew origin (Peleg); Phalek (i.e. Peleg), a patriarch.
G5318: apparent, clear, visible, manifest; adv: clearly.
From phaino; shining, i.e. Apparent (literally or figuratively); neuter (as adverb) publicly, externally.
abroad, + appear, known, manifest, open (+ -ly), outward (+ -ly).
G5319: to make clear (visible, manifest), make known.
From phaneros; to render apparent (literally or figuratively).
G532: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of paraskeuazo; unready.
G5320: Adverb from phaneros; plainly, i.e. Clearly or publicly.
G5321: From phaneroo; exhibition, i.e. (figuratively) expression, (by extension) a bestowment.
G5322: From phaino; a lightener, i.e. Light; lantern.
G5323: Phanuel, father of Anna the prophetess.
Of Hebrew origin (Pnuw'el); Phanuel (i.e. Penuel), an Israelite.
G5324: to make visible, to become visible.
From a derivative of phaino; to make apparent, i.e. (passively) to appear (neuter participle as noun, a spectacle).
G5325: From a derivative of phantazo; (properly abstract) a (vain) show ("fantasy").
G5326: From phantazo; (properly concrete) a (mere) show ("phantasm"), i.e. Spectre.
G5327: Properly, strengthened from the base of peran or rather of rhegnumi; a gap or chasm, i.e. Ravine (winter-torrent).
G5328: Pharaoh, the title of ancient Egyptian kings.
Of foreign origin (Par'oh); Pharao (i.e. Pharoh), an Egyptian king.
G5329: Perez, son of Judah and one of the ancestors of Jesus.
Of Hebrew origin (Perets); Phares (i.e. Perets), an Israelite.
G533: to deny, disown, repudiate (either another person or myself), disregard.
From apo and arneomai; to deny utterly, i.e. Disown, abstain.
G5330: a Pharisee, member of a Jewish religious sect.
Of Hebrew origin (compare parash); a separatist, i.e. Exclusively religious; a Pharisean, i.e. Jewish sectary.
G5331: the use of medicine, drugs or spells.
From pharmakeus; medication ("pharmacy"), i.e. (by extension) magic (literally or figuratively).
G5332: From pharmakon (a drug, i.e. Spell-giving potion); a druggist ("pharmacist") or poisoner, i.e. (by extension) a magician.
G5334: From phemi (not the same as "phase", which is from phaino); a saying, i.e. Report.
G5335: Prolongation from the same as phemi; to assert.
G5336: From pateomai (to eat); a crib (for fodder).
G5337: Apparently a primary word; "foul" or "flawy", i.e. (figuratively) wicked.
G5338: Probably akin to the base of phos (compare phtheggomai); brilliancy.
G5339: Of uncertain affinity; to be chary of, i.e. (subjectively) to abstain or (objectively) to treat leniently.
G534: From apo and arti; from now, i.e. Henceforth (already).
G5340: Adverb from participle of pheidomai; abstemiously, i.e. Stingily.
G5341: By transposition for a derivative probably of phaino (as showing outside the other garments); a mantle (surtout).
G5342: to carry, bear, bring; to conduct, lead; perhaps: to make publicly known.
for which other, and apparently not cognate ones are used in certain tenses only; namely, oio (oy'-o); and enegko (en-eng'-ko) to "bear" or carry (in a very wide application, literally and…
G5343: Apparently a primary verb; to run away (literally or figuratively); by implication, to shun; by analogy, to vanish.
G5344: Felix, third name of (Marcus) Antonius Felix, procurator of the Roman province Judea from an uncertain date (before A.D. 52 ?) till A.D. 59.
Of Latin origin; happy; Phelix (i.e. Felix), a Roman.
G5345: From phemi; a saying, i.e. Rumor ("fame").
G5346: Properly, the same as the base of phos and phaino; to show or make known one's thoughts, i.e. Speak or say.
G5347: Of Latin derivation; festal; Phestus (i.e. Festus), a Roman.
G5348: (a) to anticipate, precede, (b) to come, arrive.
Apparently a primary verb; to be beforehand, i.e. Anticipate or precede; by extension, to have arrived at.
G5349: From phtheiro; decayed, i.e. (by implication) perishable.
G535: From a derivative of aparti; completion.
G5350: Probably akin to pheggos and thus to phemi; to utter a clear sound, i.e. (generally) to proclaim.
G5351: Probably strengthened from phthio (to pine or waste); properly, to shrivel or wither, i.e. To spoil (by any process) or (generally) to ruin (especially figuratively, by moral influences, to deprave).
G5352: autumnal, in autumn, when fruit is expected.
From derivative of phthino (to wane; akin to the base of phtheiro) and opora (meaning late autumn); autumnal (as stripped of leaves).
G5353: From phtheggomai; utterance, i.e. A musical note (vocal or instrumental).
G5354: From phthonos; to be jealous of.
G5355: Probably akin to the base of phtheiro; ill-will (as detraction), i.e. Jealousy (spite).
G5356: From phtheiro; decay, i.e. Ruin (spontaneous or inflicted, literally or figuratively).
G5357: Of uncertain affinity; a broad shallow cup ("phial").
G5358: From philos and agathos; fond to good, i.e. A promoter of virtue.
G5359: Philadelphia, a city of the Roman province Asia.
From Philadelphos (the same as philadelphos), a king of Pergamos; Philadelphia, a place in Asia Minor.
G536: the first-fruits, the earliest crop of the year, hence also met., for example, of the earliest converts in a district; there is evidence in favor of rendering in some passages merely by: sacrifice, gift.
From a compound of apo and archomai; a beginning of sacrifice, i.e. The (Jewish) first-fruit (figuratively).
G5360: brotherly love, love of Christian brethren.
brotherly love (kindness), love of the brethren.
G5361: loving like a brother, loving one's brethren.
From philos and adephos; fond of brethren, i.e. Fraternal.
G5362: loving men, (of a wife) loving her husband.
From philos and aner; fond of man, i.e. Affectionate as a wife.
G5363: From the same as philanthropos; fondness of mankind, i.e. Benevolence ("philanthropy").
G5364: Adverb from a compound of philos and anthropos; fondly to man ("philanthropically"), i.e. Humanely.
G5366: From philos and arguros; fond of silver (money), i.e. Avaricious.
G5367: From philos and autos; fond of self, i.e. Selfish.
G5368: to love (of friendship), regard with affection, cherish; to kiss.

From philos; to be a friend to (fond of (an individual or an object)), i.e. Have affection for (denoting personal attachment, as a matter of sentiment or feeling; while agapao is wider, embracing especially the judgment and the deliberate assent of the will…
G5369: From philos and hedone; fond of pleasure, i.e. Voluptuous.
G537: From a (as a particle of union) and pas; absolutely all or (singular) every one.
G5371: Philemon, a Christian man of Colossae.
From phileo; friendly; Philemon, a Christian.
G5372: "worthy of love", Philetus, an erring Christian at Ephesus.
From phileo; amiable; Philetus, an opposer of Christianity.
G5374: a Philippian, an inhabitant of Philippi.
From Philippoi; a Philippesian (Philippian), i.e. Native of Philippi.
G5375: Philippi, a great city of the Roman province Macedonia.
Plural of Philippos; Philippi, a place in Macedonia.
G5376: Philip, (a) one of the twelve apostles of Jesus, (b) tetrarch of the Ituraean and Trachonitic region, half-brother of Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee, (c) one of the seven original deacons at Jerusalem and a…
From philos and hippos; fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites.
G5377: From philos and theos; fond of God, i.e. Pious.
G5378: From philos and logos; fond of words, i.e. Talkative (argumentative, learned, "philological"); Philologus, a Christian.
G5379: From philoneikos; quarrelsomeness, i.e. A dispute.
G538: to deceive, cheat, lead into error.
Of uncertain derivation; to cheat, i.e. Delude.
G5380: From philos and neikos (a quarrel; probably akin to nikos); fond of strife, i.e. Disputatious.
G5382: From philos and xenos; fond of guests, i.e. Hospitable.
G5383: to love the chief place, desire preeminence.
From a compound of philos and protos; to be fond of being first, i.e. Ambitious of distinction.
G5384: friendly; subst: a friend, an associate.
Properly, dear, i.e. A friend; actively, fond, i.e. Friendly (still as a noun, an associate, neighbor, etc.).
G5385: love of wisdom, philosophy, in the NT of traditional Jewish theology.
G5386: From philos and sophos; fond of wise things, i.e. A "philosopher".
G5387: From philos and storge (cherishing one's kindred, especially parents or children); fond of natural relatives, i.e. Fraternal towards fellow Christian.
G5388: From philos and teknon; fond of one's children, i.e. Maternal.
G5389: to be zealous, strive eagerly, desire very strongly.
Middle voice from a compound of philos and time; to be fond of honor, i.e. Emulous (eager or earnest to do something).
G5390: Adverb from philophron; with friendliness of mind, i.e. Kindly.
G5391: From philos and phren; friendly of mind, i.e. Kind.
G5392: to muzzle, to put to silence.
G5393: Active participle of the base of phlox; blazing; Phlegon, a Christian.
G5394: to inflame, fire with passion, set on fire, burn up.
From phlox (g5395); to cause a blaze, i.e. Ignite (figuratively, to inflame with passion).
G5395: From a primary phlego (to "flash" or "flame"); a blaze.
G5396: to gossip against, talk idly, make empty charges against, talk nonsense.
From phluaros; to be a babbler or trifler, i.e. (by implication) to berate idly or mischievously.
G5397: From phluo (to bubble); a garrulous person, i.e. Prater.
G5399: to fear, dread, reverence, be afraid, terrified.
From phobos; to frighten, i.e. (passively) to be alarmed; by analogy, to be in awe of, i.e. Revere.
G54: From hagnos; cleanness (the state), i.e. (figuratively) blamelessness.
G540: From a (as a negative particle) and pater; fatherless, i.e. Of unrecorded paternity.
G5400: a terrible sight, cause of terror, an object of fear.
Neuter of a derivative of phobeo; a frightening thing, i.e. Terrific portent.
G5401: (a) fear, terror, alarm, (b) the object or cause of fear, (c) reverence, respect.
From a primary phebomai (to be put in fear); alarm or fright.
G5402: Phoebe, a Christian woman in the church at Cenchreae.
Feminine of phoibos (bright; probably akin to the base of phos); Phoebe, a Christian woman.
G5403: Phoenicia, a northern coast strip of the Roman province Syria.
From phoinix; palm-country; Phoenice (or Phoenicia), a region of Palestine.
G5405: a Phoenician (an inhabitant of Phoenicia), Phoenix (a city of Crete).
Probably the same as phoinix; Phoenix, a place in Crete.
G5406: From phonos; a murderer (always of criminal (or at least intentional) homicide; which anthropoktonos does not necessarily imply; while sikarios is a special term for a public bandit).
G5407: From phoneus; to be a murderer (of).
G5408: From an obsolete primary pheno (to slay); murder.
G5409: From phoros; to have a burden, i.e. (by analogy) to wear as clothing or a constant accompaniment.
G541: a light flashing forth (from), radiation, gleam.
From a compound of apo and augazo; an off-flash, i.e. Effulgence.
G5410: Of Latin origin; a forum or market-place; only in comparative with Appios; a station on the Appian road.
G5411: a tax, tribute, especially on persons.
From phero; a load (as borne), i.e. (figuratively) a tax (properly, an individual assessment on persons or property; whereas telos is usually a general toll on goods or travel).
G5412: to load, burden; pass: to be laden.
From phortos; to load up (properly, as a vessel or animal), i.e. (figuratively) to overburden with ceremony (or spiritual anxiety).
G5413: a burden; the freight of a ship.
Diminutive of phortos; an invoice (as part of freight), i.e. (figuratively) a task or service.
G5414: From phero; something carried, i.e. The cargo of a ship.
G5415: Of Latin origin; "fortunate"; Fortunatus, a Christian.
G5416: Neuter of a derivative from the base of phragelloo; a whip, i.e. Roman lash as a public punishment.
G5417: From a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum; to whip, i.e. Lash as a public punishment.
G5418: From phrasso; a fence, or inclosing barrier (literally or figuratively).
G5419: Probably akin to phrasso through the idea of defining; to indicate (by word or act), i.e. (specially), to expound.
G542: From apo and the same as eido; to see fully.
G5420: Apparently a strengthening form of the base of phren; to fence or inclose, i.e. (specially), to block up (figuratively, to silence).
G5421: Of uncertain derivation; a hole in the ground (dug for obtaining or holding water or other purposes), i.e. A cistern or well; figuratively, an abyss (as a prison).
G5422: to deceive the mind, impose upon.
From phrenapates; to be a mind-misleader, i.e. Delude.
G5423: From phren and apate; a mind-misleader, i.e. Seducer.
G5424: Probably from an obsolete phrao (to rein in or curb; compare phrasso); the midrif (as a partition of the body), i.e. (figuratively and by implication, of sympathy) the feelings (or sensitive nature; by extension (also in the plural) the mind or cognitive…
G5425: to be rough, to shiver, shudder.
Apparently a primary verb; to "bristle" or chill, i.e. Shudder (fear).
G5426: (a) to think, (b) to think, judge, (c) to direct the mind to, seek for, (d) to observe, (e) to care for.

From phren; to exercise the mind, i.e. Entertain or have a sentiment or opinion; by implication, to be (mentally) disposed (more or less earnestly in a certain direction); intensively, to interest oneself in (with concern or obedience).
set the affection on, (be) care(-ful), (be like-, + be of one, + be of the same, + let this) mind(-ed), regard, savour, think.
G5427: the thought (that which is in the mind).
G5428: understanding (which leads to right action), practical wisdom, prudence.
From phroneo; mental action or activity, i.e. Intellectual or moral insight.
G5429: From phren; thoughtful, i.e. Sagacious or discreet (implying a cautious character; while sophos denotes practical skill or acumen; and sunetos indicates rather intelligence or mental acquirement); in a bad sense conceited (also in the comparative).
G5431: to be thoughtful, careful, give heed.
From a derivative of phren; to exercise thought, i.e. Be anxious.
G5432: to guard, keep, as by a military guard.
From a compound of pro and horao; to be a watcher in advance, i.e. To mount guard as a sentinel (post spies at gates); figuratively, to hem in, protect.
G5433: to be wanton, insolent; to roar, rage.
Akin to bruo, brucho; to snort (as a spirited horse), i.e. (figuratively) to make a tumult.
G5434: Neuter of a presumed derivative of phrugo (to roast or parch; akin to the base of phlox); something desiccated, i.e. A dry twig.
G5435: Phrygia, an ethnic district in Asia Minor, the north-western part of which was in the Roman province Asia and the south-eastern part in the Roman province Galatia.
Probably of foreign origin; Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor.
G5436: Phygelus, a Christian of the Roman province Asia who deserted Paul.
Probably from pheugo; fugitive; Phygellus, an apostate Christian.
G5437: From pheugo; a fleeing, i.e. Escape.
G5438: a watching, keeping guard; a guard, prison; imprisonment.
From phulasso; a guarding or (concretely, guard), the act, the person; figuratively, the place, the condition, or (specially), the time (as a division of day or night), literally or figuratively.
G544: to disobey, rebel, be disloyal, refuse conformity.
From apeithes; to disbelieve (wilfully and perversely).
not believe, disobedient, obey not, unbelieving.
G5440: a phylactery, an amulet, a parchment capsule containing little parchment rolls with the Hebrew texts, affixed to the left upper arm or the forehead of men at morning prayer, and regarded as a protection (hence the name)…
Neuter of a derivative of phulasso; a guard-case, i.e. "phylactery" for wearing slips of Scripture texts.
G5441: From phulasso; a watcher or sentry.
G5442: (a) to guard, protect; mid: to be on guard, (b) act. and mid. of customs and regulations: to keep, observe.
Probably from phule through the idea of isolation; to watch, i.e. Be on guard (literally of figuratively); by implication, to preserve, obey, avoid.
beward, keep (self), observe, save. Compare tereo.
G5443: a tribe or race of people.
From phuo (compare phullon); an offshoot, i.e. Race or clan.
G5444: From the same as phule; a sprout, i.e. Leaf.
G5445: a mass or lump, as of bread dough.
From a prolonged form of phuro (to mix a liquid with a solid; perhaps akin to phuo through the idea of swelling in bulk), mean to knead; a mass of dough.
G5446: natural, (a) according to nature, (b) merely animal.
G5447: Adverb from phusikos; "physically", i.e. (by implication) instinctively.
G5448: to inflate, puff up; pass: to be puffed up, arrogant, proud.
From phusis in the primary sense of blowing; to inflate, i.e. (figuratively) make proud (haughty).
G5449: From phuo; growth (by germination or expansion), i.e. (by implication) natural production (lineal descent); by extension, a genus or sort; figuratively, native disposition, constitution or usage.
G545: unbelieving, disobedient, who will not be persuaded.
From a (as a negative particle) and peitho; unpersuadable, i.e. Contumacious.
G5451: a plant, that which is planted.
From phuteuo; trans-planting, i.e. (concretely) a shrub or vegetable.
G5452: From a derivative of phuo; to set out in the earth, i.e. Implant; figuratively, to instil doctrine.
G5453: to grow, grow up, spring up.
A primary verb; probably originally, to "puff" or blow, i.e. To swell up; but only used in the implied sense, to germinate or grow (sprout, produce), literally or figuratively.
G5454: Of uncertain derivative; a burrow or lurking-place.
G5455: to give forth a sound, hence: (a) of a cock: to crow, (b) of men: to shout, (c) trans: to call (to myself), summon; to invite, address.
From phone; to emit a sound (animal, human or instrumental); by implication, to address in words or by name, also in imitation.
G5456: a sound, noise, voice, language, dialect.
Probably akin to phaino through the idea of disclosure; a tone (articulate, bestial or artificial); by implication, an address (for any purpose), saying or language.
G5457: light, a source of light, radiance.

From an obsolete phao (to shine or make manifest, especially by rays; compare phaino, phemi); luminousness (in the widest application, natural or artificial, abstract or concrete, literal or figurative).
G5458: a light, an illuminator, perhaps the sun; a star; brilliancy.
From phos; an illuminator, i.e. (concretely) a luminary, or (abstractly) brilliancy.
G5459: From phos and phero; light-bearing ("phosphorus"), i.e. (specially), the morning-star (figuratively).
G546: Of uncertain derivation; to menace; by implication, to forbid.
G5460: From phos; lustrous, i.e. Transparent or well-illuminated (figuratively).
G5461: (a) to light up, illumine, (b) to bring to light, make evident, reveal.
From phos; to shed rays, i.e. To shine or (transitively) to brighten up (literally or figuratively).
enlighten, illuminate, (bring to, give) light, make to see.
G5463: to rejoice, be glad; also a salutation: Hail.
A primary verb; to be "cheer"ful, i.e. Calmly happy or well-off; impersonally, especially as salutation (on meeting or parting), be well.
farewell, be glad, God speed, greeting, hall, joy(- fully), rejoice.
G5465: to let down, lower, slacken, loosen.
From the base of chasma; to lower (as into a void).
G5466: a Chaldean, an inhabitant of Chaldea.
Probably of Hebrew or (Kasdiy); a Chaldoean (i.e. Kasdi), or native or the region of the lower Euphrates.
G5467: Perhaps from chalao through the idea of reducing the strength; difficult, i.e. Dangerous, or (by implication) furious.
G5468: From a compound of chalinos and the reduplicated form of ago; to be a bit-leader, i.e. To curb (figuratively).
G5469: From chalao; a curb or head-stall (as curbing the spirit).
G5471: a worker in brass or copper; a smith.
From chalkos; a copper-worker or brazier.
G5472: chalcedony, a small stone of various colors.
From chalkos and perhaps eidos; copper-like, i.e. "chalcedony".
G5473: a brazen (i.e. of copper, bronze, brass) vessel.
Diminutive from chalkos; a copper dish.
G5474: orichalcum, a fine metal, or frankincense of a yellow color.
Neuter of a compound of chalkos and libanos (in the implied mean of whiteness or brilliancy); burnished copper, an alloy of copper (or gold) and silver having a brilliant lustre.
G5475: copper, brass, money; a brazen musical instrument.
Perhaps from chalao through the idea of hollowing out as a vessel (this metal being chiefly used for that purpose); copper (the substance, or some implement or coin made of it).
G5476: Adverb perhaps from the base of chasma through the idea of a fissure in the soil; earthward, i.e. Prostrate.
G5477: Canaan, the whole of Palestine or Palestine west of the river Jordan.
Of Hebrew origin (Kna'an); Chanaan (i.e. Kenaan), the early name of Palestine.
G5478: Canaanite, a Biblical and archaic name for Phoenician.
From Chanaan; a Chanaanoean (i.e. Kenaanite), or native of gentile Palestine.
G5479: joy, gladness, a source of joy.
From chairo; cheerfulness, i.e. Calm delight.
gladness, X greatly, (X be exceeding) joy(-ful, -fully, -fulness, -ous).
G548: to be away, to be absent.
From apo and eimi; to be away.
G5480: From the same as charax; a scratch or etching, i.e. Stamp (as a badge of servitude), or scupltured figure (statue).
G5481: an impression, representation, exact reproduction; a graving-tool.
From the same as charax; a graver (the tool or the person), i.e. (by implication) engraving (("character"), the figure stamped, i.e. An exact copy or (figuratively) representation).
G5482: From charasso (to sharpen to a point; akin to grapho through the idea of scratching); a stake, i.e. (by implication) a palisade or rampart (military mound for circumvallation in a siege).
G5483: (a) to show favor to, (b) to pardon, forgive, (c) to show kindness.
Middle voice from charis; to grant as a favor, i.e. Gratuitously, in kindness, pardon or rescue.
G5484: for the sake of, by reason of, on account of.
Accusative case of charis as preposition; through favor of, i.e. On account of.
be-(for) cause of, for sake of, +...fore, X reproachfully.
G5485: (a) grace, as a gift or blessing brought to man by Jesus Christ, (b) favor, (c) gratitude, thanks, (d) a favor, kindness.

From chairo; graciousness (as gratifying), of manner or act (abstract or concrete; literal, figurative or spiritual; especially the divine influence upon the heart, and its reflection in the life; including gratitude).
acceptable, benefit, favour, gift, grace(- ious), joy, liberality, pleasure, thank(-s, -worthy).
G5486: a gift of grace, an undeserved favor.

From charizomai; a (divine) gratuity, i.e. Deliverance (from danger or passion); (specially), a (spiritual) endowment, i.e. (subjectively) religious qualification, or (objectively) miraculous faculty.
G5487: to make graceful, endow with grace.
From charis; to grace, i.e. Indue with special honor.
G5488: Haran, a city in northwest Mesopotamia.
Of Hebrew origin (Charan); Charrhan (i.e. Charan), a place in Mesopotamia.
G5489: a sheet of paper (made of papyrus strips).
From the same as charax; a sheet ("chart") of writing-material (as to be scribbled over).
G549: From apo and eimi (to go); to go away.
G5490: From a form of an obsolete primary chao (to "gape" or "yawn"); a "chasm" or vacancy (impassable interval).
G5491: a lip, mouth, shore, edge, brink; meton: language, dialect.
From a form of the same as chasma; a lip (as a pouring place); figuratively, a margin (of water).
G5492: to expose to winter cold, to drive with storm.
From the same as cheimon; to storm, i.e. (passively) to labor under a gale.
