G5493: From the base of cheimon and rheo; a storm-runlet, i.e. Winter-torrent.
G5494: a storm, tempest; winter, the rainy season.
From a derivative of cheo (to pour; akin to the base of chasma through the idea of a channel), meaning a storm (as pouring rain); by implication, the rainy season, i.e. Winter.
G5495: Perhaps from the base of cheimon in the sense of its congener the base of chasma (through the idea of hollowness for grasping); the hand (literally or figuratively (power); especially (by Hebraism) a means or instrument).
G5496: From cheiragogos; to be a hand-leader, i.e. To guide (a blind person).
G5497: one who leads a helpless person by the hand.
From cheir and a reduplicated form of ago; a hand-leader, i.e. Personal conductor (of a blind person).
some to lead by the hand.
G5498: Neuter of a compound of cheir and grapho; something hand-written ("chirograph"), i.e. A manuscript (specially, a legal document or bond (figuratively)).
G5499: done or made with hands, artificial.
From cheir and a derivative of poieo; manufactured, i.e. Of human construction.
G55: purely, sincerely, with pure motives, honestly.
Adverb from hagnos; purely, i.e. Honestly.
G550: Reflexive past of a compound of apo and epo; to say off for oneself, i.e. Disown.
G5500: to elect by show of hands, choose by vote, appoint.
From a comparative of cheir and teino (to stretch); to be a hand-reacher or voter (by raising the hand), i.e. (generally) to select or appoint.
G5501: Irregular comparative of kakos; from an obsolete equivalent cheres (of uncertain derivation); more evil or aggravated (physically, mentally or morally).
G5502: Cherubim, heavenly beings who serve God.
Plural of Hebrew origin (kruwb); "cherubim" (i.e. Cherubs or kerubim).
G5503: Feminine of a presumed derivative apparently from the base of chasma through the idea of deficiency; a widow (as lacking a husband), literally or figuratively.
G5504: Of uncertain derivation; "yesterday"; by extension, in time past or hitherto.
G5505: a thousand, the number one thousand.
G5506: a commander of a thousand men, a military tribune.
From chilioi and archo; the commander of a thousand soldiers ("chiliarch"; i.e. Colonel.
G5507: Plural of uncertain affinity; a thousand.
G5508: Chios (modern Scio), an important island in the Aegean Sea, off the west central coast of Asia Minor.
Of uncertain derivation; Chios, an island in the Mediterranean.
G5509: Of foreign origin (kthoneth); a tunic or shirt.
G551: untried, inexperienced, untempted, incapable of being tempted.
From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of peirao; untried, i.e. Not temptable.
G5510: Perhaps akin to the base of chasma (chalao) or cheimon (as descending or empty); snow.
G5511: a short cloak, worn by military officers and soldiers.
Of uncertain derivation; a military cloak.
G5512: From a derivative probably of cheilos; to throw out the lip, i.e. Jeer at.
G5514: Chloe, probably with business connections either in Corinth or in Ephesus or in both.
Feminine of apparently a primary word; "green"; Chloe, a Christian female.
G5515: From the same as Chloe; greenish, i.e. Verdant, dun-colored.
G5516: The 22nd, 14th and an obsolete letter (stigma as a cross) of the Greek alphabet (intermediate between the 5th and 6th), used as numbers; denoting respectively 600, 60, and 6; 666 as a numeral.
G5517: From choos; dusty or dirty (soil-like), i.e. (by implication) terrene.
G5518: a choenix (a dry measure of less than a quart).
Of uncertain derivation; a choenix or certain dry measure.
G552: From a (as a negative particle) and peira; inexperienced, i.e. Ignorant.
G5520: From chole; to be bilious, i.e. (by implication) irritable (enraged, "choleric").
G5521: Feminine of an equivalent perhaps akin to the same as Chloe (from the greenish hue); "gall" or bile, i.e. (by analogy) poison or an anodyne (wormwood, poppy, etc.).
G5522: From the base of cheimon; a heap (as poured out), i.e. Rubbish; loose dirt.
G5523: Of uncertain derivation; Chorazin, a place in Palestine.
G5524: to lead a chorus (i.e. a group of performers), to defray the cost of a chorus.
From a compound of choros and ago; to be a dance-leader, i.e. (generally) to furnish.
G5525: Of uncertain derivation; a ring, i.e. Round dance ("choir".
G5526: From chortos; to fodder, i.e. (generally) to gorge (supply food in abundance).
G5528: Apparently a primary word; a "court" or "garden", i.e. (by implication, of pasture) herbage or vegetation.
G5529: Chuza, a steward of Herod Antipas.
Of uncertain origin; Chuzas, an officer of Herod.
G553: to expect eagerly, wait for eagerly, look for.
From apo and ekdechomai; to expect fully.
G5530: to use, make use of, deal with, take advantage of.

Middle voice of a primary verb (perhaps rather from cheir, to handle); to furnish what is needed; (give an oracle, "graze" (touch slightly), light upon, etc.), i.e. (by implication) to employ or (by extension) to act towards one in a given manner.
G5531: Probably the same as the base of chraomai; to loan.
G5532: From the base of chraomai or chre; employment, i.e. An affair; also (by implication) occasion, demand, requirement or destitution.
business, lack, necessary(-ity), need(-ful), use, want.
G5533: From a derivative of chrao and opheiletes; a loan-ower, i.e. Indebted person.
G5534: Third person singular of the same as chraomai or chrao used impersonally; it needs (must or should) be.
G5535: to need, have need of, want, desire.
From chreia; to make (i.e. Have) necessity, i.e. Be in want of.
G5536: a thing that one uses or needs.
Something useful or needed, i.e. Wealth, price.
G5537: (originally: to transact business), (a) act. of God: to warn; pass: to be warned by God (probably in response to an inquiry as to one's duty), (b) (to take a name from public business, hence) to receive a name, be…

From chrema; to utter an oracle (compare the original sense of chraomai), i.e. Divinely intimate; by implication, (compare the secular sense of chreia) to constitute a firm for business, i.e. (generally) bear as a title.
be called, be admonished (warned) of God, reveal, speak.
G5538: From chrematizo; a divine response or revelation.
G554: Middle voice from apo and ekduo; to divest wholly oneself, or (for oneself) despoil.
G5540: From chraomai; employment, i.e. (specially), sexual intercourse (as an occupation of the body).
G5541: to be kind (full of service to others), gentle.
Middle voice from chrestos; to show oneself useful, i.e. Act benevolently.
G5542: a kind address; in a bad sense: plausible speaking.
From a compound of chrestos and lego; fair speech, i.e. Plausibility.
G5543: From chraomai; employed, i.e. (by implication) useful (in manner or morals).
G5544: From chrestos; usefulness, i.e. Morally, excellence (in character or demeanor).
G5545: From chrio; an unguent or smearing, i.e. (figuratively) the special endowment ("chrism") of the Holy Spirit.
G5546: From Christos; a Christian, i.e. Follower of Christ.
G5547: Anointed One; the Messiah, the Christ.
From chrio; Anointed One, i.e. The Messiah, an epithet of Jesus.
G5548: Probably akin to chraomai through the idea of contact; to smear or rub with oil, i.e. (by implication) to consecrate to an office or religious service.
G5549: to delay, tarry, linger, spend time.
From chronos; to take time, i.e. Linger.
G555: a putting off (as of a garment), a casting off.
G5550: Of uncertain derivation; a space of time (in general, and thus properly distinguished from kairos, which designates a fixed or special occasion; and from aion, which denotes a particular period) or interval; by extension, an individual opportunity; by…
+ years old, season, space, (X often-)time(-s), (a) while.
G5551: to waste time, spend time, delay.
From a presumed compound of chronos and the base of tribos; to be a time-wearer, i.e. To procrastinate (linger).
G5552: golden, made of gold, adorned with gold.
G5553: a piece of gold, golden ornament.
Diminutive of chrusos; a golden article, i.e. Gold plating, ornament, or coin.
G5554: From chrusos and daktulios; gold-ringed, i.e. Wearing a golden finger-ring or similar jewelry.
G5555: a topaz, a gem with a bright yellow color.
From chrusos and lithos; gold-stone, i.e. A yellow gem ("chrysolite").
G5556: a chrysoprase, gem of a golden-greenish color.
From chrusos and prason (a leek); a greenish-yellow gem ("chrysoprase").
G5557: gold, anything made of gold, a gold coin.
Perhaps from the base of chraomai (through the idea of the utility of the metal); gold; by extension, a golden article, as an ornament or coin.
G5558: to gild, to cover with gold.
From chrusos; to gild, i.e. Bespangle with golden ornaments.
G5559: the surface of the body, skin.
Probably akin to the base of chraomai through the idea of handling; the body (properly, its surface or skin).
G556: From apo and elauno; to dismiss.
G5560: lame, deprived of a foot, limping.
Apparently a primary word; "halt", i.e. Limping.
G5561: (a) a country or region, (b) the land, as opposed to the sea, (c) the country, distinct from town, (d) plur: fields.
Feminine of a derivative of the base of chasma through the idea of empty expanse; room, i.e. A space of territory (more or less extensive; often including its inhabitants).
coast, county, fields, ground, land, region. Compare topos.
G5562: (lit: to make room, hence) (a) to have room for, receive, contain, (b) to make room for by departing, go, make progress, turn myself.
From chora; to be in (give) space, i.e. (intransitively) to pass, enter, or (transitively) to hold, admit (literally or figuratively).
come, contain, go, have place, (can, be room to) receive.
G5563: (a) to separate, put apart, (b) mid. or pass: to separate myself, depart, withdraw.
From chora; to place room between, i.e. Part; reflexively, to go away.
G5564: a place, piece of land, field, property, estate.
Diminutive of chora; a spot or plot of ground.
field, land, parcel of ground, place, possession.
G5565: Adverb from chora; at a space, i.e. Separately or apart from (often as preposition).
G5566: the north-west wind, and the quarter of the sky from which it comes.
Of Latin origin; the north-west wind.
G5567: to sing, sing psalms; earlier: to play on a stringed instrument.

Probably strengthened from psao (to rub or touch the surface; compare psocho); to twitch or twang, i.e. To play on a stringed instrument (celebrate the divine worship with music and accompanying odes).
G5568: a psalm, song of praise, the Hebrew book of Psalms.
From psallo; a set piece of music, i.e. A sacred ode (accompanied with the voice, harp or other instrument; a "psalm"); collectively, the book of the Psalms.
G5569: From pseudes and adephos; a spurious brother, i.e. Pretended associate.
G557: From a compound of apo and elegcho; refutation, i.e. (by implication) contempt.
G5570: From pseudes and apostolos; a spurious apostle, i.e. Pretended pracher.
G5571: From pseudomai; untrue, i.e. Erroneous, deceitful, wicked.
G5572: a false teacher, teacher of false things.
From pseudes and didaskalos; a spurious teacher, i.e. Propagator of erroneous Christian doctrine.
G5573: From pseudes and lego; mendacious, i.e. Promulgating erroneous Christian doctrine.
G5574: Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to utter an untruth or attempt to deceive by falsehood.
G5575: From pseudes and a kindred form of martus; a spurious witness, i.e. Bearer of untrue testimony.
G5576: to bear false witness, give false testimony.
From pseudomartur; to be an untrue testifier, i.e. Offer falsehood in evidence.
G5578: a false prophet; one who in God's name teaches what is false.
From pseudes and prophetes; a spurious prophet, i.e. Pretended foreteller or religious impostor.
G5579: a lie, falsehood, untruth; false religion.
G558: a freedman, one who has been a slave but has been manumitted by his master.
From apo and eleutheros; one freed away, i.e. A freedman.
G5580: From pseudes and Christos; a spurious Messiah.
G5581: under a false name, falsely called.
From pseudes and onoma; untruly named.
G5582: From pseudomai; a fabrication, i.e. Falsehood.
G5584: to feel, touch, handle; to feel after, grope for.
From the base of psallo (compare psephos); to manipulate, i.e. Verify by contact; figuratively, to search for.
G5585: From psephos; to use pebbles in enumeration, i.e. (generally) to compute.
G5586: (a) a pebble, small stone, (b) hence, from their use in voting: a vote.
From the same as pselaphao; a pebble (as worn smooth by handling), i.e. (by implication, of use as a counter or ballot) a verdict (of acquittal) or ticket (of admission); a vote.
G5587: From a derivative of psithos (a whisper; by implication, a slander; probably akin to pseudomai); whispering, i.e. Secret detraction.
G5588: From the same as psithurismos; a secret calumniator.
G5589: Diminutive from a derivative of the base of psallo (meaning a crumb); a little bit or morsel.
G559: Of Latin origin; Apelles, a Christian.
G5590: (a) the vital breath, breath of life, (b) the human soul, (c) the soul as the seat of affections and will, (d) the self, (e) a human person, an individual.

From psucho; breath, i.e. (by implication) spirit, abstractly or concretely (the animal sentient principle only; thus distinguished on the one hand from pneuma, which is the rational and immortal soul; and on the other from zoe, which is mere vitality, even…
heart (+ -ily), life, mind, soul, + us, + you.
G5591: natural, of the soul or mind.
From psuche; sensitive, i.e. Animate (in distinction on the one hand from pneumatikos, which is the higher or renovated nature; and on the other from phusikos, which is the lower or bestial nature).
G5594: to breathe, blow, to make cool.

A primary verb; to breathe (voluntarily but gently, thus differing on the one hand from pneo, which denotes properly a forcible respiration; and on the other from the base of aer, which refers properly to an inanimate breeze), i.e. (by implication, of…
G5595: From the base of psomion; to supply with bits, i.e. (generally) to nourish.
G5596: Diminutive from a derivative of the base of psocho; a crumb or morsel (as if rubbed off), i.e. A mouthful.
G5597: Prolongation from the same base as psallo; to triturate, i.e. (by analogy) to rub out (kernels from husks with the fingers or hand).
G5598: omega, the last letter of the Greek alphabet.
The last letter of the Greek alphabet, i.e. (figuratively) the finality.
G5599: O, an exclamation, used in addressing someone.
A primary interjection; as a sign of the vocative case, O; as a note of exclamation, oh.
G56: From a (as negative particle) and gnosis; ignorance (properly, the state).
G560: to give up in despair, despair of; to hope to receive from or in return.
From apo and elpizo; to hope out, i.e. Fully expect.
G5600: Including the oblique forms, as well as es (ace); e (ay); etc. The subjunctive of eimi; (may, might, can, could, would, should, must, etc.; also with ei and its comparative, as well as with other particles) be.
+ appear, are, (may, might, should) be, X have, is, + pass the flower of her age, should stand, were.
G5601: Of Hebrew origin (Owbed); Obed, an Israelite.
G5602: here, the things here, what is here, what is going on here, the state of affairs here.
From an adverb form of hode; in this same spot, i.e. Here or hither.
G5603: From aido; a chant or "ode" (the general term for any words sung; while humnos denotes especially a religious metrical composition, and psalmos still more specially, a Hebrew cantillation).
G5604: the pain of childbirth, acute pain, severe agony, a snare.
Akin to odune; a pang or throe, especially of childbirth.
G5605: to be in travail, suffer birth-pangs.
From odin; to experience the pains of parturition (literally or figuratively).
G5606: Perhaps from the alternate of phero; the shoulder (as that on which burdens are borne).
G5607: Including the feminine ousa (oo'-sah); and the neuter on (on) present participle of eimi; being.
G5608: Middle voice from an apparently primary onos (a sum or price); to purchase (synonymous with the earlier pimpremi).
G561: against, over against, opposite, in view of, in the presence of.
From apo and enanti; from in front, i.e. Opposite, before or against.
before, contrary, over against, in the presence of.
G5610: (a) a definite space of time, a season, (b) an hour, (c) the particular time for anything.
Apparently a primary word; an "hour" (literally or figuratively).
day, hour, instant, season, X short, (even-)tide, (high) time.
G5611: From hora; belonging to the right hour or season (timely), i.e. (by implication) flourishing (beauteous (figuratively)).
G5612: to roar, howl, as a beast.
Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to "roar".
G5613: as, like as, about, as it were, according as, how, when, while, as soon as, so that.
Probably adverb of comparative from hos; which how, i.e. In that manner (very variously used, as follows).
about, after (that), (according) as (it had been, it were), as soon (as), even as (like), for, how (greatly), like (as, unto), since, so (that), that, to wit, unto, when(-soever), while, X with all…
G5614: (Aramaic and Hebrew, originally a cry for help), hosanna!, a cry of happiness.
Of Hebrew origin (yasha' and na'); oh save!; hosanna (i.e. Hoshia-na), an exclamation of adoration.
G5615: in like manner, likewise, just so.
From hos and an adverb from autos; as thus, i.e. In the same way.
even so, likewise, after the same (in like) manner.
G5616: as if, as it were, like; with numbers: about.
From hos and ei; as if.
about, as (it had been, it were), like (as).
G5617: Of Hebrew origin (Howshea'); Hosee (i.e. Hoshea), an Israelite.
G5618: From hos and per; just as, i.e. Exactly like.
G5619: just as if, as it were.
From hosper and ei; just as if, i.e. As it were.
G562: From a (as a negative particle) and a secondary derivative of peran; unfinished, i.e. (by implication) interminable.
G5620: so that, therefore, so then, so as to.
From hos and te; so too, i.e. Thus therefore (in various relations of consecution, as follow).
(insomuch) as, so that (then), (insomuch) that, therefore, to, wherefore.
G5621: Diminutive of ous; an earlet, i.e. One of the ears, or perhaps the lobe of the ear.
G5622: From a derivative of the base of ophelimos; usefulness, i.e. Benefit.
G5623: to help, benefit, do good, be useful (to), profit.
From the same as opheleia; to be useful, i.e. To benefit.
G5624: From a form of ophelos; helpful or serviceable, i.e. Advantageous.
G563: Adverb from a compound of a (as a negative participle) and a presumed derivative of perispao; undistractedly, i.e. Free from (domestic) solicitude.
G564: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of peritemno; uncircumcised (figuratively).
G565: to come or go away from, depart, return, arrive, go after, follow.
From apo and erchomai; to go off (i.e. Depart), aside (i.e. Apart) or behind (i.e. Follow), literally or figuratively.
come, depart, go (aside, away, back, out,... Ways), pass away, be past.
G566: Third person singular present indicative active of apecho used impersonally; it is sufficient.
G567: to abstain from, keep myself away from.
Middle voice (reflexively) of apecho; to hold oneself off, i.e. Refrain.
G568: to hold back, keep off, to be away, be distant.
From apo and echo; (actively) to have out, i.e. Receive in full; (intransitively) to keep (oneself) away, i.e. Be distant (literally or figuratively).
G569: to be unfaithful, disbelieve, refuse belief, prove false.
From apistos; to be unbelieving, i.e. (transitively) disbelieve, or (by implication) disobey.
G57: From a (as negative particle) and gnostos; unknown.
G570: From apistos; faithlessness, i.e. (negatively) disbelief (lack of Christian faith), or (positively) unfaithfulness (disobedience).
G571: unbelieving, incredulous, unchristian; sometimes subst: unbeliever.
From a (as a negative particle) and pistos; (actively) disbelieving, i.e. Without Christian faith (specially, a heathen); (passively) untrustworthy (person), or incredible (thing).
that believeth not, faithless, incredible thing, infidel, unbeliever(-ing).
G572: From haplous; singleness, i.e. (subjectively) sincerity (without dissimulation or self-seeking), or (objectively) generosity (copious bestowal).
G573: Probably from a (as a particle of union) and the base of pleko; properly, folded together, i.e. Single (figuratively, clear).
G574: Adverb from haplous (in the objective sense of haplotes); bountifully.
G575: A primary particle; "off," i.e. Away (from something near), in various senses (of place, time, or relation; literal or figurative).
(X here-)after, ago, at, because of, before, by (the space of), for(-th), from, in, (out) of, off, (up-)on(-ce), since, with. In composition (as a prefix) it usually denotes separation, departure,…
G576: to go or come out of, disembark, turn out, result, become, happen.
From apo and the base of basis; literally, to disembark; figuratively, to eventuate.
G577: to throw away from, throw overboard, cast aside.
From apo and ballo; to throw off; figuratively, to lose.
G578: to look away from all else at one object, look steadfastly.
From apo and blepo; to look away from everything else, i.e. (figuratively) intently regard.
G579: worthy to be cast away, worthless, regarded as vile.
From apoballo; cast off, i.e. (figuratively) such as to be rejected.
G58: market-place, forum, public place of assembly.
From ageiro (to gather; probably akin to egeiro); properly, the town-square (as a place of public resort); by implication, a market or thoroughfare.
G580: a casting away, rejection, a loss.
G581: to be away, be removed from, depart life, die.
Past participle of a compound of apo and ginomai; absent, i.e. Deceased (figuratively, renounced).
G582: From apographo; an enrollment; by implication, an assessment.
G583: to enroll, inscribe in a register; mid: to give name for registration (or census-taking).
From apo and grapho; to write off (a copy or list), i.e. Enrol.
G584: to show by proof, demonstrate, set forth, proclaim to an officer.
From apo and deiknuo; to show off, i.e. Exhibit; figuratively, to demonstrate, i.e. Accredit.
G586: to take off (deduct) a tenth part (of property) (and give it away), pay tithe.
From apo and dekatoo; to tithe (as debtor or creditor).
G587: worthy to be received (welcomed), acceptable, welcome, pleasant.
G588: to receive, welcome, entertain (with hospitality), embrace.
From apo and dechomai; to take fully, i.e. Welcome (persons), approve (things).
G589: to be away from home, go into another country, be away, be abroad.
From apodemos; to go abroad, i.e. Visit a foreign land.
go (travel) into a far country, journey.
G59: to buy in the marketplace, purchase.
From agora; properly, to go to market, i.e. (by implication) to purchase; specially, to redeem.
G590: away from home, sojourning in another country.
From apo and demos; absent from one's own people, i.e. A foreign traveller.
G591: (a) to give back, return, restore, (b) to give, render, as due, (c) mid: to sell.
From apo and didomi; to give away, i.e. Up, over, back, etc. (in various applications).
deliver (again), give (again), (re-)pay(-ment be made), perform, recompense, render, requite, restore, reward, sell, yield.
G592: to make a logical distinction, make an invidious distinction.
From apo and a compound of Alexandros and horizo; to disjoin (by a boundary, figuratively, a party).
G593: From apo and dokimazo; to disapprove, i.e. (by implication) to repudiate.
G594: (properly: reception, welcome, of guests), acceptance, appreciation, approbation.
G595: a putting off, a laying down.
From apotithemi; a laying aside (literally or figuratively).
G596: From apotithemi; a repository, i.e. Granary.
G597: From apo and thesaurizo; to treasure away.
G598: (lit: to rub), jostle, press hard, crowd.
From apo and thlibo; to crowd (from every side).
G599: to be dying, be about to die, wither, decay.
From apo and thnesko; to die off (literally or figuratively).
be dead, death, die, lie a-dying, be slain (X with).
G6: Abel, second son of Adam and Eve, brother of Cain.
Of Hebrew origin (Hebel); Abel, the son of Adam.
G60: a lounger in the market-place, perhaps with the idea of agitator.
From agora; relating to the market-place, i.e. Forensic (times); by implication, vulgar.
G600: to set up again, restore to its original position or condition; hence: to restore, give back.
From apo and kathistemi; to reconstitute (in health, home or organization).
G601: to uncover, bring to light, reveal.
From apo and kalupto; to take off the cover, i.e. Disclose.
G602: appearing, coming, lighten, manifestation, be revealed, revelation.
G603: From a comparative of apo and a compound of kara (the head) and dokeo (in the sense of watching); intense anticipation.
G604: to reconcile, change from one state of feeling to another.
From apo and katallasso; to reconcile fully.
G606: to have been put away, be stored, be reserved for.
From apo and keimai; to be reserved; figuratively, to await.
G607: From apo and kephale; to decapitate.
G608: to shut fast, close, shut up.
From apo and kleio; to close fully.
G609: to smite, cut off, cut loose; mid: to emasculate, castrate, mutilate myself.
From apo and kopto; to amputate; reflexively (by irony) to mutilate (the privy parts).
G61: From ago; (abstractly) a catching (of fish); also (concretely) a haul (of fish).
G610: From apokrinomai (in its original sense of judging); a judicial decision.
G611: to answer, reply, take up the conversation.
From apo and krino; to conclude for oneself, i.e. (by implication) to respond; by Hebraism (compare anah) to begin to speak (where an address is expected).
G613: to hide away, conceal, keep secret.
From apo and krupto; to conceal away (i.e. Fully); figuratively, to keep secret.
G614: From apokrupto; secret; by implication, treasured.
G615: to put to death, kill; fig: to abolish.
From apo and kteino (to slay); to kill outright; figuratively, to destroy.
G616: to bring forth, give birth to (a child), a medical or physical word, marking the close of pregnancy.
From apo and the base of kuma; to breed forth, i.e. (by transference) to generate (figuratively).
G617: From apo and kulioo; to roll away.
G618: (a) to get back, receive back, (b) to get (receive) as due (deserved), (c) mid: to draw aside, separate.
From apo and lambano; to receive (specially, in full, or as a host); also to take aside.
G619: the faculty or experience of enjoyment.
From a comparative of apo and lauo (to enjoy); full enjoyment.
G62: unlettered, illiterate, uneducated, perhaps with the narrower idea: unacquainted with Rabbinic teaching.
From a (as negative particle) and gramma; unlettered, i.e. Illiterate.
G620: to leave, leave behind; pass: to be reserved, remain; to desert, abandon.
From apo and leipo; to leave behind (passively, remain); by implication, to forsake.
G621: to lick off, lick clean, lick up.
From apo and leicho (to "lick"); to lick clean.
G622: (a) to kill, destroy, (b) to lose, mid: to be perishing (the resultant death being viewed as certain).
From apo and the base of olethros; to destroy fully (reflexively, to perish, or lose), literally or figuratively.
G623: Apollyon, The Destroying One, a Greek translation of the Hebrew: Abaddon.
Active participle of apollumi; a destroyer (i.e. Satan).
G624: From the pagan deity Apollon (i.e. The sun; from apollumi); Apollonia, a place in Macedonia.
G625: Probably from the same as Apollonia; Apollos, an Israelite.
G626: to give a defense, defend myself (especially in a law court): it can take an object of what is said in defense.
Middle voice from a compound of apo and logos; to give an account (legal plea) of oneself, i.e. Exculpate (self).
answer (for self), make defence, excuse (self), speak for self.
G627: a verbal defense (particularly in a law court).
From the same as apologeomai; a plea ("apology").
answer (for self), clearing of self, defence.
G628: to wash off, mid: to wash away (sins, in baptism).
From apo and louo; to wash fully, i.e. (figuratively) have remitted (reflexively).
G629: release effected by payment of ransom; redemption, deliverance.
From a compound of apo and lutron; (the act) ransom in full, i.e. (figuratively) riddance, or (specially) Christian salvation.
G63: to spend the night in the open, bivouac.
From agros and auleo (in the sense of aule); to camp out.
G630: to release, let go, send away, divorce, be rid; mid: to depart.
From apo and luo; to free fully, i.e. (literally) relieve, release, dismiss (reflexively, depart), or (figuratively) let die, pardon or (specially) divorce.
(let) depart, dismiss, divorce, forgive, let go, loose, put (send) away, release, set at liberty.
G631: to wipe off, wipe clean; mid: to wipe myself off.
Middle voice from apo and masso (to squeeze, knead, smear); to scrape away.
G632: From apo and the base of nomos; to apportion, i.e. Bestow.
G633: From apo and nipto; to wash off (reflexively, one's own hands symbolically).
G634: From apo and pipto; to fall off.
G635: to cause to go astray; pass: to be led astray.
From apo and planao; to lead astray (figuratively); passively, to stray (from truth).
G636: From apo and pleo; to set sail.
G637: From apo and pluno; to rinse off.
G638: (a) to suffocate, choke, drown, (b) to stop the growth of.
From apo and pnigo; to stifle (by drowning or overgrowth).
G639: to be at a loss, be perplexed; mid: to be in doubt.
From a compound of a (as a negative particle) and the base of poreuomai; to have no way out, i.e. Be at a loss (mentally).
G64: From agra; to hunt, i.e. (figuratively) to entrap.
G640: From the same as aporeo; a (state of) quandary.
G641: to throw away from, throw overboard.
From apo and rhipto; to hurl off, i.e. Precipitate (oneself).
G642: to separate from some one, be bereaved.
From apo and a derivative of orphanos; to bereave wholly, i.e. (figuratively) separate (from intercourse).
G643: to prepare for a journey, depart.
From apo and a derivative of skeuos; to pack up (one's) baggage.
G644: either a shadow cast by an object, or a faint image or copy of an object.
From a compound of apo and a derivative of skia; a shading off, i.e. Obscuration.
G645: lit: to wrench away from, drag away, but perhaps sometimes in the well-attested weakened sense: to be parted or withdrawn.
From apo and spao; to drag forth, i.e. (literally) unsheathe (a sword), or relatively (with a degree of force implied) retire (personally or factiously).
G646: Feminine of the same as apostasion; defection from truth (properly, the state) ("apostasy").
G647: repudiation, divorce; met: bill of divorce.
Neuter of a (presumed) adjective from a derivative of aphistemi; properly, something separative, i.e. (specially) divorce.
G648: to unroof, take the roof off.
From apo and a derivative of stege; to unroof.
G649: to send forth, send (as a messenger, commission, etc.), send away, dismiss.
From apo and stello; set apart, i.e. (by implication) to send out (properly, on a mission) literally or figuratively.
put in, send (away, forth, out), set (at liberty).
G65: From agrios and elaia; an oleaster.
G650: to defraud, deprive of, despoil; mid: to endure deprivation; pass: to be bereft of.
From apo and stereo (to deprive); to despoil.
defraud, destitute, kept back by fraud.
G652: a messenger, envoy, delegate, one commissioned by another to represent him in some way, especially a man sent out by Jesus Christ Himself to preach the Gospel; an apostle.
From apostello; a delegate; specially, an ambassador of the Gospel; officially a commissioner of Christ ("apostle") (with miraculous powers).
apostle, messenger, he that is sent.
G653: From apo and a (presumed) derivative of stoma; to speak off-hand (properly, dictate), i.e. To catechize (in an invidious manner).
G654: to turn away, pervert, remove; to restore, replace; mid: to desert, reject.
From apo and strepho; to turn away or back (literally or figuratively).
G655: From apo and the base of stugnetos; to detest utterly.
G656: away from the synagogue, expelled from the synagogue, excommunicated.
G657: to withdraw from, take leave of, renounce, send away.
Middle voice from apo and tasso; literally, to say adieu (by departing or dismissing); figuratively, to renounce.
bid farewell, forsake, take leave, send away.
G658: to complete, accomplish, form fully, perfect, bring to maturity.
From apo and teleo; to complete entirely, i.e. Consummate.
G659: to lay off or aside, renounce, stow away, put.
From apo and tithemi; to put away (literally or figuratively).
cast off, lay apart (aside, down), put away (off).
G66: living in the fields, wild, savage, fierce.
From agros; wild (as pertaining to the country), literally (natural) or figuratively (fierce).
G660: From apo and tinasso (to jostle); to brush off.
G661: to repay, pay what is due (by way of punishment or fine), make good.
From apo and tino; to pay in full.
G662: From apo and tolmao; to venture plainly.
G663: (lit: sheerness, of a rock), abruptness, harshness, severity, rigor.
From the base of apotomos; (figuratively) decisiveness, i.e. Rigor.
G664: Adverb from a derivative of a comparative of apo and temno (to cut); abruptly, i.e. Peremptorily.
G665: From apo and the base of trope; to deflect, i.e. (reflexively) avoid.
G666: From the participle of apeimi; a being away.
G667: to carry, bear away (sometimes with violence).
From apo and phero; to bear off (literally or relatively).
G668: From apo and pheugo; (figuratively) to escape.
G669: From apo and phtheggomai; to enunciate plainly, i.e. Declare.
G67: Agrippa, the name of two descendant of Herod the Great.
Apparently from agrios and hippos; wild-horse tamer; Agrippas, one of the Herods.
G670: From apo and the middle voice of phortizo; to unload.
G671: From a compound of apo and chraomai; the act of using up, i.e. Consumption.
G672: From apo and choreo; to go away.
G673: to separate from; mid: to part; pass: to be swept aside.
From apo and chorizo; to rend apart; reflexively, to separate.
G674: to faint, breathe out life, die, be dismayed.
From apo and psucho; to breathe out, i.e. Faint.
G675: the township Appi Forum on the Appian Way, 43 Roman miles from Rome, was named.
Of Latin origin; (in the genitive, i.e. Possessive case) of Appius, the name of a Roman.
G676: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a comparative of pros and eimi (to go); inaccessible.
G677: (free from hurt or harm, hence) not offending, not causing offence, blameless.
From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of proskopto; actively, inoffensive, i.e. Not leading into sin; passively, faultless, i.e. Not led into sin.
G678: (literary and Jewish), without any preference (undue favor, partiality) for a person.

Adverb from a compound of a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a presumed compound of prosopon and lambano (compare prosopoleptes); in a way not accepting the person, i.e. Impartially.
G679: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of ptaio; not stumbling, i.e. (figuratively) without sin.
G68: a field, especially as bearing a crop; the country, lands, property in land, a country estate.
From ago; a field (as a drive for cattle); genitive case, the country; specially, a farm, i.e. Hamlet.
country, farm, piece of ground, land.
G680: prop: to fasten to; to lay hold of, touch, know carnally.
Reflexive of hapto; properly, to attach oneself to, i.e. To touch (in many implied relations).
G681: to fasten to, lay hold of.
A primary verb; properly, to fasten to, i.e. (specially) to set on fire.
G682: Apphia, a Christian lady of Colossae, either wife or sister of Philemon.
Probably of foreign origin; Apphia, a woman of Collosae.
G683: to push (thrust) away, repulse, reject, refuse.
Or apothomai ap-o'-thom-ahee from apo and the middle voice of otheo or otho (to shove); to push off, figuratively, to reject.
cast away, put away (from), thrust away (from).
G684: destruction, ruin, loss, perishing; eternal ruin.
From a presumed derivative of apollumi; ruin or loss (physical, spiritual or eternal).
damnable(-nation), destruction, die, perdition, X perish, pernicious ways, waste.
G685: a prayer; more commonly: a prayer for evil, a curse, imprecation.
Probably from airo; properly, prayer (as lifted to Heaven), i.e. (by implication) imprecation.
G686: Probably from airo (through the idea of drawing a conclusion); a particle denoting an inference more or less decisive (as follows).
haply, (what) manner (of man), no doubt, perhaps, so be, then, therefore, truly, wherefore. Often used in connection with other particles, especially ge or oun (after) or ei (before). Compare also…
G687: an untranslatable interrogative particle implying anxiety or impatience.
A form of ara, denoting an interrogation to which a negative answer is presumed.
G688: Arabia, a peninsula of Asia near Africa.
Of Hebrew origin ( Arab); Arabia, a region of Asia.
G689: Ram, son of Hezron and father of Amminadab.
Of Hebrew origin (Ram); Aram (i.e. Ram), an Israelite.
G69: to be not asleep, be awake; especially: to be watchful, careful.
Ultimately from a (as negative particle) and hupnos; to be sleepless, i.e. Keep awake.
G690: From Arabia; an Arab or native of Arabia.
G691: From argos; to be idle, i.e. (figuratively) to delay.
G692: From a (as a negative particle) and ergon; inactive, i.e. Unemployed; (by implication) lazy, useless.
G694: silver, a piece of silver, a shekel, money in general.
Neuter of a presumed derivative of arguros; silvery, i.e. (by implication) cash; specially, a silverling (i.e. Drachma or shekel).
G695: From arguros and kopto; a beater (i.e. Worker) of silver.
G696: From argos (shining); silver (the metal, in the articles or coin).
G697: Areopagus, or Mar's Hill, an open space on a hill in Athens where the supreme court was held.
From Ares (the name of the Greek deity of war) and a derivative of pegnumi; rock of Ares, a place in Athens.
G698: member of the Council of the Areopagus, an Areopagite.
From Areios Pagos; an Areopagite or member of the court held on Mars' Hill.
G699: From a derivative of aresko; complaisance.
G7: Abijah, (a) a king, son of Rehoboam, (b) founder of the eighth class of priests.
Of Hebrew origin ('Abiyah); Abijah, the name of two Israelites.
G70: the state of being awake (at night), sleeplessness, watching.
From agrupneo; sleeplessness, i.e. A keeping awake.
G700: to please, with the idea of willing service rendered to others; hence almost: to serve.
Probably from airo (through the idea of exciting emotion); to be agreeable (or by implication, to seek to be so).
G701: From aresko; agreeable; by implication, fit.
G702: Aretas IV, King of the Nabataeans.
Of foreign origin; Aretas, an Arabian.
G703: goodness, a gracious act, virtue, uprightness.
From the same as arrhen; properly, manliness (valor), i.e. Excellence (intrinsic or attributed).
G704: Perhaps the same as arrhen; a lamb (as a male).
G705: From arithmos; to enumerate or count.
G706: From airo; a number (as reckoned up).
G707: Arimathea, probably a city near Jer.
Of Hebrew origin (Ramah); Arimathaea (or Ramah), a place in Palestine.
G708: Aristarchus, a Christian, belonging to Thessalonica in Macedonia.
From the same as ariston and archo; best ruling; Aristarchus, a Macedonian.
G709: to breakfast, to take a meal.
From ariston; to take the principle meal.
G71: to lead, lead away, bring (a person, or animal), guide, spend a day, go.
A primary verb; properly, to lead; by implication, to bring, drive, (reflexively) go, (specially) pass (time), or (figuratively) induce.
be, bring (forth), carry, (let) go, keep, lead away, be open.
G710: Apparently a comparative of the same as ariston; the left hand (as second-best).
G711: From the same as ariston and boule; best counselling; Aristoboulus, a Christian.
G712: Apparently neuter of a superlative from the same as arrhen; the best meal (or breakfast; perhaps from eri ("early")), i.e. Luncheon.
G714: to keep off, assist; to suffice; pass: to be satisfied.
Apparently a primary verb (but probably akin to airo through the idea of raising a barrier); properly, to ward off, i.e. (by implication) to avail (figuratively, be satisfactory).
be content, be enough, suffice, be sufficient.
G715: Probably from arkeo; a bear (as obstructing by ferocity).
G716: Probably from airo (perhaps with a (as a particle of union) prefixed); a chariot (as raised or fitted together (compare harmos)).
G717: Of Hebrew origin (har and Mgiddown); Armageddon (or Har-Meggiddon), a symbolic name.
G718: to fit, join; mid: (the middle indicating deep personal interest) to espouse, betroth; mid: to take a wife, give in marriage.
From harmos; to joint, i.e. (figuratively) to woo (reflexively, to betroth).
G719: From the same as harma; an articulation (of the body).
G72: a leading, guiding; hence: mode of life, conduct.
Reduplicated from ago; a bringing up, i.e. Mode of living.
G720: (a) to deny (a statement), (b) to repudiate (a person, or belief).
Perhaps from a (as a negative particle) and the middle voice of rheo; to contradict, i.e. Disavow, reject, abnegate.
G721: (originally: a little lamb, but diminutive force was lost), a lamb.
G724: the act of plundering; plunder, spoil, robbery.
G725: spoil, an object of eager desire, a prize.
G726: to seize, snatch, obtain by robbery.
From a derivative of haireomai; to seize (in various applications).
catch (away, up), pluck, pull, take (by force).
G727: rapacious, ravenous; a robber, an extortioner.
G728: an earnest, earnest-money, a large part of the payment, given in advance as a security that the whole will be paid afterwards.
Of Hebrew origin (arabown); a pledge, i.e. Part of the purchase-money or property given in advance as security for the rest.
G729: without seam, of a single piece.
From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of the same as rhaphis; unsewed, i.e. Of a single piece.
G73: an (athletic) contest; hence, a struggle (in the soul).
From ago; properly, a place of assembly (as if led), i.e. (by implication) a contest (held there); figuratively, an effort or anxiety.
G730: Arsen (ar'-sane) probably from airo; male (as stronger for lifting).
G731: not to be uttered (because too sacred), secret, unspeakable, unspoken.
From a (as a negative particle) and the same as rhetos; unsaid, i.e. (by implication) inexpressible.
G732: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of rhonnumi; infirm.
G733: a male engaging in same-gender sexual activity; a sodomite, pederast.
From arrhen and koite; a sodomite.
abuser of (that defile) self with mankind.
G734: "gift of Artemis", Artemas, a friend of the apostle Paul.
Contracted from a compound of Artemis and doron; gift of Artemis; Artemas (or Artemidorus), a Christian.
G735: Artemis, a goddess, worshipped principally at Ephesus, typifying fertility (she had no relation with the other Artemis, the maiden huntress, to whom corresponded the Latin Diana).
Probably from the same as artemon; prompt; Artemis, the name of a Grecian goddess borrowed by the Asiatics for one of their deities.
G736: something hung up or fastened, a foresail.
From a derivative of arti; properly, something ready (or else more remotely from airo (compare artos); something hung up), i.e. (specially) the topsail (rather foresail or jib) of a vessel.
G737: now, just now, at this moment.
Adverb from a derivative of airo (compare artos) through the idea of suspension; just now.
this day (hour), hence(-forth), here(-after), hither(-to), (even) now, (this) present.
G738: From arti and gennetos; just born, i.e. (figuratively) a young convert.
G739: From arti; fresh, i.e. (by implication) complete.
G74: (properly the feeling of the athlete before a contest), great fear, terror, of death; anxiety, agony.
From agon; a struggle (properly, the state), i.e. (figuratively) anguish.
G740: From airo; bread (as raised) or a loaf.
G741: prop: to arrange, make ready; to season, flavor.
From a presumed derivative of airo; to prepare, i.e. Spice (with stimulating condiments).
G742: Arphaxad, a son of Shem and an ancestor of Christ.
Of Hebrew origin ('Arpakshad); Arphaxad, a post-diluvian patriarch.
G743: a ruler of angels, a superior angel, an archangel.
From archo and aggelos; a chief angel.
G745: Archelaus, Herod Archelaus, son and successor of Herod to, reigned over Judea from 4 B.C. to A.D. 6 and died before A.D. 18.
From archo and Laodikeus; people-ruling; Archelaus, a Jewish king.
G746: (a) rule (kingly or magisterial), (b) plur: in a quasi-personal sense, almost: rulers, magistrates, (c) beginning.
From archomai; (properly abstract) a commencement, or (concretely) chief (in various applications of order, time, place, or rank).
beginning, corner, (at the, the) first (estate), magistrate, power, principality, principle, rule.
G747: From arche and ago; a chief leader.
G748: high priestly, to which the chief priest belongs.
From arche and a derivative of hieros; high-priestly.
G749: From arche and hiereus; the high-priest (literally, of the Jews, typically, Christ); by extension a chief priest.
chief (high) priest, chief of the priests.
G75: to be struggling, striving (as in an athletic contest or warfare); to contend, as with an adversary.
From agon; to struggle, literally (to compete for a prize), figuratively (to contend with an adversary), or genitive case (to endeavor to accomplish something).
G750: From arche and poimen; a head shepherd.
G751: From arche and hippos; horse-ruler; Archippus, a Christian.
G752: a leader of the synagogue, a leader connected with the synagogue: sometimes there was only one, and the name was in some cases merely honorary.
From arche and sunagoge; director of the synagogue services.
G753: From arche and tekton; a chief constructor, i.e. "architect".
G754: head of a custom-house, chief tax-gatherer or publican.
From arche and telones; a principle tax-gatherer.
G755: master of ceremonies at a dinner, master of the feast.
From arche and a compound of treis and klino (a dinner-bed, because composed of three couches); director of the entertainment.
G756: Middle voice of archo (through the implication, of precedence); to commence (in order of time).
G757: A primary verb; to be first (in political rank or power).
G758: a ruler, governor, leader, leading man; with the Jews, an official member (a member of the executive) of the assembly of elders.
Present participle of archo; a first (in rank or power).
G759: From airo (in the sense of sending off scent); an aromatic.
G76: Adam, the first man, the first parent of the human race.
Of Hebrew origin ('Adam); Adam, the first man; typically (of Jesus) man (as his representative).
G760: Asa, son of Abijah and father of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah about 900 B.C. for 41 years.
Of Hebrew origin ('Aca'); Asa, an Israelite.
G761: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of saleuo; unshaken, i.e. (by implication) immovable (figuratively).
G762: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of sbennumi; not extinguished, i.e. (by implication) perpetual.
G763: From asebes; impiety, i.e. (by implication) wickedness.
G764: to be impious, to be ungodly.
From asebes; to be (by implied act) impious or wicked.
commit (live, that after should live) ungodly.
G765: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of sebomai; irreverent, i.e. (by extension) impious or wicked.
G766: (outrageous conduct, conduct shocking to public decency, a wanton violence), wantonness, lewdness.
From a compound of a (as a negative particle) and a presumed selges (of uncertain derivation, but apparently meaning continent); licentiousness (sometimes including other vices).
G767: From a (as a negative particle) and the base of semaino; unmarked, i.e. (figuratively) ignoble.
G768: Asher, one of the sons of Jacob, and founder of one of the Twelve Tribes.
Of Hebrew origin ('Asher); Aser (i.e. Asher), an Israelite tribe.
G769: want of strength, weakness, illness, suffering, calamity, frailty.
From asthenes; feebleness (of mind or body); by implication, malady; morally, frailty.
G77: without expense, for which nothing has to be paid.
From a (as negative particle); and dapane; costless, i.e. Gratuitous.
G770: to be weak (physically: then morally), to be sick.
From asthenes; to be feeble (in any sense).
be diseased, impotent folk (man), (be) sick, (be, be made) weak.
G771: From astheneo; a scruple of conscience.
G772: (lit: not strong), (a) weak (physically, or morally), (b) infirm, sick.
From a (as a negative particle) and the base of sthenoo; strengthless (in various applications, literal, figurative and moral).
more feeble, impotent, sick, without strength, weak(-er, -ness, thing).
G773: the Roman province of Asia, roughly the western third of Asia Minor.
Of uncertain derivation; Asia, i.e. Asia Minor, or (usually) only its western shore.
G774: belonging to the Roman province Asia.
From Asia; an Asian (i.e. Asiatic) or an inhabitant of Asia.
G775: an Asiarch, an official connected with the worship of Rome and the Emperor in the Roman province Asia.
From Asia and arche; an Asiarch or president of the public festivities in a city of Asia Minor.
G776: either: lack or wheat, lack of food (the literal meaning), or: abstinence from food, a fast, loss of appetite, sea-sickness (the extended meaning).
G777: From a (as a negative particle) and sitos; without (taking) food.
G778: Probably from the same as skeuos; to elaborate, i.e. (figuratively) train (by implication, strive).
G779: From the same as askeo; a leathern (or skin) bag used as a bottle.
G78: Addi, son of Cosam, and father of Melchi, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
Probably of Hebrew origin (compare adiy); Addi, an Israelite.
G780: Adverb from a derivative of the base of hedone; with pleasure.
G781: From a (as a negative particle) and sophos; unwise.
G782: to greet, salute, pay respects to, welcome.
From a (as a particle of union) and a presumed form of spao; to enfold in the arms, i.e. (by implication) to salute, (figuratively) to welcome.
G783: From aspazomai; a greeting (in person or by letter).
G784: From a (as a negative particle) and spiloo; unblemished (physically or morally).
G785: Of uncertain derivation; a buckler (or round shield); used of a serpent (as coiling itself), probably the "asp".
G786: without libation, without truce, admitting of no truce.
From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of spendo; literally, without libation (which usually accompanied a treaty), i.e. (by implication) truceless.
G787: a small coin equal to the tenth part of a drachma.
Of Latin origin; an assarius or as, a Roman coin.
G788: Neuter comparative of the base of eggus; more nearly, i.e. Very near.
G789: Assos, a port of Mysia, in the Roman province Asia.
Probably of foreign origin; Assus, a city of Asia minor.
G79: a sister, a woman (fellow-)member of a church, a Christian woman.
Fem of adephos; a sister (naturally or ecclesiastically).
G790: to be unsettled, have no fixed abode, lead a vagabond life.
From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of histemi; to be non-stationary, i.e. (figuratively) homeless.
G791: (lit: belonging to the city; then: witty, clever), elegant, pretty, fair, fine, beautiful.
From astu (a city); urbane, i.e. (by implication) handsome.
G792: Probably from the base of stronnumi; a star (as strown over the sky), literally or figuratively.
G793: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of sterizo; unfixed, i.e. (figuratively) vacillating.
G794: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of stergo (to cherish affectionately); hard-hearted towards kindred.
G795: to miss the mark, miss aim, make a false aim, fail.
From a compound of a (as a negative particle) and stoichos (an aim); to miss the mark, i.e. (figuratively) deviate from truth.
G796: a flash of lightning, brightness, luster.
From astrapto; lightning; by analogy, glare.
G797: to flash (with, then like, lightning), be lustrous.
Probably from aster; to flash as lightning.
G798: Neuter from aster; properly, a constellation; put for a single star (natural or artificial).
G799: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of sugkrino; incomparable; Asyncritus, a Christian.
G8: Abiathar, a priest in King David's time.
Of Hebrew origin ('Ebyathar); Abiathar, an Israelite.
G80: a brother, member of the same religious community, especially a fellow-Christian.
From a (as a connective particle) and delphus (the womb); a brother (literally or figuratively) near or remote (much like a).
G800: From a (as a negative particle) and sumphonos; inharmonious (figuratively).
G801: unintelligent, without wisdom, unwise, undiscerning (implying probably moral defect).
From a (as a negative particle) and sunetos; unintelligent; by implication, wicked.
G802: not covenanting, untrue to an agreement, treacherous.
From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of suntithemai; properly, not agreed, i.e. Treacherous to compacts.
G804: (lit: unfailing), safe, reliable, trustworthy, certain, sure.
From a (as a negative particle) and sphallo (to "fail"); secure (literally or figuratively).
G806: Adverb from asphales; securely (literally or figuratively).
G807: to act improperly, be unseemly, behave unbecomingly (or even dishonorably); perhaps: to consider (something) unseemly.
From askemon; to be (i.e. Act) unbecoming.
G808: unseemly behavior, unseemliness, indecency, shame, nakedness, an indecent (lewd) act.
From askemon; an indecency; by implication, the pudenda.
G809: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of echo (in the sense of its congener schema); properly, shapeless, i.e. (figuratively) inelegant.
G81: brotherhood (in the collective sense), the members of the Christian Church, Christendom.
From adephos; brotherhood (properly, the feeling of brotherliness), i.e. The (Christian) fraternity.
G810: From a compound of a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of sozo; properly, unsavedness, i.e. (by implication) profligacy.
G811: Adverb from the same as asotia; dissolutely.
G812: (lit: to march out of order; then: to riot, rebel), behave disorderly, neglect duty, be careless (or idle) in habits.
From ataktos; to be (i.e. Act) irregular.
G813: (lit: out of order), disorderly, slack (in performance of duty).
From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of tasso; unarranged, i.e. (by implication) insubordinate (religiously).
G815: From a (as a negative particle) and teknon; childless.
G816: From a compound of a (as a particle of union) and teino (to stretch); to gaze intently.
behold earnestly (stedfastly), fasten (eyes), look (earnestly, stedfastly, up stedfastly), set eyes.
G817: A particle probably akin to aneu; aloof, i.e. Apart from (literally or figuratively).
G818: to disgrace, treat disgracefully, dishonor, insult; to despise.
From atimos; to render infamous, i.e. (by implication) contemn or maltreat.
despise, dishonour, suffer shame, entreat shamefully.
G819: From atimos; infamy, i.e. (subjectively) comparative indignity, (objectively) disgrace.
G82: From a (as a negative particle) and delos; hidden, figuratively, indistinct.
G820: From a (as a negative particle) and time; (negatively) unhonoured or (positively) dishonoured.
despised, without honour, less honourable (comparative degree).
G821: From atimos; used like atimazo, to maltreat.
G822: From the same as aer; mist.
G823: (lit: that cannot be cut), an indivisible part of time, a moment.
From a (as a negative particle) and the base of tomoteros; uncut, i.e. (by implication) indivisible (an "atom" of time).
G824: (lit: out of place, unusual, unbecoming), improper, unrighteous, perverse.
From a (as a negative particle) and topos; out of place, i.e. (figuratively) improper, injurious, wicked.
G825: Attalia, the port of Perga in Pamphylia.
From Attalos (a king of Pergamus); Attaleia, a place in Pamphylia.
G826: to flash, gleam, shine forth, appear white, bright; but perhaps: to see, see clearly, discern.
G827: Of uncertain derivation; a ray of light, i.e. (by implication) radiance, dawn.
G828: Augustus, a title conferred on the first Roman Emperor, C. Iulius Octauianus, denoting sanctity (almost divinity).
From Latin ("august"); Augustus, a title of the Roman emperor.
G829: From autos and the base of hedone; self-pleasing, i.e. Arrogant.
G83: the quality of being unseen (of disappearing), indefiniteness, uncertainty.
G830: From autos and the same as hairetizo; self-chosen, i.e. (by implication) voluntary.
of own accord, willing of self.
G831: to domineer, govern, have mastery over.
From a compound of autos and an obsolete hentes (a worker); to act of oneself, i.e. (figuratively) dominate.
G832: From aulos; to play the flute.
G833: court-yard, fore-court, sheep-fold; but it may be understood as: palace, house.
From the same as aer; a yard (as open to the wind); by implication, a mansion.
G835: to lodge in the open, lodge, pass the night.
Middle voice from aule; to pass the night (properly, in the open air).
G836: From the same as aer; a flute (as blown).
G837: (a) to cause to increase, become greater (b) to increase, grow.
A prolonged form of a primary verb; to grow ("wax"), i.e. Enlarge (literal or figurative, active or passive).
G839: From a derivative of the same as aer (meaning a breeze, i.e. The morning air); properly, fresh, i.e. (adverb with ellipsis of hemera) to-morrow.
G84: out of sight, obscurely, inconspicuously, uncertainly, without certain aim.
G840: grim, severe, strict, exacting, harsh, rigid.
From a (presumed) derivative of the same as aer (meaning blown); rough (properly as a gale), i.e. (figuratively) severe.
G841: From autarkes; self-satisfaction, i.e. (abstractly) contentedness, or (concretely) a competence.
G842: From autos and arkeo; self-complacent, i.e. Contented.
G843: From autos and a derivative or katakrino; self-condemned.
G844: acting of one's own will, of its own accord.
From autos and the same as maten; self-moved ("automatic"), i.e. Spontaneous.
G845: From autos and optanomai; self-seeing, i.e. An eye-witness.
G846: (1) self (emphatic) (2) he, she, it (used for the third person pronoun) (3) the same.

From the particle au (perhaps akin to the base of aer through the idea of a baffling wind) (backward); the reflexive pronoun self, used (alone or in the comparative heautou) of the third person, and (with the proper personal pronoun) of the other persons.
her, it(-self), one, the other, (mine) own, said, (self-), the) same, ((him-, my-, thy-)self, (your-)selves, she, that, their(-s), them(-selves), there(-at, - by, -in, -into, -of, -on, -with), they,…
G847: Genitive (i.e. Possessive) of autos, used as an adverb of location; properly, belonging to the same spot, i.e. In this (or that) place.
G848: her own, his own, their own, themselves, they.
Contracted for heautou; self (in some oblique case or reflexively, relation).
her (own), (of) him(-self), his (own), of it, thee, their (own), them(-selves), they.
G849: From autos and cheir; self-handed, i.e. Doing personally.
G85: to feel fear, lack courage, be distressed, troubled.
From a derivative of adeo (to be sated to loathing); to be in distress (of mind).
be full of heaviness, be very heavy.
G850: (poetical, lit: dry and parched; then: squalid and rough), dingy, murky, obscure, dark, funereal.
From auchmos (probably from a base akin to that of aer) (dust, as dried by wind); properly, dirty, i.e. (by implication) obscure.
G851: From apo and haireomai; to remove (literally or figuratively).
G852: From a (as a negative particle) and phaino; non-apparent).
G853: to cause to disappear, hide, remove; to disfigure (probably by leaving unwashed for a long period), destroy.
From aphanes; to render unapparent, i.e. (actively) consume (becloud), or (passively) disappear (be destroyed).
G855: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of phaino; non-manifested, i.e. Invisible.
G856: a place of sitting apart, a privy, drain.
From a compound of apo and the base of hedraios; a place of sitting apart, i.e. A privy.
G857: From a compound of a (as a negative particle) and pheidomai; unsparingness, i.e. Austerity (asceticism).
G858: From a compound of a (as a negative particle) and phellos (in the sense of a stone as stubbing the foot); smoothness, i.e. (figuratively) simplicity.
G859: a sending away, a letting go, a release, pardon, complete forgiveness.
G86: Hades, the abode of departed spirits.
From a (as negative particle) and eido; properly, unseen, i.e. "Hades" or the place (state) of departed souls.
G860: a band, fastening (hence, possibly: a ligament), joint.
From haptomai; probably a ligament (as fastening).
G861: From aphthartos; incorruptibility; genitive, unending existence; (figuratively) genuineness.
G862: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of phtheiro; undecaying (in essence or continuance).
G863: (a) to send away, (b) to let go, release, permit to depart, (c) to remit, forgive, (d) to permit, suffer.
From apo and hiemi (to send; an intensive form of eimi, to go); to send forth, in various applications (as follow).
cry, forgive, forsake, lay aside, leave, let (alone, be, go, have), omit, put (send) away, remit, suffer, yield up.
G864: to arrive at, reach, come to.
From apo and the base of hikanos; to go (i.e. Spread) forth (by rumor).
G865: not loving that which is good.
From a (as a negative particle) and philagathos; hostile to virtue.
despiser of those that are good.
G866: From a (as a negative particle) and philarguros; unavaricious.
without covetousness, not greedy of filthy lucre.
G867: From aphikneomai; properly, arrival, i.e. (by implication) departure.
G868: to make to stand away, draw away, repel, take up a position away from, withdraw from, leave, abstain from.
From apo and histemi; to remove, i.e. (actively) instigate to revolt; usually (reflexively) to desist, desert, etc..
depart, draw (fall) away, refrain, withdraw self.
G869: Adverb from aphanes (contraction); unawares, i.e. Unexpectedly.
G87: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of diakrino; properly, undistinguished, i.e. (actively) impartial.
G870: Adverb from a compound of a (as a negative particle) and phobos; fearlessly.
G871: From apo and homoioo; to assimilate closely.
G872: to look away from (something else) to, see distinctly.
From apo and horao; to consider attentively.
G873: to mark off by boundaries from, set apart.
From apo and horizo; to set off by boundary, i.e. (figuratively) limit, exclude, appoint, etc.
G874: (a) a starting, a start, (b) cause, occasion, opportunity.
From a compound of apo and hormao; a starting-point, i.e. (figuratively) an opportunity.
G875: From aphros; to froth at the mouth (in epilepsy).
G876: Apparently a primary word; froth, i.e. Slaver.
G877: want of sense, foolishness, impiety, wickedness.
From aphron; senselessness, i.e. (euphemistically) egotism; (morally) recklessness.
G878: From a (as a negative particle) and phren; properly, mindless, i.e. Stupid, (by implication) ignorant, (specially) egotistic, (practically) rash, or (morally) unbelieving.
G879: From a compound of apo and hupnos; properly, to become awake, i.e. (by implication) to drop (off) in slumber.
G88: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of dia and leipo; unintermitted, i.e. Permanent.
G880: From a (as a negative particle) and phone; voiceless, i.e. Mute (by nature or choice); figuratively, unmeaning.
G881: Ahaz, son of Jotham and father of Hezekiah.
Of Hebrew origin ('Achaz); Achaz, an Israelite.
G882: the Roman Province Achaia, governed by a proconsul, and practically conterminous with modern Greece before 1912.
Of uncertain derivation; Achaia (i.e. Greece), a country of Europe.
G883: "an Achaian", Achaicus, a Christian at Corinth.
From Achaia; an Achaian; Achaicus, a Christian.
G884: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of charizomai; thankless, i.e. Ungrateful.
G885: Achim, son of Zadok and father of Eliud.
Probably of Hebrew origin (compare Yowqiym); Achim, an Israelite.
G886: From a (as a negative particle) and cheiropoietos; unmanufactured, i.e. Inartificial.
G887: Of uncertain derivation; dimness of sight, i.e. (probably) a cataract.
G888: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of chre (compare chreia); useless, i.e. (euphemistically) unmeritorious.
G889: (lit: to become sour, to turn, of milk), to be good for nothing, render useless; met: to become corrupt.
From achreios; to render useless, i.e. Spoil.
G89: Adverb from adialeiptos; uninterruptedly, i.e. Without omission (on an appropriate occasion).
G890: From a (as a negative particle) and chrestos; inefficient, i.e. (by implication) detrimental.
G891: as far as, up to, until, during.
Or achris akh'-rece; akin to akron (through the idea of a terminus); (of time) until or (of place) up to.
as far as, for, in(-to), till, (even, un-)to, until, while. Compare mechri.
G892: Perhaps remotely from cheo (to shed forth); chaff (as diffusive).
G893: From a (as a negative particle) and pseudos; veracious.
G894: Of uncertain derivation; wormwood (as a type of bitterness, i.e. (figuratively) calamity).
G895: From a (as a negative particle) and psuche; lifeless, i.e. Inanimate (mechanical).
G896: Baal, chief deity of the Phoenicians and other Semitic nations.
Of Hebrew origin (Ba'al); Baal, a Phoenician deity (used as a symbol of idolatry).
G897: (a) Babylon, the ancient city on the Euphrates, to which the people of Jerusalem, etc., were transported, (b) hence allegorically of Rome, from the point of view of the Christian people.
Of Hebrew origin (Babel); Babylon, the capitol of Chaldaea (literally or figuratively (as a type of tyranny)).
G898: a step (of a stairway); hence: a stage in a career, a position.
From the same as bathos; a step, i.e. (figuratively) grade (of dignity).
G899: depth; deep water; met: fullness, immensity; an extreme degree; profundities, deep-laid plans.
From the same as bathus; profundity, i.e. (by implication) extent; (figuratively) mystery.
G9: the Abilenian territory, the territory of Abila (in Syria), a small principality in the mountains of Damascus.
Of foreign origin (compare 'abel); Abilene, a region of Syria.
G90: From a derivative of a compound of a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of diaphtheiro; incorruptibleness, i.e. (figuratively) purity (of doctrine).
G901: deep (lit. and met.); in the depths of the early morning, while still very early; profound.
From the base of basis; profound (as going down), literally or figuratively.
G902: A diminutive of a derivative probably of the base of basis; a palm twig (as going out far).
G903: Balaam, son of Beor of Pethor on the Euphrates, a soothsayer in the Old Testament.
Of Hebrew origin (Bil'am); Balaam, a Mesopotamian (symbolic of a false teacher).
G904: Balak, son of Zippor, King of Moab.
Of Hebrew origin (Balaq); Balak, a Moabite.
G905: Probably remotely from ballo (as a depository); a pouch (for money).
G906: (a) to cast, throw, rush, (b) often, in the weaker sense: to place, put, drop.
A primary verb; to throw (in various applications, more or less violent or intense).
arise, cast (out), X dung, lay, lie, pour, put (up), send, strike, throw (down), thrust. Compare rhipto.
G907: lit: to dip, submerge, but specifically of ceremonial dipping; to baptize.

From a derivative of bapto; to immerse, submerge; to make whelmed (i.e. Fully wet); used only (in the New Testament) of ceremonial ablution, especially (technically) of the ordinance of Christian baptism.
G908: (the result of) a dipping or sinking.
G91: to act unjustly towards, injure, harm.
From adikos; to be unjust, i.e. (actively) do wrong (morally, socially or physically).
hurt, injure, be an offender, be unjust, (do, suffer, take) wrong.
G910: the baptizer, the Baptist, epithet used only of John, the son of Zechariah and Elizabeth, forerunner of Jesus.
From baptizo; a baptizer, as an epithet of Christ's forerunner.
G911: A primary verb; to whelm, i.e. Cover wholly with a fluid; in the New Testament only in a qualified or special sense, i.e. (literally) to moisten (a part of one's person), or (by implication) to stain (as with dye).
G912: "son of Abba", Barabbas, the Israelite robber released instead of Christ.
Of Chaldee origin (dikaiosis and Abba); son of Abba; Bar-abbas, an Israelite.
G913: Barak, one of the judges of Israel.
Of Hebrew origin (Baraq); Barak, an Israelite.
G914: Barachiah; his identity is uncertain, perhaps father of the Zechariah killed by the Zealots in the last Jewish War.
Of Hebrew origin (Berekyah); Barachias (i.e. Berechijah), an Israelite.
G915: a foreigner, one who speaks neither Greek nor Latin; as adj: foreign.
Of uncertain derivation; a foreigner (i.e. Non-Greek).
G916: to weight, load, burden, lit. and met.
G918: Bartholomew, surname of Nathanael, one of the twelve apostles of Jesus.
Of Chaldee origin (bar and Talmay); son of Tolmai; Bar-tholomoeus, a Christian apostle.
G919: Bar-Jesus, the name of the magician and false prophet at Paphos in Cyprus; he is also called Elymas.
Of Chaldee origin (bar and Yhowshuwa'); son of Jesus (or Joshua); Bar-jesus, an Israelite.
G92: a legal wrong, crime (with which one is charged), misdeed, crime against God, a sin.
evil doing, iniquity, matter of wrong.
G920: Bar-Jonas, son of Jonas, the surname of Simon Peter.
Of Chaldee origin (diakoneo and Malchos); son of Jonas (or Jonah); Bar-jonas, an Israelite.
G921: Barnabas, a Cypriote Jew, uncle of John Mark; his other name was Joseph.
Of Chaldee origin (diakoneo and tacha); son of Nabas (i.e. Prophecy); Barnabas, an Israelite.
G922: a weight, burden, lit. or met.
Probably from the same as basis (through the notion of going down; compare bathos); weight; in the New Testament only, figuratively, a load, abundance, authority.
G923: "son of Sabba", Barsabbas, the surname of two Israelites Christian.
Of Chaldee origin (bar and probably tsba'); son of Sabas (or Tsaba); Bar-sabas, the name of two Israelites.
G924: Of Chaldee origin (diakoneo and kruphe); son of Timoeus (or the unclean); Bar-timoeus, an Israelite.
G926: heavy, weighty, burdensome, lit. and met; violent, oppressive.
From the same as baros; weighty, i.e. (fig) burdensome, grave.
G927: From barus and time; highly valuable.
G928: to examine, as by torture; to torment; to buffet, as of waves.
G93: From adikos; (legal) injustice (properly, the quality, by implication, the act); morally, wrongfulness (of character, life or act).
G930: one who tortures, a tormentor, jailor.
G931: a touchstone (a dark stone used in testing metals), examination by torture, torture.
Perhaps remotely from the same as basis (through the notion of going to the bottom); a touch-stone, i.e. (by analogy) torture.
G932: kingship, sovereignty, authority, rule, especially of God, both in the world, and in the hearts of men; hence: kingdom, in the concrete sense.
From basileus; properly, royalty, i.e. (abstractly) rule, or (concretely) a realm (literally or figuratively).
G934: courtiers, palaces, a body of kings, royal.
G935: a king, ruler, but in some passages clearly to be translated: emperor.
Probably from basis (through the notion of a foundation of power); a sovereign (abstractly, relatively, or figuratively).
G936: (a) to rule, reign, (b) to reign over.
From basileus; to rule (literally or figuratively).
G937: connected with a king, royal, regal, (a) an officer in the service of the king, (b) the king's country.
From basileus; regal (in relation), i.e. (literally) belonging to (or befitting) the sovereign (as land, dress, or a courtier), or (figuratively) preeminent.
G939: From baino (to walk); a pace ("base"), i.e. (by implication) the foot.
G94: From a (as a negative particle) and dike; unjust; by extension wicked; by implication, treacherous; specially, heathen.
G940: to give the evil eye to, fascinate, bewitch, overpower.
Akin to phasko; to malign, i.e. (by extension) to fascinate (by false representations).
G941: (a) to carry, bear, (b) to carry (take) away.
Perhaps remotely derived from the base of basis (through the idea of removal); to lift, literally or figuratively (endure, declare, sustain, receive, etc.).
G942: Of uncertain derivation; a brier shrub.
G943: a bath, a liquid measure among the Jews, containing 72 sextarii, that is, between eight and nine gallons.
Of Hebrew origin (bath); a bath, or measure for liquids.
G945: to chatter, be long-winded, utter empty words, stammer, repeat.
From Battos (a proverbial stammerer) and logos; to stutter, i.e. (by implication) to prate tediously.
G946: an abominable thing, an accursed thing.
From bdelusso; a detestation, i.e. (specially) idolatry.
G948: From a (presumed) derivative of bdeo (to stink); to be disgusted, i.e. (by implication) detest (especially of idolatry).
G949: From the base of basis (through the idea of basality); stable (literally or figuratively).
G950: to confirm, ratify, secure, establish; pass: to guarantee.
G952: permitted to be trodden, by implication unhallowed.
From the base of basis and belos (a threshold); accessible (as by crossing the door-way), i.e. (by implication, of Jewish notions) heathenish, wicked.
G954: Beelzebul, a name of Satan, the chief of evil spirits.
Of Chaldee origin (by parody on Ba'al Zbuwb); dung-god; Beelzebul, a name of Satan.
G955: "lord of the forest", Beliar, a name of Satan.
Of Hebrew origin (bliya'al); worthlessness; Belial, as an epithet of Satan.
G956: From ballo; a missile, i.e. Spear or arrow.
G957: Neuter of a compound of a derivative of ballo (used for the comparative of agathos); better.
G958: Benjamin, youngest son of Jacob, founder of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
Of Hebrew origin (Binyamiyn); Benjamin, an Israelite.
G959: Bernice, daughter of Agrippa to and Kypros, and sister of M. Julius Agrippa II.
From a provincial form of phero and nike; victorious; Bernice, a member of the Herodian family.
G96: failing to pass the test, unapproved, counterfeit.
From a (as a negative particle) and dokimos; unapproved, i.e. Rejected; by implication, worthless (literally or morally).
G960: Berea, a town of the province Macedonia.
Perhaps a provincial from a derivative of peran (Peroea, i.e. The region beyond the coast-line); Beroea, a place in Macedonia.
G961: From Beroia; a Beroeoean or native of Beroea.
G962: Of Hebrew origin (bayith and abarah); ferry-house; Bethabara (i.e. Bethabarah), a place on the Jordan.
G963: (a) Bethany, the home of Lazarus, Martha, and Mary, near Jerusalem, (b) Bethany, beyond Jordan.
Of Chaldee origin; date-house; Beth-any, a place in Palestine.
G964: Bethesda, name of a pool in Jerusalem.
Of Chaldee origin (compare bayith and checed); house of kindness; Beth-esda, a pool in Jerusalem.
G965: "house of bread", Bethlehem, a city near Jer.
Of Hebrew origin (Beyth l-'Aphrah); Bethleem (i.e. Beth-lechem), a place in Palestine.
G966: "house of fish", Bethsaida, the name of two cities on the shore of the Sea of Galilee.
Of Chaldee origin (compare bayith and tsayad); fishing-house; Bethsaida, a place in Palestine.
G967: Bethphage, a village in the neighborhood of Jerusalem, on the Mt. of Olives.
Of Chaldee origin (compare bayith and pag); fig-house; Beth-phage, a place in Palestine.
G968: an elevated place ascended by steps, a throne, tribunal.
From the base of basis; a step, i.e. Foot-breath; by implication, a rostrum, i.e. A tribunal.
G969: a beryl, a precious stone of various colors, the best known being sea-green.
G97: From a (as a negative particle}; and dolos; undeceitful, i.e. (figuratively) unadulterated.
G970: Probably akin to bia (through the idea of vital activity); force.
G971: (a) mid: to use force, force way, come forward violently, (b) pass: to be forcibly treated, suffer violence.
From bios; to force, i.e. (reflexively) to crowd oneself (into), or (passively) to be seized.
G973: a forceful, violent man; one who is eager in pursuit.
From biazo; a forcer, i.e. (figuratively) energetic.
G974: A diminutive of biblion; a booklet.
G975: A diminutive of biblos; a roll.
G976: a written book, roll, or volume, sometimes with a sacred connotation.
Properly, the inner bark of the papyrus plant, i.e. (by implication) a sheet or scroll of writing.
G977: A reduplicated and prolonged form of an obsolete primary verb (perhaps causative of bosko); to eat.
G978: Bithynia, a Roman province, north-west of Asia Minor and south-west of the Black Sea.
Of uncertain derivation; Bithynia, a region of Asia.
G979: A primary word; life, i.e. (literally) the present state of existence; by implication, the means of livelihood.
G98: belonging to Adramyttium, a port in Mysia, in Asia Minor.
From Adramutteion (a place in Asia Minor); Adramyttene or belonging to Adramyttium.
G981: From bioo; living (properly, the act, by implication, the mode).
G982: From a derivative of bioo; relating to the present existence.
of (pertaining to, things that pertain to) this life.
G984: A primary verb; properly, to hinder, i.e. (by implication) to injure.
G985: intrans: to sprout; trans: to cause to sprout, make to grow up.
From blastos (a sprout); to germinate; by implication, to yield fruit.
G986: Blastus, chamberlain of King Herod Agrippa to.
Perhaps the same as the base of blastano; Blastus, an officer of Herod Agrippa.
G987: to speak evil against, blaspheme, use abusive or scurrilous language about (God or men).
From blasphemos; to vilify; specially, to speak impiously.
(speak) blaspheme(-er, -mously, -my), defame, rail on, revile, speak evil.
G989: From a derivative of blapto and pheme; scurrilious, i.e. Calumnious (against men), or (specially) impious (against God).
G99: the Hadria, a name given by sailors not merely to the Adriatic Sea, to which it properly belonged, but also to the open Mediterranean to the south-east of Italy, to the sea that lay between Malta, Italy, Greece, and…
From Adria (a place near its shore); the Adriatic sea (including the Ionian).
G990: a look, glance; sight and hearing.
From blepo; vision (properly concrete; by implication, abstract).
G991: (primarily physical), to look, see, perceive, discern.
A primary verb; to look at (literally or figuratively).
behold, beware, lie, look (on, to), perceive, regard, see, sight, take heed. Compare optanomai.
G992: a verbal adj: one must put, that ought to be put.
From ballo; fit to be cast (i.e. Applied).
G993: Boanerges, an epithet applied to the two sons of Zebedee.
Of Chaldee origin (ben and rgaz); sons of commotion; Boanerges, an epithet of two of the apostles.
G994: Apparently a prolonged form of a primary verb; to halloo, i.e. Shout (for help or in a tumultuous way).
G995: From boao; a halloo, i.e. Call (for aid, etc.).
G996: (a) abstr: assistance, (b) concr: (a technical term of nautical language), a help.
From boethos; aid; specially, a rope or chain for frapping a vessel.
G997: to come to the rescue of, come to help, help.
From boethos; to aid or relieve.
G998: From boe and theo (to run); a succorer.
G999: Akin to bathuno; a hole (in the ground); specially, a cistern.
H1: A primitive word; father, in a literal and immediate, or figurative and remote application).
chief, (fore-)father(-less), X patrimony, principal. Compare names in "Abi-".
H10: The same as 'abedah, miswritten for 'abaddown; a perishing.
H100: From the same as 'agam; a marshy pool (others from a different root, a kettle); by implication a rush (as growing there); collectively a rope of rushes.
H1000: From the same as buwts; an egg (from its whiteness).
H1002: Of foreign origin; a castle or palace.
H1004: Probably from banah abbreviated; a house (in the greatest variation of applications, especially family, etc.).

court, daughter, door, + dungeon, family, + forth of, X great as would contain, hangings, home(born), (winter)house(-hold), inside(-ward), palace, place, + prison, + steward, + tablet, temple, web, +…
H1006: The same as bayith; Bajith, a place in Palestine.
H1007: From bayith and 'aven; house of vanity; Beth- Aven, a place in Palestine.
H1008: "house of God", a city in Ephraim, also a place in S. Judah.
From bayith and 'el; house of God; Beth-El, a place in Palestine.
H1009: "house of God's ambush", a place in Palestine.
From bayith and 'ereb and 'el; house of God's ambush; Beth-Arbel, a place in Palestine.
H101: Probably from nagan; a bowl (as pounded out hollow).
H1010: "house of Baal of (the) habitation", a place East of the Jordan.

From bayith and Ba'al and ma'own; house of Baal of (the) habitation of (apparently by transposition); or (shorter) Beyth M own {bayth me-own'}; house of habitation of (Baal); Beth- Baal-Meon, a place in Palestine.
Beth-baal-meon. Compare Ba'al m'own and b'on.
H1011: "house of a creative one", a place in Palestine.
From bayith and bara'; house of a creative one; Beth-Biri, a place in Palestine.
H1012: "place of ford", a place in Palestine.
Probably from bayith and abarah; house of (the) ford; Beth-Barah, a place in Palestine.
H1013: "place of a wall", a place in Judah.
From bayith and gader; house of (the) wall; Beth-Gader, a place in Palestine.
H1014: "place of recompense", a place in Moab.
From bayith and the passive participle of gmuwl; house of (the) weaned; Beth-Gamul, a place East of the Jordan.
H1015: From bayith and the dual of dbelah; house of (the) two figcakes; Beth-Diblathajim, a place East of the Jordan.
H1016: "house of Dagon", two places in Palestine.
From bayith and Dagown; house of Dagon; Beth-Dagon, the name of two places in Palestine.
H1017: Patrial from Beyth-'El with the article interposed; a Beth-elite, or inhabitant of Bethel.
H1018: From bayith and 'etsel with the article interposed; house of the side; Beth-ha-Etsel, a place in Palestine.
H1019: "house of the Gilgal", a place in Palestine.
From bayith and Gilgal with the article interposed; house of Gilgal (or rolling); Beth-hag-Gilgal, a place in Palestine.
H102: Probably from nagaph (through the idea of impending); a cover or heap; i.e. (only plural) wings of an army, or crowds of troops.
H1020: "place of the desert", a place East of the Jordan in Moab.
From bayith and the plural of yshiymah with the article interposed; house of the deserts; Beth-ha- Jeshimoth, a town East of the Jordan.
H1021: From bayith and kerem with the article interposed; house of the vineyard; Beth-hak-Kerem, a place in Palestine.
H1022: Patrial from Beyth Lechem with the article inserted; a Beth-lechemite, or native of Bethlechem.
H1023: Beth-ham-Merchak, a place in Palestine; place that was far off.
From bayith and merchaq with the article interposed; house of the breadth; Beth-ham-Merchak, a place in Palestine.
H1024: "place of chariots", a place in Simeon.

Or (shortened) Beyth Mar-kabowth {bayth mar-kaw-both'}; from bayith and the plural of merkabah (with or without the article interposed); place of (the) chariots; Beth-ham-Markaboth or Beth-Markaboth, a place in Palestine.
H1025: "valley house", a place on the border of Asher.
From bayith and emeq with the article interposed; house of the valley; Beth-ha-Emek, a place in Palestine.
H1026: "place of the depression", a place near the Dead Sea.
